Sentence: There's a trick to getting these pens not to leak globs of paint everywhere when you first get them.
Content: There's a trick to getting these pens not to leak globs of paint everywhere when you first get them. You have to hold the pen with the point upwards, towards the ceiling, push the nib in with your finger, you'll hear a small amount of air escape, like a hissing sound. Then turn back over and press repeatedly onto paper to get the paint going. If you don't do this, globs will come out and go everywhere! Happened to me and lots of paint was wasted. But they work great once you get them going correctly.

Sentence: Put the cover on well and it shouldn't dry out.
Content: I love anything to do with color. Recently I started buying things to do finger nail art.  I am a water paint artist and glass artist. I was looking for something that I could use that would give me better outlines when painting in miniature.  I saw these pens and decided to give them a try.  The price was reasonable. I did read the mixed reviews. Yes, the instructions are in Japanese and I can't read them, but how many American products are translated into Japanese.I decided to try all of them to make sure they worked. I found that if you don't want them to gush out some ink or whatever it is when you try to get the color flowing, you should first take all of them out of the box. Shake one back and forth a few times and then put it back in the box with point end standing up. Then after you have repeated this with all the pens, take the 1st one you shook turn it over and very lightly and I mean lightly, press it down on a paper just about 1 or 2mm, no more, Do it once and then a second time, then wait. The ink will slowly start to flow onto the point of the pen. It starts out as white and then slowly the color changes.  You can now test it with a lite touch.  If you press hard the ink will gush out. It will also do that if you shake it and immediately use it as you should allow the ink to settle and not all be in the tip. I know from experience. Put the cover on well and it shouldn't dry out. The tip is not felt but a material that if firm and won't absorb the ink, just enough .The ink is a nice consistency.It appears to be ink. It dries very fast and on paper it is a matt finish as well as on nails. I put a clear coat over it and then it had a gloss finish. It does cover well as it is opaque. I bought another set that has the extra fine tip and am looking forward to getting it.

Sentence: The tips are firm and don't fray.
Content: We use these paint pens for our hobby of painting smooth river stones, and they are terrific.  The tips are firm and don't fray.  The only caution I would give is that you get the best and smoothest line if you 'pull' the pen toward you.  If you 'push' the line away from you (as you would if you're writing the letter "O"), you will get some feathering unless you ease up on the pressure.  Or, if you are drawing, just turn the stone so you are drawing the pen toward you rather than pushing it away from you.We have these pens in the Extra Fine point, the Fine point, and the Medium point, and we seldom use the tiny brushes anymore.  These pens allow us (and even our 92 year old Nana) to do fine detail work, and we love them!Note:  We always put a spray coat of sealer on our stones to protect the artwork.

Sentence: Pilling is the result of the pen nib being so abrasive on the paper's surface that it rips up the paper's surface/tooth.
Content: Hello everyone! My name is Aspen, @Paraslider on Twitter, I'm an artist and animator entering college this year, and I'd like to say I've been using these for 2 years now and they still work fine to this day. Some problems arose with the paint itself, which I'll get into later.For now, I'll start off with a brief introduction to how these pens work. Posca pens are notable for their usage in graffiti and street art, so the pen nibs are pretty much made to go through the wringer. As long as the surface you're going on isn't *too* toothy, like a broken brick or something, you can expect the nib to last a while. That being said; if you plan to use these on any kind of paper, expect the paper to pill. Pilling is the result of the pen nib being so abrasive on the paper's surface that it rips up the paper's surface/tooth. It won't destroy the paper by any means if it's watercolor paper or heavier weight paper, but printer paper is never ideal for these. The way you activate these is fairly simple-- you just press the nib down on a surface a bunch until the paint fills the nib, alternating between shaking the pen (cap on, of course) and pumping the nib like crazy until you get a nice, clean, consistent stroke.Let it be known, though, you will be shaking these pens a lot. I don't want to understate this in the slightest. You will spend a lot of time shaking these pens. If your batch is particularly fussy, hours even. When I tell you I've spent upwards of an hour or two just shaking and pumping my pens for the second piece of art in particular, please believe me there. Once that's done, you should be smoothly sailing. If not, I can only refer you to Kasey Golden's posca pen videos on YouTube for troubleshooting and tips.For clarity, I'll describe the processes behind each of these art pieces, as the size you're working on and the surface material matters greatly.1- The first painting (the side profile of my OC, grey background) is something I was able to do with just this 15 pen set, and it was my first go with these, done around late 2018. Watercolor paper, 7x7 inch size if I remember correctly, and yes, the paper pilled here and there. It wasn't at all a distraction or a major flaw of the markers, and it turned out perfectly fine. It sort of feels like eraser shavings, and if you like the texture the pilling produces, feel free to keep it! if not, it's really easy to wipe off after the paint dries.As can be seen, with just the base 15 markers, a lot can be done. If you're looking for a challenge and can work in a limited color palette, this set can take you far. The colors dry opaque and are super vibrant as expected. The coverage, especially for 3M size, is really nice and it dries down smooth and matte, no streaks abound. Poscas are renowned for their ability to create flat, sleek color blocks, so if that's your thing, you'll love these.2- This next piece (pattern background, 4 characters) was a lot larger than the first one, and was done on a 16x20 inch canvas and it was completed around a month or two ago. It's clear that I expanded the color count here, and you can totally buy different colors of posca pens on amazon for relatively cheap if you get them in packs. Individual pens, however, tend to be a lot pricier and more of a hassle to get, like 6-10 bucks a pop. Unlike the paper, there was no pilling at all on a canvas surface and was overall a much smoother experience. It took a bit of getting used to the canvas's surface, but it was a really fun project regardless.Aside from all the troubleshooting I had to do.You see, herein lies my major point of contention with these paint pens, but I'm sure this isn't just limited to posca, but all paint pens in general. I was painting this on an angle, and the canvas was stationed on an easel. Because of gravity, you can expect some of your pens to go rogue on you. They may appear to dry out or get streaky, but this is just due to the orientation of your canvas. This can typically be fixed by pumping the nib and shaking, but I will admit even after a while of this, some pens just don't want to cooperate. Some might stay watery, and others might stay streaky, and some might just die on you, and that's when I suggest a replacement. For instance, the navy blue and regular blue colors here were really temperamental, but after some deep, mindful, therapeutic thoughts such as "goddamnit, please let me finish this before these die on me" I was able to power through. Don't give up on your pens because they're showing signs of wear, because there's a chance they might still work/can be revived.TL:DR; These pens are spectacular for any artist of any skill level, but they aren't perfect and have some flaws. The orientation of the pen and your canvas affects the flow of the paint. In general, you won't see these problems with a majority of your pens, but every once in a while this may occur to a few in your batch. These are lovely for color laydown and produce consistent vibrant hues. They are definitely an investment though, so consider how you intend to use them and if it's worth the cost. These will make a lovely gift for any artist or creative!

Sentence: They pill the paper (almost all types of paper I’ve tried) and get little bits on the end of the nib that makes it scratchy to use and make the paint look uneven on the paper.
Content: I know a lot of people rave about Posca pens, but I’m not the biggest fan. They leak fairly often and get way too much paint on my paper. They pill the paper (almost all types of paper I’ve tried) and get little bits on the end of the nib that makes it scratchy to use and make the paint look uneven on the paper. I’ve tried other brands of paint pens, and some of them weren’t like this, so I know it’s not just a paint pen thing. It’s Posca specifically. (In fairness, one other brand did this, too.) I don’t know. I don’t HATE them. There’s just a lot of room for improvement, IMO.That said, the colors are quite vibrant, and they are convenient to use if you want to do something like a basic flat gouache looking painting. I may purchase more of these in the future, but they aren’t my favorite.

Sentence: They're easy to use and they're really worth its value.For anyone having trouble with exploding Posca Pens, here's a tip I learned.
Content: I've been wanting Posca Pens for a while now, and now that I'm finally able to use them, I'm just left speechless! They're easy to use and they're really worth its value.For anyone having trouble with exploding Posca Pens, here's a tip I learned. Hold the posca pen with the nib facing up, press down on the nib and then you'll hear the air coming out, and then you turn it upside down and start pressing the nib onto the paper for the ink to come down. Hope this helps!

Sentence: then you get a paper towel and fold it up, maybe even a piece of wax paper underneath if you worried about oozing pen paint everywhere, and you push the pen tip down on the dry towel.
Content: I haven't had any of the issues using these pens. first time getting them: You need to shake them, cap facing down for 3 minutes tops, and I mean a *real* shake. if you've ever had old acrylic paint in a bottle, and you had to shake them to stir it up, you know how much *umph* I'm talking about here. then you get a paper towel and fold it up, maybe even a piece of wax paper underneath if you worried about oozing pen paint everywhere, and you push the pen tip down on the dry towel. Hold it down for a good minute. This is the more laborious part because each pen tip may or may not be more dry/wet than the others. so it could seem like your pen is defective, but most likely you haven't put enough pressure on the tip for the paint to saturate the tip. I'd do circles or figure 8's so it doesn't feel like you're waiting for a proverbial elevator's worth of time for your pen to be functional. once the pen is saturated you'll all set, you might notice times where the tip will dry out, and you just dap it with the damp towel to fix that, if the paint is dried then a soft scrub with a damp towel may be needed. You might notice times where you start to get streaks, which means the pen needs a break. Cap it, shake it cap side down for a minute or so then you should be good to go. Now that the troubleshooting is over with here's my actual review.REVIEW:I bought these for multiple projects, rock painting, signing paintings, touching up miniatures, etc. these worked best on flat surfaces. those round mandala rocks that are everywhere didn't work well in my experience. after I got a sense of flow from the paint in the pen it was easier to write and color with it, but I didn't like the actual look on the pen since the paint is a matte finish. i was hoping for a glossier paint. the pigments in the paint are higher than anything else I own though, and I found myself just buying crystal clear gloss spray, and running out of paint in the pens before ever having a blowout and ink running out of my pens. I think that just has to do with individual pressure people put on their pens, it's a balance of firm enough like holding a screwdriver so it didn't shake when you use it, and remember there's a canister of paint in a pen, and slamming the tip down is just opening a socket for the paint, so using all your hand/arm power to press down would make the paint run free.So in conclusion, if you take the time needed these pens work great, they're made for drawing and painting on canvas or thicker "art" paper. That said rock art is doable just tricky sometimes, and coloring mugs or shoes could also be a viable use for these.

Sentence: Many people complain of paint pens leaking big blobs after the fist couple of uses.
Content: Posca pens are awesome...plain & simple.  I will re-interate what someone else said about using ANY kind of paint pen because I think this is invaluable information. PAINT PENS LEAK IF NOT STARTED PROPERLY!!!!  Many people complain of paint pens leaking big blobs after the fist couple of uses. It's a real issue! Here's the trick (at least as far as I know)... SHAKE THE PEN LIKE CRAZY. HOLD THE PEN UPRIGHT . PUT IT UP TO YOUR EAR, THEN HOLD DOWN THE NIB WITH YOUR FINGER TIP OR FINGER NAIL. YOU WILL HEAR A LITTLE CLICK & HISS. HOLD IT DOWN FOR 10 SECONDS. (Yes, count to 10 SLOWLY.) THEN FLIP THE PEN AND VERY GRADUALLY WORK THE PAINT INTO THE FRESH NIB BY PRESSING DOWN HALF WAY. BE GENTLE. BE PATIENT. LITTLE PRESSES UNTIL YOU SEE THE PAINT HAS FILLED THE NIB AND PAINT IS SHOWING UP FULL COLOR ON YOUR PAPER. Voila! That is it. Now the pen shouldn't "blob"!

Sentence: They're very comfortable to hold in my hand and draw or write with.
Content: These pens work if used properly. These, like other acrylic paint pens, require a little bit of prep before you use them. First, you want to gently press the nib inward, then you want to gently depress the nib several times (again, gently) until paint fills it.  Use a pen improperly, no matter the brand, and you will get paint blobs. A gentle hand and patience are the two magic tools here.When it comes to ease, Posca paint pens are just like holding a pen or a pencil. If you can do that, you'll be successful with these! They're very comfortable to hold in my hand and draw or write with. The flow of the paint is nice, and the colors are very vibrant and do no require more than one coat. I cannot speak of longevity, just yet, but depending on what you're painting with these, you should probably use some sort of sealer.The only thing I do not like about these markers is that they eat paper, it's not a big deal, certainly not a deal breaker for me, but it's definitely something I thought should be mentioned.These would make a great gift for yourself, or for the artists in your life.

Sentence: The colors remain vibrant and are quick-drying, yet easily wash off if they get on your hands.
Content: I absolutely LOVE these paint pens, and have both the set of medium and fine-point pens. The colors remain vibrant and are quick-drying, yet easily wash off if they get on your hands. They can be used on a variety of surfaces, and do not bleed through my sketchbook paper or Zentangle tiles. The only drawback was that all information on the box is in Chinese, so I had to look online to find out how to initially get the paint to flow (shake the pens, remove the cap, and pump the tip up and down on scrap paper until the pain flows into the tip). A simple insert in English would be a big help. The pens are appropriate for both adult and child use, and there is virtually no odor to them. They are my favorite paint medium.

Sentence: The tips are firm and don't fray.
Content: We use these paint pens for our hobby of painting smooth river stones, and they are terrific.  The tips are firm and don't fray. If you 'push' the line away from you (as you would if you're writing cursive and you are writing the letter "O"), you will get some feathering unless you ease up on the pressure.  Or, if you are drawing, just turn the stone so you are drawing the pen toward you rather than pushing it away from you.We have these pens in the Extra Fine point, the Fine point, and the Medium point, and we seldom use the tiny brushes anymore.  These pens allow us (and even our 92 year old Nana) to do fine detail work, and we love them!

Sentence: AMAZING!I originally bought these to paint a surfboard, and paint on acrylic and mixed media paper.
Content: AMAZING!I originally bought these to paint a surfboard, and paint on acrylic and mixed media paper. I own both the PC-5 and PC-3 in the original set, and the natural set, as well as extra PC-1 for black.PROS: These don't leave marks like pens do. When you run over the same area multiple times, it will no leave lines. They last for a long time! (I bought my first set in early 2015, and can still use over 50% of that box. (I draw a lot!) The colors are beautiful too!CONS: They can be runny sometimes, I keep an extra pad next to me to check how fast the paint is coming out, and if it drips too much I just press it a few times until it is normal again. If you plan to paint on a surface that will be outdoor, or touched, you should put a covering on it. The first board I did, I went in the water without spraying some sort of sealant and it smeared.TIPS: If I want to blend color I use Q-Tips! Works like a charm! If I paint on a surfboard, I always used a hand sander with a very fine paper to have it stick a little better. If I paint on acrylic paper or canvas, I seal with Mod Podge, either Matte or Satin, and sometimes both.

Sentence: I keep an art journal, and these write well over acrylics and watercolors on mixed media paper.
Content: I had never used Posco paint pens before and now I am hooked.  Product arrived exactly how pictured and the box they are in is great to store them.  Check the size of the pen output and make sure you understand which one you are buying.  The whole thing with Posco pens is patience when opening.  The pen has a white tip.  Shake the pen and then hold the pen directly vertical, perpendicular to the paper.  Press down, and wait, wait, while the ink spreads through tip.  It may take longer than expected to prime, but these pens write smooth.  I keep an art journal, and these write well over acrylics and watercolors on mixed media paper.  I love how they add extra details and clean up messy lines around the paint.  I pair these with the fine line ones, and they are so fun to use on any paper.

Sentence: I usually work on hard, textured surfaces.The paint mostly has great opacity, except for the light orange and yellow.
Content: "Medium nib" might be a bit deceptive. These are 2mm+ bullet tip nibs--great for some things, but not precision. I really like them in conjunction with a 3M or 1M set with finer nibs. I usually work on hard, textured surfaces.The paint mostly has great opacity, except for the light orange and yellow. However, that's a problem shared by the more expensive Molotow markers. Obviously the markers can't hold a huge amount of paint, but I've been happy with how much mileage I've gotten out of them so far.Someone commented that these might be knock-offs of authentic POSCA markers. I don't think this is the case--the shades perfectly match the markers I've purchased from my local art supply.

Sentence: I use them mainly in mixed media drawing, though I've also used them to label planters for my container garden and various household items.
Content: I love these! It has been my first experience using paint pens, and I plan to buy more. I use them mainly in mixed media drawing, though I've also used them to label planters for my container garden and various household items. I haven't had any problems with them drying out, even after being left on my desk unused for a month or two at a time. Some of the pens spurt out profuse amounts of paint when you press the tip in, but I've only had this issue with 3 of them. I just make sure to use a scrap piece of paper to test them while they're in use and use the leaky ones with caution as once you blot them they still mark just fine. They draw splendidly and I love how the paint sticks to most surfaces.I'm not sure what the paint is, but it layers over dry media just fine. It was really fun to experiment with them on black paper (all the colors show up great, though the white needed an extra layer over the first to be completely opaque). I can use it with a layer of fixative over pastels, without the fixative the tips tend to pick up the pigment and it takes a while to get it off. The medium points work well for filling in the designs I do, though I want to get some finer points for more detailed work and lettering. I can't read the instructions, so to be safe I shook them for five minutes before the first use and two minutes before using them when they have been sitting a while, giving them a good shake before I reload the tip during use. I also always store them tip up in the box on top of my desk.I look forward to picking up some more colors and tip sizes! They're quite addictive and I love the bright colors.

Sentence: I love the variety of colors that comes in the set and the pack is a great value for the money.
Content: These are fantastic! I have never used paint pens before, but I saw them at a kids museum and decided to try them. I love the variety of colors that comes in the set and the pack is a great value for the money. Most of the writing on the box is in Chinese, which isn't an issue- just wanted to forewarn future buyers. :)The markers are unique from other products in two ways- they are literally fast drying paint, so the colors are bold and cover the object you are writing on completely. There is very little run (unless you press to much), and when the paint drys (in a matter of minutes), it leaves a nice shiny finish. I used these to make pet rocks with the kids, to decorate Easter eggs (I dyed them first, then used the markers to draw designs over top), paper, wood projects, and I'm sure they would work on tons more surfaces.I appreciate all of the reviews I read on Amazon, and I hope you do to. If you found my review helpful, please let me know below. Thanks!

Sentence: Only one has run out and one became super runny, but the rest are still working fine!!!
Content: Update: It is 2020 and I am still using these paint pens 4 years later. Only one has run out and one became super runny, but the rest are still working fine!!! They get light usage, and I keep them stored, tip up, in the original box. Other paint pens from the big craft stores have had to be replaced multiple times, these are like that pink bunny!!!Awesome paint pens. I have used them in several projects on wood, canvas, paper, and plastic. The paint does not bleed and it dries quickly. I found the colors to be true to their caps.  I wish they had additional shades of the included colors. As stated, these are not fine tip, but depending on how you hold them you can get various line thicknesses.The directions are written in Japanese, but a.) if you're ordering paint pens, you probably know how to use them, and b.) if you don't it will take you about 20 seconds to locate directions on the net.This is a great value compared to what you'd pay at the craft store.

Sentence: I can't put my finger on whether the nib is the incorrect size, the valve is jenky or if the paint is too thin...
Content: **There is a "too long, didn't read" version at the bottom of this review**Disclosure: I am absolutely no stranger to paint markers. I am also no stranger to Uni Posca, and I decided to get a set of them because the last remaining one I had ran out of paint and the nib was getting pretty savage. This purchase is a lesson in consumer discretion because I should have read the 1 star reviews before purchasing, and here's why:So my package arrived 2 days early, without any updates on tracking info past "Shipped." "Oh cool, what a nice surprise" you may think. Naw, I had the misfortune of reading negative reviews beforehand saying these markers are gonna pool paint when pumping the valve and waste paint. I also kept track of the seller page and noticed the seller kept changing names (I bought from "japan-Container" but even to this day it keeps changing). I thought "surely these buyers are just being picky" because there were a lot of positive reviews compared to negative. Most of the positive reviews, if legitimate and non-bot, are clearly from beginners and hobbyists who haven't experimented with many paint markers and just settle for these out of ignorance. I should have just assumed they were bots/fake accounts from the beginning.As other people who have bought these and left a negative review have said: the markers dump paint out when you pump the nib down, even the first pump. On real Posca's, when you pump the nib down it juices the nib and primes it, just like with pretty much all other paint markers. But on these markers, even after the first pump it just dumps paint and pools at where the nib is. I can't put my finger on whether the nib is the incorrect size, the valve is jenky or if the paint is too thin... Either way, pretty much useless and I can't see myself using these markers on anything done professionally in the foreseeable future. I'm probably going to leave these markers alone until my Sharpie, Decocolor, Montana or Molotows run out of paint and could use more of a similar colour, otherwise i'll stick to familiar brands in the future. Hell, i'm even considering purchasing Molotow 227 empties just to use the Posca's paint.**Too Long, Didn't Read**Not real Uni Posca's, they are cheap knockoffs. Seller is non-responsive, shadey and routinely cycles through other sellers; tracking info is wildly inaccurate. Markers dump paint out when juicing the nib, even with pumping minimally. Spend the extra $ on purchasing locally or elsewhere.

But instructions are in Japanese, so: (1) Shake the pens for 30 seconds to a minute...you can shake several markers at the same time.  You'll notice the tip is white.  (2) Press the tip against a piece of scrap paper or cardboard, and pump the pen up and down until paint starts to make its way into the tip...again, you can do this with more than one pen at the same time.  They make a nice fat line, and dry pretty quick...only need to wait about 1 minute or less before painting a new layer.  So they're great if you like to paint eyes, flowers, and anything else that needs a few layers of details, and if you like to work at a fast pace.

Sentence: For Black Book use I wouldn't really recommend because they're water based and it tends to make the paper want to bend and chew it up.
Content: I do like these markers very much but I will say this. For Black Book use I wouldn't really recommend because they're water based and it tends to make the paper want to bend and chew it up. you can always use a light coat of " flat clean acrylic lacquer " but just a light coat to avoid the paper from being chewed up n bend.TIP #1 When pumping the markers up point the nib upwards then press the nib down to let the pressure out first then juice them up or you will end up with a big mess and paint shooting out of the marker.TIP #2 Make sure the paint is coming out solid or you will end up with really watered down lines, if not give the marker a quick little pump or two.TIP #3 Let the paint fully dry before going over it with another one.the light colors seem to have a hard time going over dark colors sometimes. mainly Yellow n Pink.but all n all I do like these markers for canvas use.

Sentence: Bright colors, the paint dries quickly, and colors layer together beautifully.
Content: Bright colors, the paint dries quickly, and colors layer together beautifully. My one disappointment was how easily the markers seem to "eat" some papers. Same thing happened on wood. Very annoying, as the bits of paper stuck to the nibs and had to be picked off with tweezers. It did fine on bristol paper, cardboard, primed canvas, and glossy surfaces. Overall, I would definitely buy these again (and I plan to!) because they're bright, have great coverage, and are incredibly versatile.

Sentence: superb cover with very consistent lines, a great selection of colors, odorless, I could go on and on.
Content: These are by far the best markers I have ever used. superb cover with very consistent lines, a great selection of colors, odorless, I could go on and on. And for some reason sometimes when I open my white marker a little bit of paint flies out, it's a rare occasion though. These markers write on nearly any surface. They are amazing and I recommend them for any artist of any skill level or style. I'm getting a set of fine points.

Sentence: And the blue and the pink colours are my absolute favourite for colour pay off.These prices for the pens are a steal, too.
Content: I absolutely love these paint pens.  I was introduced to them by watching ZHC on YouTube with my little brother.  We kept watching their draw challenges and thought the pens would be awesome to do art with so I ordered a ton of different Posca pens! this bundle being one of the many bundles I purchased.  The pens do not disappoint.  The marker only needs to be shook once and then pressed down on for the paint to disperse into the felt tip.  The blunt tip holds A LOT of paint,and if it seems like it's running out,  just give it a good shake and press down again to pump more paint into the felt tip.  The colours are amazing and so bright.  Once dried you can certainly layer other colours on top without them bleeding into eachother or the paint mixing.  I love the black pen for thick outlines.  And the blue and the pink colours are my absolute favourite for colour pay off.These prices for the pens are a steal,  too.  Because in my local art stores it is much much much more expensive for the paint pen packs. The only thing I dislike is that I feel like there's not as much paint in the pens as I would like.  Maybe I'm using them more often than most would and that's just how it goes.  I've been able to paint/draw multiple pictures before the pens run out,  though. I love that the caps snap on and do not come off easily like some caps to pens and paint pens.The colours are so bright and you do not have to press hard what so ever to get the paint out and keep it coming out smoothly.I absolutely one hundred percent will buy these pens again and from this seller.Things were packaged well and I recieved everything quite quicklyHighly recommend the Posca brand.  And if you haven't watched the art videos on the ZHC channel,  you have to! These artists are impeccable and it definitely inspired me to start drawing again and I'm glad my little brother has some inspiration to get into art.  He really loves the pens and has been so excited when Amazon comes to the front door with more of them haha

Sentence: Pros:Strongly OpaqueCrisp Matte FinishReversible TipsBright ColorsDries VERY quickly (suspiciously quickly...)Don't reak of xyleneCons:Can sometimes leave a chalky/pasty residue when filling in large areasIn my opinion, these are the best paint pens for the price.
Content: Pros:Strongly OpaqueCrisp Matte FinishReversible TipsBright ColorsDries VERY quickly (suspiciously quickly...)Don't reak of xyleneCons:Can sometimes leave a chalky/pasty residue when filling in large areasIn my opinion, these are the best paint pens for the price. I have been using paint pens like Decocolor and Craftsmart from craftstores like michael's and A.C. moore, and they are about the same price as these, but uniPOSCAs are MUCH MUCH MUCH better. Craftstore brand markers leak, blot, take forever to dry, and sometimes it can take multiple layers to get a totally opaque cover. And they REAK of xylene! I'll have headaches after I'm done using them! These are a game changer, awesome coverage, no terrible xylene smell, dry COMPLETELY within a matter of 1-2 minutes, and have bright colors. My only complaint is when filling in large areas there is sometimes a chalky/pasty residue left over the area, but this can easily be wiped away. Bottomline: Just wait the few shipping days to get these and stop wasting money at the cheap-os at the craft store.

Content: hiii! so i was scared to buy this mainly because i read reviews saying they’ll pool paint and it’s pretty cheap considering the amt of pens ur getting. i went out and bought a different set (same size and a few of the same colours as well) from micheals and i compared them both. the pens from amazon did not pool paint for me and the process of getting the ink to ‘flow’ was the same as the ones from micheals.these ones from amazon did have a few problems: the peach colour for example was not very opaque and almost “streaky” which was a bit odd.when compared to the ones from micheals, there were a few very very minor differences in colour for like three of the pens- it’s so unnoticeable though i had to squint to really see it.i’m not sure if maybe some people got a bad batch? but these behave the same way as other poscas for me so i dont think theyre knock offs or fake.tldr: be cautious when buying these because i’m seeing that it’s honestly a hit or miss. for me they worked great and behaved exactly like the other poscas i have. they also did not pool paint like others are saying but this is just my experience with them.

Sentence: Let's face it, $30 for 15 pens you can "adjust" is a much better bargain than 15 pens that will cost you $150-$200.
Content: As usual, these Uni-Posca paint pens perform superbly.  The only issue I have with these 5M markers is that the orange does not match the orange in the1M or 3M  pens.  It is "closer" to the "light orange" in the other set than it is to the orange. The pen cap matches the orange caps on the other sets, so I was kinda bummed about that. On the plus side, I guess I have 3 shades of orange now because I doubt the seller will replace it.The other colors all matched the 1M and 3M sets perfectly. I check all pens when they arrive and I recommend you do the same BEFORE you intermix you sets.  Just lay down some blocks of color side by side on some scrap canvas or watercolor paper.Also, I have tried 3 other brands of acrylic paint pens. The Uni-Posca pens outperform most brands.  Unless you want to spend $9-$12 PER PEN, the Uni-Posca pens are the way to go. Granted, the color selection is limited compared to the high-end paint pens, but you can supplement the Uni-Posca pens with those if necessary.ALSO, if you have a limited budget, stick with multiple sets of the Uni-Poscas, open the pens, and "adjust" the color with your own paint.  Just apply the adjusted color to the caps so you can readily see your new color while working with the pens. Let's face it, $30 for 15 pens you can "adjust" is a much better bargain than 15 pens that will cost you $150-$200. 👍😎BTW, the pens arrived in 4 days which was unexpected.

Sentence: Tips: Shake well before use.
Content: These acrylic based opaque markers are sheer delight for any artist to paint over any type of surface. I painted over my shoes, laptop and Instax camera reel box so far. Extremely delighted, worth your money. Tips: Shake well before use. Press the nib a few times over a flat surface to activate the markers and fill the tip with ink. Store them horizontally for better life of the markers. Don't forget to scrape off the industrial gloss from the surface of any glossy product,before applying the paint, in case you want to customise them with your artwork. For this, you can use a sandpaper or liquid spirit/nailpolish remover. After you're done painting, use an acrylic clear quote varnish to protect the paint from peeling off.

Sentence: You have to press the pen on a hard surface a few times to get the "ink" flowing, after shaking the pen until the internal ball is rattling loud and hard.
Content:
I've been looking for marker pens that give a good, even coverage with no pen marks and can't be easily erased. Sadly, these pens don't fit that bill. However, there are other features of these pens that appeal instead.

To start with, these chunky pens are like marker pens, with a wide 8mm nib. You have to press the pen on a hard surface a few times to get the "ink" flowing, after shaking the pen until the internal ball is rattling loud and hard. Once the "ink" is running, you're good to go.

I keep using "ink" as the liquid that comes out of these pens isn't like ink but, instead, is more like thin poster paint. The finish is very matt, exactly like poster paint, and the colours are bright. You'll definitely want to try out the colours on a spare bit of paper to see exactly what the colours will look like; subtle they aren't. The ink/paint does seem permanent and does resist casual rubbing. Once dry, you can cover over with a different colour, but I've found that, as the ink/paint dries, it tends to curl the paper. So far, I've had to reverse curl the paper and put it under some books to get a flat finish. However, I do like the matt finish you get, but you can still see the "brush" marks.

These aren't the marker pens I was looking for, but they are the marker pens I would have been looking for next, purely for the matt finish and bright colours.

Not perfect, but a good alternative to the more common ink-based systems.

Sentence: They do dry quickly so it makes blending hard.
Content: I really love Uni-POSCA paint markers!  I got these in a bold chisel tip so I could make signs for a school carnival. I was able to get bold and gorgeously opaque coloring that really stood out on a black background. I finished them with a quick spray of poly acrylic spray paint so it wouldn't run or smear and it lasted a very long time.I've attached a photo of a fun little craft project I did with black cardstock. The colors layer very well as long as you let them dry completely between layers. They do dry quickly so it makes blending hard. If you want a soft blended look acrylic paint is better than these paint pens.Lettering with these is a breeze and since it's a chisel tip you can get varying line widths depending on how you hold the markers. It does take a little while to get the ink flowing. I do all of the colors as soon as I get it so that I'm not wasting time getting the ink to flow in the middle of a project. I wish some colors like the white and peach were more opaque. The white, as pictured, leaves marker strokes which I don't like. Overall this is a great set though! Will be buying thes for life.

Sentence: When each one is activated, you do have to press down on the tip, a half dozen times or so, before the paint begins to flow.
Content: I tested these out last evening and they all worked fine.  When each one is activated, you do have to press down on the tip, a half dozen times or so, before the paint begins to flow.  I played around a bit, and was very happy with them.  There wasn't any noticeable shift in color when dry.  Do be sure  any paint is dry before you go over it with another color though.  Otherwise you will get the first color on the tip of the new color pen.  This happened to me.  I quickly released more color; dabbed at the tip with a wet paper towel, and it cleaned up fine.  I would use another blending tool, if you like to blend when you paint.  I am not a blender/painter, so I didn't test that out.  Another thing I did test though was using it to ink up some home made stamps made of craft foam.  They worked beautifully for that application.  These will be great for art journaling.  Because all of the information was in another language, I do not have any idea of the lightfast ratings.  I would not use them in any fine art pieces.  The pigment load seems good though, and as mentioned before; dry true to color.

Sentence: They are really easy to use and dont leak at all, which is something that tends to happen to other cheaper paint pens.
Content: I've had these markers for about four months now and though i do jot use them continuously, i have made several large projects such as the big menu board pictured and i still get very good ink payoff. They are really easy to use and dont leak at all, which is something that tends to happen to other cheaper paint pens. The colors are bright and opaque. They are also great for layering but you do have to make sure that the ink has dried completely, which only takes a couple of minutes. They can write on almost any surface. The nib is soft but firm enough to hold its shape, though i would recommend against pressing down too hard as it could destroy the tip and render the marker useless. It only takes a few shakes or a couple pumps on the tip to get ink flowing. Overall this is a great marker that i highly recommend for artists who want to learn a new medium and are well worth the price.

Sentence: I originally ordered this pack of markers for marking various industrial items, but quickly found out the paint used in this product is not permanent at all.
Content: I originally ordered this pack of markers for marking various industrial items, but quickly found out the paint used in this product is not permanent at all. (Not to mention the fact that the writing nibs on them are soft and obviously built for art paper/canvases.) These markers would definitely be perfect for any school projects/creating posters as they are fairly opaque and apply to surfaces with ease. The marker body and valve are both made of plastic, but this doesn't seem to affect the performance at all. Overall, I'd have to say they are perfect markers for light art uses, but I would not recommend them for outdoor and/or alternative surface use. I really enjoyed the paint used in these markers on paper, so I'm looking forward to purchasing the smaller sized markers from this company for later projects!

Sentence: This is about as good as it gets for a high quality acrylic water based marker.
Content: This is about as good as it gets for a high quality acrylic water based marker. I've used and abused many high quality acrylic markers and nothing compares to the Uni-POSCA PC series for quality versus price. Posca ink is world renowned for it's silky smooth, slightly chalky finish, not to mention the high opacity.These markers are excellent on paper, canvas, wood, plastic, glass, or metal, and just about any smooth dry surface can be painted. Really smooth surfaces such as plastic may need a slight scuffing with a high grit sandpaper to ensure proper paint adherence. Rough surfaces will work in some cases, but tend to eat up the nib and require more ink for complete coverage.One coat is usually suffice, but I like to apply two coats to smooth out any uneven areas, with at least ten minutes of drying time between coats. Several light coats of a matte acrylic clear coat will ensure permanency as well for long term archival of projects.

Sentence: Bright colors, the paint dries quickly, and colors layer together beautifully.
Content: Bright colors, the paint dries quickly, and colors layer together beautifully. I love them! However, I have to give them 4 stars...Two disappointments:1) As with the medium points, the extra-fine point markers seem to "eat" some papers. I tried using them with my regular sketchbook, kraft paper, black paper, and other cardstocks and passing over an area more than once, the nibs scratched away the fibers of the paper. Same thing happened on wood. Very annoying, as the bits of paper stuck to the nibs and had to be picked off with tweezers. It did fine on bristol paper, cardboard, primed canvas, and glossy surfaces.2) The lighter colors (white, pink, baby blue, yellow) need to be shaken and tested before every use, because sometimes the color comes out very watery and just soaks the paper instead of coloring it.Despite this, I would definitely buy these again (and I plan to!) because they're bright, have great coverage, and are incredibly versatile. After I received them, I couldn't put them down for more than a week!

Sentence: A lot of people told me that paint pens don’t work well, they skip, they splatter, they are prone to leaking, the tips shred, etc.
Content: I just started painting rocks, and I did a lot of research before buying my supplies. I chose these pens because they had a high average rating. If I layer the red and use clear coat spray / shellac, it seems to help with this. I currently use dark gray river rocks, and some of the darker colors (dark blue, purple, black) don’t show up as well, but all colors should work great on white rocks.I highly recommend these pens if you are using them for rock painting.

Sentence: The video instructor said she taped her caps on to be sure the markers wouldn't dry out.I think this set might be less expensive because the markers are smaller than the ones used in the videos.
Content: WOW! These are great acrylic paint markers! One of my favorite video acrylic painting teachers recommends these markers and uses them to sign her name on her painting at the end of each lesson. Another video teacher uses paint markers for projects that require a small line such as fine tree branches. I had purchased a couple of markers from a leading American acrylic paint brand and kept wondering why my markers didn't work like the ones in the video lessons. Then I saw this set and the price was so good I wanted to try them out. I LOVE these markers; the tips are actually as fine as advertised. The video instructor said she taped her caps on to be sure the markers wouldn't dry out.I think this set might be less expensive because the markers are smaller than the ones used in the videos. I don't think they are full sized Posca markers, but that is OK with me since it enabled me to get 12 beautiful colors. One full size marker of the American brand company cost about $7, while 12 markers in this pack was about $25 at the time I purchased them. I tried to find a volume on both brands of pen, but the Posca pen info is all in Japanese, and the American brand did not have a volume that I could find. I did find nib size--the Posca was 0.7mm and the American brand was 2.4mm. Both brands are about the same diameter, but the pens in this set are about an inch shorter than the other brand (Posca-4.75", other brand 5.5" with caps on).I tested the titanium white since some acrylic colors, such as yellow, are very transparent and need the area under them painted white first to give them good coverage. Both brands needed several coats of white to cover over a black line so I would say they were equal in transparency.I was concerned about the tips being firm enough to last a long time. I have a tendency to press too hard most of the time and some marker tips get mushy with use. Since the tip has to be pressed against a firm surface to prime with paint to get it flowing this could be a problem. I was pleased to see that the tips kept their point after pressing against the surface of my craft table (with a protective silicone cover over it).I needed a teal color but the set did not have teal. I pressed the tip several times to get a tiny puddle of a light blue and another puddle of yellow. I mixed a tiny bit of each color until I got a match close enough to what I needed, used a small paint brush to fill in where I needed to cover a mistake, and was very pleased with the result.I would highly recommend this set to any one wanting to try out acrylic markers. I don't know how long the markers will last since they are not full size, but I think if they are used carefully and capped immediately after use they will be OK. Tape placed around the cap edge of the marker to seal out any air leaks should help. The markers are a great size for adding to a travel crafts bag and would make great stocking stuffers for the painter/crafter in your family.

Both brands are about the same diameter, but the pens in this set are about an inch shorter than the other brand (Posca-4.75", other brand 5.5" with caps on).I tested the titanium white since some acrylic colors, such as yellow, are very transparent and need the area under them painted white first to give them good coverage. Both brands needed several coats of white to cover over a black line so I would say they were equal in transparency.I was concerned about the tips being firm enough to last a long time. I have a tendency to press too hard most of the time and some marker tips get mushy with use. Since the tip has to be pressed against a firm surface to prime with paint to get it flowing this could be a problem. I was pleased to see that the tips kept their point after pressing against the surface of my craft table (with a protective silicone cover over it).I needed a teal color but the set did not have teal. I pressed the tip several times to get a tiny puddle of a light blue and another puddle of yellow. I mixed a tiny bit of each color until I got a match close enough to what I needed, used a small paint brush to fill in where I needed to cover a mistake, and was very pleased with the result.I would highly recommend this set to any one wanting to try out acrylic markers. I don't know how long the markers will last since they are not full size, but I think if they are used carefully and capped immediately after use they will be OK. Tape placed around the cap edge of the marker to seal out any air leaks should help. The markers are a great size for adding to a travel crafts bag and would make great stocking stuffers for the painter/crafter in your family.

Sentence: Others almost always have dried paint in the point fibers so you have to work at getting the paint to flow once again and then, in addition to overly large lines, the paint flows unevenly because it's kind of flowing along the outside of dried up nib instead of through it.
Content: This is how every paint marker should be made. Instead of some compressed fabric point to carry/apply the paint, these have a hard plastic nib that the paint flows through. You still have to push down hard enough to compress point back up into the barrel to first get the paint to flow, but unlike every other brand, instead of partially dulling and rounding out the nib, you have a very fine point that you can use to either make precise lines and dots or go over an area more for wider effects. On top of that, when you go to use them again at a later date, they still work. Others almost always have dried paint in the point fibers so you have to work at getting the paint to flow once again and then, in addition to overly large lines, the paint flows unevenly because it's kind of flowing along the outside of dried up nib instead of through it.  Try these if you've almost given up on paint markers and if you have never used paint markers before, don't bother with any others. Hopefully, all the other brands will switch to this method.

Sentence: The color is bold, and really pops out on what you are using them on.
Content: First of all I must stress that these are PAINT markers and not Alcohol based markers. Both are good, but both behave slightly differently.This being said, these Posca markers are great. The color is bold, and really pops out on what you are using them on. However, these are NOT wide tips. They have a nice point to them and are not super fine. With the right angle, you can get a variety of thickness.Now, I've seen reviews that say that they pool out too much, and yes this can happen, but if you're careful you can prevent this from happening. This can also happen to other kinds of markers too. I started by slowly pressing the tip gently, and watched for the paint to start filling the nib. Once it stared I lifted the pen and waited for it to fill completely. The paint then smoothly flows out as you run it along the object you're drawing on. You may have to go over your line a few times to get a solid line, but with patience it'll look nice. Let the paint dry completely before going over it, otherwise the colors will bleed into each other. As I said, these paint markers are great. Colorful, bold, and works on many different surfaces. Just be careful and don't press down too hard, or the paint will pool out everywhere. I've included a test run of these on common scrap paper. No bleed through as long as you don't keep the pen on one spot for too long.

Sentence: Some colours took a few more pushes, however none of the nibs had a blob of paint come out like some people complained about.Once the ink was in the nib, the pen was super easy to use and they have been ready to use repeatedly without anything else being done.
Content: Got these paint pens a few days ago and am loving them! To get the ink into the nib I pushed the pen straight down onto an old piece of cloth, held for a second or two, and then repeated it. I held the pen up to see if ink was flowing into the nib. If it wasn’t, I repeated the process checking after each push. Some colours took a few more pushes, however none of the nibs had a blob of paint come out like some people complained about.Once the ink was in the nib, the pen was super easy to use and they have been ready to use repeatedly without anything else being done. Of course, you have to shake them to mix the paint the same as you would a bottle of paint.A couple of times there was a bit of splatter but I’ve discovered that it doesn’t happen if you move the pen towards you.They are so easy to use and are perfect for doing detail work on rocks. I used the black one to outline the images on all three rocks. I also used pink, yellow, green and orange on the cat rock.

Sentence: I also use them in my mixed media painting.
Content: I love these posca paint pens!  I mostly use them for painting on rocks, they are opaque and if you make a mistake it is easy to fix it by waiting till it is dry and then painting over the mistake.  If you are putting your rocks outside, they should have a clear spray coat applied, 4 or 5 coats.  First coat very light to seal the colors.  I found that if I didn't clear seal them with 4 or 5 coats, after a year of being out in the weather (very rainy here) the paint would flake off.  I'm waiting to see if more coats will prevent that, plus I clear coated both sides to be extra sure.  They haven't been through a winter yet.  I don't like the red color, it is too orangy for me, but all the other colors I'm happy with.  I also use them in my mixed media painting.  As long as I'm painting on a dry surface they seem to paint over anything without clogging.  If I'm very careful I can get a thin line made or tiny dots, or be more generous to fill in a larger space.  The construction of the tip is such that they can splatter tiny splats if you aren't careful, there is a bit of a learning curve to their use in detailed coloring.  But all in all, I'm very satisfied with these PC 1m pens.  I also have some in size 0.7mm in pastel colors that are wonderful and some sparkly ones.  Different tip on them.  They all work well.

Sentence: The paint is nicely opaque, it goes on canvas fairly easily, and there's a nice range of color.There's a few issues that make these less than perfect- the hard, nylon/plastic tips make the paint "splatter" if there's any texture at all on your canvas, and if you are painting over dried acrylic that's not perfectly smooth, that will happen.
Content: I am a painter who does work in acrylic on canvas and I paint really detailed, *tiny* patterns. Getting that small with a brush, even the smallest ones on the market, is sometimes really difficult so I have been searching high and low for acrylic paint pens that work on canvas, work with traditional fluid/heavy body acrylics, and are fairly opaque. The Posca is one of the better brands I have found, especially at the price point. The paint is nicely opaque, it goes on canvas fairly easily, and there's a nice range of color.There's a few issues that make these less than perfect- the hard, nylon/plastic tips make the paint "splatter" if there's any texture at all on your canvas, and if you are painting over dried acrylic that's not perfectly smooth, that will happen. But it happens less than with the water-based Sharpies. The colors are a bit dull- they aren't rich, but they ARE opaque, so I find that I can just use the Poscas for the detail work (especially filling in tiny open areas) and then dab a little fluid acrylic over the center of what I did with the Posca and the color intensifies.All in all, these (along with the Derwent Graphik Painters) are the best acrylic paint pens for working on canvas that I have found. Definitely recommended.

The colors are a bit dull- they aren't rich, but they ARE opaque, so I find that I can just use the Poscas for the detail work (especially filling in tiny open areas) and then dab a little fluid acrylic over the center of what I did with the Posca and the color intensifies.All in all, these (along with the Derwent Graphik Painters) are the best acrylic paint pens for working on canvas that I have found. Definitely recommended.

Sentence: I've got more expensive markers.
Content: These ARE everything they have been hyped to be! I was hesitant, so glad I splurged and got these markers. These are absolutely fantastic! They arrived faster than expected, they were all individually shrink wrapped and all of these work with no issue.  They write beautifully on my relatively smooth rocks which I have primed with white. I can definitely see why people rave over these. Very easy to use. Quality!The only thing is I was surprised they felt small. But I have only the Montana markers to compare to, and those are more long and skinny. I don't think it's a lack of product, I think it's just form and function. I will be buying additional colors as needed.I will also be using these on baked polymer clay for doodle art pendants.  I can't wait!

Sentence: The tips are firm and don't fray.
Content: We use these paint pens for our hobby of painting smooth river stones, and they are terrific.  The tips are firm and don't fray.  The only caution I would give is that you get the best and smoothest line if you 'pull' the pen toward you.  If you 'push' the line away from you (as you would if you're writing cursive and you are writing the letter "O"), you will get some feathering unless you ease up on the pressure.  Or, if you are drawing, just turn the stone so you are drawing the pen toward you rather than pushing it away from you.We have these pens in the Extra Fine point, the Fine point, and the Medium point, and we seldom use the tiny brushes anymore.  These pens allow us (and even our 92 year old Nana) to do fine detail work, and we love them!We allow our artwork to dry when we change colors, usually using a hair dryer to speed things along.  We also spray our stones with a clear coat spray, and these pens do not run.Tips:  When a pen is used for the first time, you'll need to "pump" the tip of the pen gently on a practice surface, like a paper plate or sheet of copy paper.  You will see the ink flow into the tip.  Then you'll need to cap the pen and shake it.  Draw a line on the practice surface, to make sure it is ready.  You will need to shake the pen every time you use it, and occasionally, you will need to pump it on the practice surface again, to get the ink flowing.  CAUTION:  If you depress the tip of the pen on your artwork, it will allow the ink to flow freely down the tip.  This will cause a "blob" on your artwork.

Sentence: So, as far as longevity goes, it's up to you and how much or little you use them and for what purpose.
Content: I first tried POSCA paint pens about 9 months ago and fell in love. Hard. I'm not an artist, I can barely draw a straight line but I am a decorative planner who is a severe pen snob and a bit of a pen sl*t as well. But I'm loyal! I originally purchased POSCAs to write on my black planner paper and have been doing so ever since. I also use them to write on my neon and white planner paper. So, as far as longevity goes, it's up to you and how much or little you use them and for what purpose. I have several colors from that original purchase with a lot of paint left in them but colors like white, black, pink, yellow, bright blue, and a few more, those are almost empty(and I'm on my 2nd white pen) because I would use those colors more. As far as sheerness, well, that also depends on you and how much pressure you put on the pen when you are doing what you do. When I'm writing, they are not sheer at all. Like I said, I'm not an artist, so I've never used them for anything but writing. I suspect if you were an artist and adjusted the ink flow and your pressure, you could make it as sheer as you needed or as thick as you needed. For my purpose, I love these pens and I highly recommend them to any other planner people out there. Just make sure you have a heavy enough paper so you dont get bleed through. Happy Planner paper or Recollections planner paper wont cut it. You need Lights Planner Action paper, Paper Penguin Co, and the like(ALWAYS shop small-you get better quality!). I hope this review helps someone, all I did was gush about POSCAs. I know I've seen people decorate glass, Chucks, Vans, other, cheaper canvas shoes, faux leather,  I've had friends that painted rocks with these, lettered tshirts for a quick protest shirt, posters, etc, so the possibilities are endless, really. Check out POSCA on IG, they usually feature people's projects and do giveaways. Also, unless they are on sale or you have a coupon, this is the best price I've seen, as opposed to crafting stores. Hope this helps!! Happy crafting/arting!

Sentence: Betem had more colors and were considerably less expensive, but the Posca’s 12 colors were certainly sufficient – you just might have to wait your turn a little more for the color you wanted.
Content: We've now purchased 2 brands of acrylic paint pens this summer... these (Posca, made in Japan) and Betem (made in China).  They've been a huge hit!  Originally purchased for the kids to paint lake rocks as much as their hearts desired, we found the adults sitting down with the kids, using the markers almost as much!  It also creates an easy kids-adults interaction environment, which is helpful when they perhaps don’t already know each other well (as at a family reunion).  So all in all, great!!  Poscas were great in every way – they wrote on glass (we had some wine glass decorating going on – let the paint cure for a day or two), and the colors were vibrant.  They don’t have dual tips like Betem (meaning broad at one end, fine point at the other) but you can achieve fine, broad, or anything inbetween easily via pressure applied and angle of the pen.  The kids had no problem mastering that.  Betem had more colors and were considerably less expensive, but the Posca’s 12 colors were certainly sufficient – you just might have to wait your turn a little more for the color you wanted.  While both brands were a big hit, if you want to write on glass, get the Posca brand – Betem states they write on glass but our experience was that they absolutely do not.  Last comment -- these make for a good rainy day activity as well, but you might want to put down paper or such first.  We created acrylic paint spots and smears on a picnic table and deck, which isn't a big deal in that kid-oriented outside area, but it's a consideration for some locations.

Sentence: Before these I only used Painters brand that you can buy at art and department stores.I bought these as a cheap alternative, not expecting them to be anywhere near as nice as the costlier brands out there.
Content: I've used these on and off for a year now. About as much as I used other paint markers. Before these I only used Painters brand that you can buy at art and department stores.I bought these as a cheap alternative, not expecting them to be anywhere near as nice as the costlier brands out there. I bought them not because I didn't HAVE markers, but because the markers I did have had dried up within a year of sparse use and tightly closed lids. Much to my surprise in the year I've owned THIS Uni-Posca brand, they are STILL working PERFECTLY. Just make sure to shake them up and get the paint flowing on a scrap paper (like all paint markers).Not to mention, I bought some gold Painters brand within that year after buying this brand, used them a couple times over the months, and one of the Painters markers is actually partially DRIED?! Keep in mind I keep all brands closed tightly and well stored, and yet the more expensive brand has dried partially while the cheap Uni-Posca brand is still working great. And I've even had this brand longer than I had the partially dried Painters marker for. Both brands have had relatively light use. Makes you wonder if Painters brand wants their markers to dry out fast so you have to buy more when you still had some left that don't work well anymore.

Content: I have been using ball point pens in drawings for years because of the vibrant colors and contrasts, but especially for the control you have in detail work due to the fine tips. However, they are extremely limited in what you can do with them, and once the ink is on the paper - final corrections are close to impossible, at least in my experience. I find these pens/markers to be the perfect solution. I tried them out after having a bit of luck with Sharpie extra fine point water based paint markers. Great for those of us who are maybe a little too obsessive about lines and details to experiment with paints and brushes - or in my case too broke from compulsive online shopping to afford the good materials. Ha.In any case, I have spent countless hours and plenty of cash in the past twenty years tracking down, researching and experimenting with colored pens and markers. I am writing this review because in all honesty, I have never come across a better performing tool for this purpose. The paint flows smooth and consistently - and even lasts a long time. It is easy to achieve bright, full coverage. The Extra Fine Point lives up to the hype I am laying on. The best part to me is that you can easily correct ANY MISTAKE. Over and over. The first drawing I did must have areas of 10-15 layers in some places. This does make it harder for me to actually finish a drawing, but at least Uni-Posca markers allow you this option.

My hands are very shaky and I am not able to get my details in a project. Overall, the smooth light vibrant paint with the amount of colors for the price makes me like it. I wish I could love it, but I'm upset with the orange pen.

Sentence: They do dry quickly so if you plan to use techniques that require smearing or mixing, you need to work fast.
Content: Great pens but the price has gone up to a ridiculous amount in less than a month. I paid $18 in July 2017. I paint rocks with these and the extra-fine tip is perfect for writing words and drawing fine lines. They do dry quickly so if you plan to use techniques that require smearing or mixing, you need to work fast. The new pen tip needs to be depressed in order to bring the paint down the tip so you can begin painting. Wipe off excess paint before applying or it will splatter on your project. The pens seem fairly durable but probably will not do well with rough handling. The paint is easily applied and there is no need to press hard. These are not like markers where more pressure gets a darker color, gentle pressure is enough. Happy painting!

Sentence: About the claim that they are lightfast - some of the colors without a doubt hold up wonderfully over time.
Content: About the claim that they are lightfast - some of the colors without a doubt hold up wonderfully over time. I've done a full year of testing in a window and in this set of 12 colors only 3 faded badly: PINK ORANGE AND BROWN fade within 1 year of daytime sun exposure inside a northern facing window with limited UV exposure during the AM hours. This should give a good example of what could happen to artwork you hung on a wall near a window created with these markers.There was very minor change to the yellow that got lighter. Now, no artwork should ever be stored in direct sunlight, but this is a good way to test how your art will hold up over time. I have quality paints from other manufacturers such as Montana acrylic markers that held up a bit better over time. Overall the product is quality enough that I consider it useful for artists who will sell their work, however these 3 colors you may not want to use in artwork you know will be hung on a wall in a well lit room. I post all my tests on The Enchanted Gallery's lightfast testing page, including many brands of acrylic paint, india inks, watercolors and craft supplies. Hope this helps someone :)

Sentence: Now I haven't used these extensively yet, but what I have done with them has been enjoyable thus far.Cons, the nibs are a teeny bit scratchy and if you're not careful with the paper you use or how much pressure you apply when drawing, the markers will "spit" so you'll get flecks of little paint everywhere.
Content: While these are a little smaller than I had thought they were going to be, (chock that up to me not reading the description properly lol), these are actually a lot better than I was expecting.I've used paint pens before, albeit they were oil based paints by Sharpie, and I've got to say, I'm pleasantly surprised by Posca.I'd been leery of using them before because I'd heard they were notorious for gumming up and drying out but they don't seem to have that issue if you take care of them properly. Now I haven't used these extensively yet, but what I have done with them has been enjoyable thus far.Cons, the nibs are a teeny bit scratchy and if you're not careful with the paper you use or how much pressure you apply when drawing, the markers will "spit" so you'll get flecks of little paint everywhere. Likewise, sometimes they can "leak" in that while you're drawing you COULD end up with a blob in your line work, but I have deduced it's most likely caused by pushing the nib in accidentally while you move the pen. Additionally, dependant on the colour, they can take a while to dry so you'll want to give them time to do so between coats and or just use a heat gun or a hair dryer to speed up the process.Pros, a little goes a LONG way, so you don't really need to empty them in one go and they don't really need more than two coats, if that. They work on a multitude of surfaces like paper, plastic, metal, wood, vinyl, but as with most acrylic paints, you'll want to seal them for longevity later. One feature I thought was kind of cool is that they work with Copic makers~! You can use Copics on top of them, but you have to be careful not to use too much of the Copic ink in one spot or it might dissolve the paint. Lastly, these work surprisingly well with Shrink-Dinks~! Just don't use an excessive amount of the paint and be sure to coat them with varnish after so they stay.All in all, I'm glad I finally caved and bought these. Definitely recommend for people that want to give an acrylic paint pen a try~!

Sentence: I was under the impression the ink (though water-based) would stay on the ping pong balls without rubbing off, but the opposite happened when I used them.
Content: After reading all the reviews I was sure these markers would work for my applications--writing letters on ping pong balls for a spelling game, and writing words on cardstock for a literacy activity.  I was under the impression the ink  (though water-based) would stay on the ping pong balls without rubbing off, but the opposite happened when I used them.  The paint remained wet and transferred to other balls and the container I set them in to dry.  After about 20 minutes of drying time, I tested the writing by rubbing it gently to see if it would come off--and it did...easily.  I then tried the markers on paper and found that they cause the paper to shred and ball up on the tip (the way regular washable markers do if you keep coloring over the same spot repeatedly).  I am not sure what else I can use them for since these two applications seemed pretty simple.  Maybe I am doing something wrong?  Just don't want someone else to waste his/her money.

Sentence: My first impression when I opened these was that they looked cheap which was honestly not what I was expecting.
Content: My first impression when I opened these was that they looked cheap which was honestly not what I was expecting. But when I started using them, I was very pleased with the results.I tested them with my 7-year-old kiddo on blank canvas boards from the art store. The colors were lovely and true, and it really was like drawing with paint. My kiddo was very pleased with their knight drawing/painting.The colors are a bit sheer, especially the light colors (white, yellow, etc), and it took a few coats for them to really stand out on top of the darker colors. (My second photo shows the painting after I went back and added more colors on top of / with the first ones I chose.I did go back to them several days later (expecting the tips to be completely dried up honestly) and they worked as well as they did the first use.I would like to use them on fabric, and that's my next test. I've heard mixed reviews about how well they work on fabric. I'm also a bit concerned that the fabric I would like to use them on (a dark stretchy denim) might not take the colors very well.So, overall I'd say these are good pens, especially if you're going to be working on a light-colored surface.

Sentence: I just pulled them out to use again and the two I used were kind of dried out and wouldn’t budge in order to pump new paint to the tip.
Content: These pens are great! The paint flows so nice and smoothly! No having to go and pump the pen over and over during use like with previous pens I’ve used. I have used them on stones as well as wood. My FAVOURITE thing about these pens though is the customer service. I bought my pens over a year ago and only used two at that time. I just pulled them out to use again and the two I used were kind of dried out and wouldn’t budge in order to pump new paint to the tip. Of course my first course of action was force. Do not recommend! I mashed my white paint tip and now the tip won’t pop back out when I pump it. Not wanting to wreck the black one too I decided to email them using the email address that came in the box. I asked if I could do something to fix the dried tip on my black pen and if there was anything I could do to prevent the same thing happening to other pens in the future. They got back to me within an hour! Suggested gently pulling the tip out and washing it and the reinserting it and trying again. Worked like a charm! She also suggested washing tips after use to prevent it in the future. I am SO GLAD I contacted them! My white one is hooped because of me whacking it lol but the black one is now good as new. Highly recommend!

It's possible that I just got a defective box, but in that case, I would think it would only be maybe 1-2 pens max that didn't work -- not almost half of the box.

Sentence: The pens are so easy to use, which is appreciated as I am a lifelong artist who has gotten incapacitated through years.
Content: Painted a garden hat as a gift for my green-thumb daughter.  The pens are so easy to use, which is appreciated as I am a lifelong artist who has gotten incapacitated through years.  Sitting at a table for any length of time is a no-no.  With these little paint dispensers I was able to work from my recliner and still accomplish pretty close to what I had in mind.  The paint soaks into the fabric at first, until a layer dries and seals, then layering colors is far easier.  It took several coats of paint to get the lighter colors to show up as the accents I wanted.  I will definitely use this product again for similar hat projects, but have learned from this first one.  In future, a coat of clear acrylic gesso or a layer of background color will be painted on first, let dry, then go for the art work.  ...  I'm back today to buy a larger set of Artistry pens with fine points and more colors.  I was frustrated by the lack of variety of color in this set... only one green and no light blue or violet, for instance.  Otherwise, excellent.  Update:  Also painted a garden hat for myself.

Sentence: Pens were easy to use and gave a good result when used on standard white mugs.
Content: Pens were easy to use and gave a good result when used on standard white mugs. Most of the colors wrote smoothly and clearly. Yellow was a little drippy but others worked perfectly. Note that before you bake, the paint will wash off completely in water so if you mess up, you can redo your design.I tested removing paint by scratching with my fingernail, and with a scrubby sponge, on paint that had been baked on in the oven. After baking, some colors seem to adhere better than others. Green and blue seemed to have "thinner" paint and scratched/washed off more easily after baking.  If you use these pens on plates that will be cut on with a knife, I think you can count on the design scratching.I also tested running my painted mugs through the dishwasher: green washed off completely in one wash while red, pink, yellow, and purple seemed unaffected by one dishwasher wash. Multiple washes may wash the paint off slowly over time. Hand washing is definitely better but once or twice in the dishwasher probably won't matter too much.Overall, these pens got the job done (personalizing mugs for a party) for a reasonable price. And I will use them again on other projects.

Sentence: Finally, the inks are water-resistant but will still dilute somewhat when in contact with water, even when allowed to dry for several days.
Content: A couple of things to know before using these in your art project...They take at least a day to dry fully. If you paint layers on top of each other before the paint is dry, they will bleed into one another, creating a hybrid colour which will also change the colour of the nib. I found it frustrating that I had to wait a day before applying the next layer with confidence. When creating art, I really just want to get on with it. Also, when you pump the pen and apply ink to the nib, sometimes not much comes out and sometimes too much which will create blobs of paint on your project and then need to be cleaned up. Not great for applying fine lines. Finally, the inks are water-resistant but will still dilute somewhat when in contact with water, even when allowed to dry for several days. Be warned.That said, they are brilliant. The colours are vibrant and semi-permanent and dry to solid a matt finish which can pretty much be applied to any dry surface. Great fun and easy to use. I would not call the paint permanent though by any meaningful definition.  4 stars. A good alternative to more expensive brands, and would definitely buy again. Hope this helped.
