Sentence: They are expensive, and the nibs wear out easily and the paint is too thin to cover.
Content: I paint in acrylic, and sometimes I like to use paint markers to add clarity to an image or even give the painting a graffitied look. I have a large collection of Liquatex acrylic markers, but their performance is disappointing. They are expensive, and the nibs wear out easily and the paint is too thin to cover. Aristo's acrylic paint markers are less expensive, but I would buy them even if they weren't. The paint is consistent, and even the lightest colors can cover darker ones. Also, the pen nibs don't wear out at all. I only wish that Aristo made more colors. The largest collection has only 30 pens. If this company made more colors, I would purchase them all.

Sentence: I ordered both the thin and wide water based acrylic pens so that I could try a full range of possibilities with this product.
Content: I used Artistro paint pens to paint an underwater scene on a large stone. I ordered both the thin and wide water based acrylic pens so that I could try a full range of possibilities with this product. As a professional artist who sells their work I normally paint with high quality fluid acrylics and  brushes. Paint pens were a departure for me, and I was pleasantly surprised with how vibrant the hues were, and I thought that they covered well too. I like to paint in layers and blend colors and found that a dampened brush made blending more than one color together possible, but the crisp edges of the thin markers made defining small details simple. The light colors easily covered dark areas although I gave white areas an extra coat. I had to figure out how much pressure I needed to place on the tips so that too much paint wouldn’t come out at once but once I figured it out I didn’t have any issues. I would recommend these pens for rock painting (which is what I did with them) and will also try them on other types of support such as canvas and paper.

Sentence: They were super easy to use and provided a thin, opaque layer of paint that didn't run.
Content: I bought these to paint rocks with my kids (10, 8, 6).  They worked fabulously! They were super easy to use and provided a thin, opaque layer of paint that didn't run.  They dried pretty quickly. The colours were vibrant and my kids especially liked the gold and silver colours.  They were easier and tidier than using paints and brushes, although we did also use paints and brushes.  They were super easy to get consistent line thicknesses (see the rainbow rock) and also easy to write large words. (The words on this rock were done with other, extra fine paint markers)  I would recommend them. The colour selection was great as a starting-out set, which would also make them a great gift for budding artists or crafters.  I am excited to try them for different projects as well.

Sentence: Applied 2 coats of waterproof and UV-resistant sealant.
Content: SO disappointed.  Worked with the PTA to bring a rock art project to over 200 elementary school students.  I purchased 5 sets for school use and 2 for my personal use.  I used these markers after reading multiple reviews.  Product states that they are durable and colorfast and can be used on stone.  Reviews recommended these for rock art.  Applied 2 coats of waterproof and UV-resistant sealant.  Less than a month in to a mild Pacific NW summer, ALL of the reds, pinks and oranges on the rocks have faded to white.  Even the sealed ones placed under cover (out of rain and sun) at my house have faded.  I have used a lot of sealants, and the one I used for this project has sealed other acrylic, outdoor art, and has lasted for over 2 years.  Thus I know the sealant used was not the issue.  Now an entire school is going to be disappointed when they return from summer break to see that all their beautiful art has faded.  I DO NOT recommend this product.  If only I could get my money back but it's the students' disappointment that will be tougher to bear.  :(

Sentence: It says “quick drying” the white outline had sat for at least an hour, the light green had sat for about 45 minutes.
Content: I’m not one to write many reviews and when I do, I usually write reviews because I’m so happy with the product, this time is a different story. I make custom garden decor. This specific video was me “Trying” to draw a cactus on a planter. It says “quick drying” the white outline had sat for at least an hour, the light green had sat for about 45 minutes. The light green took the white off immediately. I thought maybe I hadn’t let it sit long enough. The next green I used was 45 minutes later. It scratched the light green off almost immediately. One the other marker went over a previous color, it ruined the tip. I primed the marker a fair amount. You can see on the notepad I was priming on, it primed enough to leak out on the sides but not enough to make the tip of the marker work. Also, one came damaged. I’m hoping I can get a refund. I was so excited for these and now I’m very disappointed for spending almost $40.00 on these. Not worth it. I wouldn’t purchase again.

Used these to paint some peg dolls for my daughter. You need a base coat in brushed paint if youre painting on wood and don't want it to bleed through the grains. I also found that some of the colours didn't mix properly even after many attempts (the white of the paint got stuck in part of the pen so only an inky colour was coming out, not mixed paint).
Overall really nice finish though and easy to use. A bit expensive, and not sure whether they will dry up soon or not. But fun for projects like this!

Sentence: These pens work awesome---until the tips stop working, that is, while they are still full of paint.
Content: These pens work awesome---until the tips stop working, that is, while they are still full of paint. If you're doing a job that needs to be done all at once, like repainting the numbers on your mailbox, as I was, then either buy two sets, for insurance, or have a paint brush and wire cutters handy, so you can cut the tubes open when they stop working and brush the paint on by hand from a tuna tin. I had this problem with both yellow and gold, but not with other colors, so maybe it's a feature of these pigments in particular.

Sentence: The tips are not fraying, even on the very rough polyester I mark on.
Content: I usually use Posca or Uchida decocolor for my paint markers. These pretty much stand up to the same quality with a variable for pricing. You do have to shake these more often to keep the flow. But they do not spill over and the tips are consistent. I paint on everything and these are versatile, but more importantly, durable! The tips are not fraying, even on the very rough polyester I mark on. I've ruined quite a few $8 Posca markers with the material I was working on. So that is a big selling point. The pigment is vibrant and consistent with label, top, and the Amazon picture. Does require a few layers for vibrancy on black surfaces, but I easily got it to make my design pop. In working that way, I am able to build a gradient with less variant markers. I WILL DEFINITELY be ordering for a full collection. So glad to find a paint marker that works at a professional artist level with a starving artist price.

And even if all instructions followed properly).

Sentence: They can draw on a lot of surfaces, there super fun to use, and they dry pretty quickly but leave just enough time if you wanna purposefully smudge the colors together.
Content: These Markers or Pens are absolutely amazing, they’re just like I imagined, I absolutely love them. They can draw on a lot of surfaces, there super fun to use, and they dry pretty quickly but leave just enough time if you wanna purposefully smudge the colors together. They are pretty durable but if you do come into an issue with the nib wearing or the paint dried, you just need to reverse the nib by taking it out and flipping. Caution, be super careful when you do this, make sure the pen is facing upwards so that the pain doesn’t drip out. I do recommend a good strong paper if that’s what you’re using them for. Preferably the less textured the better, as well as the thicker the better.How to use:Apparently there’s a whole lot of misconceptions about how to use these. I didn’t know until I read the comments before buying. They are going to come dry.1. Shake the pen while it’s closed (unless you wanna sprinkle of paint)2. Open the pen and push the pen nib up and down on the edge of paper or scrap paper until the paint reaches the end of the nib or until the pen flows well when drawing.3. Repeat if necessaryIf you do step 1, 2, 1 but with the cap open you can get nice stars on your work.DO NOT push the nib down/press to hard when drawing. If you press to hard you might wear down the tip. But my biggest concern is people saying that these pens leak, they do not leak, but they will if you draw so hard that the nib goes all the way down.Heads up:Don’t worry if the individual markers don’t come wrapped in the plastic like  they used to, I’ve heard that they are no longer doing that. Also if you get markers and some are in a different language, it’s ok. I’m not sure why you would get them that way but these markers originally are from Japan. For those of you who don’t know a lot about art supplies, I guarantee that any art supplies you buy that’s actually Japanese is probably the best art supplies there is.  Mine came without the plastic wrapping around the marker but did all come in English.

Sentence: When I purchased these, it worked out to be about $2.02 per marker, which is a good $1.50 cheaper than most other sellers and stores price POSCAs at.I received 29 unique colors: a box of the 15 standard range colors, a box of the 7 pastel/natural range colors, and 7 individually sealed markers comprising the five colors in the dark range and the two select metallic colors.The PS-5C is a good nib size for filling in broader areas, lettering, and sticker-size work.
Content: When I purchased these, it worked out to be about $2.02 per marker, which is a good $1.50 cheaper than most other sellers and stores price POSCAs at.I received 29 unique colors: a box of the 15 standard range colors, a box of the 7 pastel/natural range colors, and 7 individually sealed markers comprising the five colors in the dark range and the two select metallic colors.The PS-5C is a good nib size for filling in broader areas, lettering, and sticker-size work. You won't be able to achieve too much fine detail with these; however, I think they are a very good "starter" set that you can supplement with 3Cs or 1Cs as needed.The markers themselves worked beautifully and as expected. All have fresh white nibs and show no sign of previous use. I didn't have any issues with the markers seeming dried out or spilling blobs all over the page. I primed my markers as follows: (1) uncap upright marker and depress nib with finger, (2) shake upright for 30 s, (3) gently depress nib on paper about 30 times until ink filters into and saturates nib.I definitely will be purchasing future sets from here as the price is unbeatable and the quality is equal to those bought at any fine art store. They are Japan imports, so the marker barrel is written in Japanese, but considering that many other fine art brands are Japan imports branded in Japanese, I don't see this as an issue. For me, it matches the rest of my supplies.

Sentence: That is, if you push the tip down on a piece of paper it will go into the marker and you will start to see the paint flow onto the tip.
Content:
Even though I don't mind not having a nice box or packaging for these paint markers, I was very disappointed to see all 29 of them thrown together in a bag that was ripped down the side inside of its amazon packaging. Were they not individually sealed, I would have thought I'd been sold a used item. So be sure your markers come in better packaging or are individually wrapped.

Secondly, I was worried as a first-time user because when I first used opened one of the markers the tip was white and dry. I shook and shook the marker and could not for the life of me get color to come out until I googled how to prep the marker correctly as the item did not come with instructions (I'm sure they say on the markers, but they're in Japanese which I cannot read- I understand this is partly on me for ordering an item from a foreign company, but with their rising popularity they really should have instructions in other languages as well if on nothing else but the listing). However, I was able to find directions on their official website as mentioned, so I digress.

To get your markers to work, you must shake them (you will hear a noise, this is normal) and then "pump" the marker a few times. That is, if you push the tip down on a piece of paper it will go into the marker and you will start to see the paint flow onto the tip. The website said to pump one or two times but I find I need to pump it for much more than that, but maybe each marker is different. This is easy enough to do and I don't mind the prepping at all, I just wish I knew this beforehand so I didn't almost lose my mind thinking I was sold defective markers.

The colors are very bright and pop well, even with pastels. They cover pencil or even ink fairly well with just one coat. Being as bright as they are they might not work for every project, but I bought them because of that uniqueness. I have not used them much but I have noticed the tip will flake a bit when covering large areas which is annoying, so I wish they'd used a different material but I'm not an expert on other options so maybe this was the best they could do.

Overall, they're expensive as art supplies tend to be, but they're a solid brand with a good reputation. I just probably wouldn't buy them from amazon again due to the poor packaging and instructions. Hopefully they last me a while and don't dry out.

Sentence: Just prime the paper with a layer of white acrylic/house paint and then use the pens on top of that to prevent pilling.
Content: I'm a painter (primarily acrylic) and I kept seeing my fellow artists posting pics bragging about Posca pens. I decided to give em a go and well.... They're kinda lack-luster. I've worked with other acrylic paint pens that are a fraction of the cost and just as good. The lighter colors aren't very opaque but I am impressed by the opacity of the darker colors. But, honestly, you're better off doing more research and investing in a different acrylic pen set or just reg acrylic paint.Also, I've heard a lot of people have issues using these on paper (even heavy-weight watercolor paper). Just prime the paper with a layer of white acrylic/house paint and then use the pens on top of that to prevent pilling.

Sentence: This set came well packaged, each marker individually wrapped - the issues began when I started using them.
Content: I love Poscas and have enjoyed using them for years.  This set came well packaged, each marker individually wrapped - the issues began when I started using them.  Normally, the bullet nibs aren’t loose, and the nib needs to be fully compressed multiple times to saturate with paint.  With these, however, the nibs slid out pretty easily and there is an audible hissing sound when the nib is compressed.  Then paint just pours out.  I’ve tried to make it work, since if the nib isn’t pressed too hard it’s fine, but if I press just a little too hard, out pours the paint, ruining my work.  This seems like a quality control issue on the part of the manufacturer but it is very frustrating.  I am a paint marker aficionado and have used many types, and this is the first time I’ve ever had issues with Poscas.  Bad batch perhaps?

Sentence: I received all 29 markers, all different colors like intended.A few people said these were dried out/used when they received them, but I'm not sure that's truly the case?
Content: One of my friends introduced me to using Poscas and I've greatly enjoyed them, so I decided to get some of my own to mess around with. This seemed like a great pack so I thought I'd grab it.I read some of the reviews, especially the bad ones, and I did have some worries about getting them from Amazon, but these are legitimate Posca markers. I received all 29 markers, all different colors like intended.A few people said these were dried out/used when they received them, but I'm not sure that's truly the case? If the nibs are white, they haven't been used at all, and I discovered they sometimes do take a little work to get the paint flowing.Also don't be an idiot and shake them with the cap off, that can cause paint splatter everywhere (I remembered the reviews with that and laughed, do none of you have common sense?).Anywho, when you're first "activating" them, you gotta shake them a bit while upside down, press the nib down against paper a few times, and shake a bit more, rinse and repeat until paint is saturating the nib. It doesn't work perfectly each time, sometimes takes a little extra work, but once they're working they are excellent! I tested all of mine and made sure they were working.The tips for the 5M markers are removable/reversable for cleaning/rinsing apparently, although the box does not give instructions nor mentions this (the USA Posca site DOES mention this, though, but they also have no instructions there either... I imagine it's just as simple as pulling the nib out, cleaning it, then slotting it back in? Unsure but I will test it later).I would highly recommend reading the FAQ on the Posca site if you have any curiosities about anything regarding the markers otherwise.

Sentence: The Posca Markers I received were old and mostly dried out.
Content: The Posca Markers I received were old and mostly dried out. I didn't return them because I needed them for a project, but their overall life expectancy is anticipated to be very low (if I didn't look up how to fix the issue), as the paint flow is pitiful and the nibs are brittle.The Fix - If you don't feel like reading, search on YouTube for "How To Refill or Recycle Posca Paint Pens." I took a pair of plyers and opened each marker by taking the cap off and screwing the top clockwise (in the opposite direction that you would expect to turn to open it), removing the clear plastic piece, and filling the marker with water. Once that was done I put the marker back together, screwed the top back on, put the cap on, and shook vigorously to break up and reconstitute the dried paint, and it worked!However, this was a long and messy process, and no one should have to pay money for an item they expect to work as advertised, and I didn't find this fix until after I finished my project. The amount of trust I have with Amazon and its sellers have dwindled to non-existent, not just with art supplies, but throughout all departments. Personally, I'm sticking with either ordering from Blick, or finding a 40% off coupon and heading to Michaels for now on because the two day shipping just isn't enough for me to want to put up with this crap anymore.

I took a pair of plyers and opened each marker by taking the cap off and screwing the top clockwise (in the opposite direction that you would expect to turn to open it), removing the clear plastic piece, and filling the marker with water. Once that was done I put the marker back together, screwed the top back on, put the cap on, and shook vigorously to break up and reconstitute the dried paint, and it worked!However, this was a long and messy process, and no one should have to pay money for an item they expect to work as advertised, and I didn't find this fix until after I finished my project. The amount of trust I have with Amazon and its sellers have dwindled to non-existent, not just with art supplies, but throughout all departments. Personally, I'm sticking with either ordering from Blick, or finding a 40% off coupon and heading to Michaels for now on because the two day shipping just isn't enough for me to want to put up with this crap anymore.

Sentence: These aren’t just markers—they’re a creative revolution in a box!
Content: If you’re an artist, crafter, or just someone who loves to add a splash of color to life, the **24 Posca Paint Markers** are about to become your new best friends. These aren’t just markers—they’re a creative revolution in a box! Whether you’re doodling on fabric, sketching on canvas, or turning your sneakers into wearable art, these acrylic paint pens are here to make your imagination run wild.### **What’s in the Box?**First off, let’s talk about the sheer joy of unboxing this set. You get **24 vibrant colors** that cover every shade you could possibly need. From bold primaries to soft pastels, this collection is like a rainbow in marker form. Each pen features **reversible tips** (3M fine and broad), so you can switch between precision detailing and bold, sweeping strokes with ease. It’s like having two markers in one—genius!### **Why Posca Markers Are a Game-Changer**1. **Versatility on Steroids**: These markers work on *everything*. Paper? Check. Fabric? Check. Glass, wood, metal, plastic, rocks, even your old denim jacket? Triple check! They’re like the Swiss Army knife of art supplies.2. **Acrylic Paint That Pops**: The pigment is rich, opaque, and vibrant. No more streaky, watery mess—just smooth, consistent color that dries quickly and stays put. Plus, it’s water-based and non-toxic, so you can create without worrying about fumes or mess.3. **Reversible Tips for the Win**: The fine tip is perfect for intricate details (think: tiny flowers, lettering, or shading), while the broad tip is ideal for filling in larger areas or making bold statements. Switching between them is as easy as a click.4. **Long-Lasting and Reliable**: These markers don’t dry out easily, even if you forget to cap them (we’ve all been there). The paint flows smoothly, and the nibs are durable, so you won’t have to worry about fraying or clogging.### **Fun Ways to Use Posca Markers**- **Customize Everything**: Turn plain tote bags into statement pieces, personalize mugs, or jazz up your phone case. The possibilities are endless!- **Rock Painting**: Yes, it’s a thing, and Posca markers are perfect for it. Create little masterpieces to hide around your neighborhood or use as paperweights.- **Fabric Art**: These markers are fabric-friendly, so you can design your own T-shirts, shoes, or even curtains. Just heat-set your design, and it’s washable!- **Mixed Media Magic**: Combine them with other art supplies like watercolors, pastels, or ink for stunning mixed-media projects.### **The Downsides?**Honestly, there aren’t many. The only “issue” is that once you start using these, you’ll want to buy more colors. It’s addictive. Also, if you’re heavy-handed, you might go through the paint faster, but that’s just a sign of how much fun you’re having.### **Final Verdict**The **24 Posca Paint Markers** are worth every penny. They’re high-quality, versatile, and downright fun to use. Whether you’re a professional artist or a weekend DIY enthusiast, these markers will elevate your creativity to new heights. Plus, they make an amazing gift for anyone who loves art (or needs a little push to unleash their inner Picasso).So, what are you waiting for? Grab this set, unleash your creativity, and let the world see what you can do with a little Posca magic. Trust me, your art supplies collection will thank you! 🎨✨Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5 stars)**Posca Markers: Because life’s waaay too short for boring art.

Sentence: Posca markers tend to leak more than other professional quality paint markers, such as MOLOTOW or Krink.
Content: I have used Posca Paint Markers for years and I am still a fan, but I feel like the formula has changed and the quality is not as high as it used to be. That being said, these are still pretty good and they are a good value choice. Posca markers tend to leak more than other professional quality paint markers, such as MOLOTOW or Krink. They also dry out more quickly than more expensive brands. Several colors are specifically frustrating; the blues will run if sprayed with a sealant (this was not the case a few years ago) and the oranges and pinks require several coats to fully cover the surface, as they are somewhat translucent. The colors are bright in general but some colors are dull and can appear muddy compared to other brands. These will stick to most surfaces and are pretty permanent. The variety of shades for the price make these a good starter set. I recommend only shaking the markers downward 2-3 times before pumping the paint. If used on paper surfaces, the marker tips can easily get ruined and the tips will not be as crisp so that can lead to uneven line thickness. These used to be much more expensive, and the packaging reflects the affordability of the current product line.

Sentence: Warning: you can and will poke through the foam core board with the fine tip pens, so be sure you're doing this on a surface that you don't care about - otherwise, it'll end up looking like it has the measles once you're done.You've probably read other reviews that say on certain pens you can pull the tips out and turn them around if they become frayed.
Content: So I gave in and decided to try acrylic paint pens because I couldn't locate the huge plastic tub of brand new, never opened bottles of acrylic paint. The tub is somewhere in my craft studio, and that place is like a snake pit - I can't find anything! ANYway, I ordered three different sets of Posca Paint Pens - the 0.7 mm extra-fine pen tips and the 1.8/2.5mm medium bullet tip pens., as well as the black and white variety pack (sizes range from 0.7 to 8mm chisel tip to 15mm big mama jama).Takes a bit to get all the wrappers off. Then you need to 'burp' the tip (hold the pen with the tip pointing up, and with your thumb, press down to get rid of the air that's settled between the inner paint skin and the new felt/plastic tip inside where you can't see it). While burping is fun, this is tedious. And can leave you with bruised thumb tips. Yeah. It's a thing.Once they've been burped, the real non-fun part begins: you gotta prime them. You can shake, shake, shake senora, shake it all around, but you should have a piece of notebook paper or old foam core (I used foam core) so that once you've shaken the snot out of them, you can press down on the paper a few dozen times to coax the paint into the tip. Warning: you can and will poke through the foam core board with the fine tip pens, so be sure you're doing this on a surface that you don't care about - otherwise, it'll end up looking like it has the measles once you're done.You've probably read other reviews that say on certain pens you can pull the tips out and turn them around if they become frayed. I saw the same reviews. And I remember thinking, oh great - I'm gonna spend this kind of money on paint pens that aren't gonna last very long at all before I gotta swap the tips, and then have to get more pens sooner than later. Well, lemme tell ya, I've had these for over 2 months, with daily heavy use, and I've only got one tip that I should probably flip but haven't because I can still use it for larger coverage areas. So, don't freak out. They'll last a good long while.One bit of advice I learned was, don't push the pens away from you when drawing/filling/lining with them. The pens want to flow, and they will if you remember to pull them towards you, and pull them gently. Sure, rocks (in my case) have uneven surfaces and textures, but taking it a bit slower when it comes to outlining with a fine tip pen, you'll discover your pen doesn't skip or leave little eyelash-length splats or flecks.Another pointer is, if you're lettering with these pens and you make a mistake/paint blobs out, if you keep a few clean Q-tips/cotton swabs nearby, you can pop one into your mouth to get it a little moist, and swipe away the problem.The very cool thing about Posca Paint Pens is that, once they dry (and they dry very fast! bonus!) you can go right in with another color and have that color show up bright and clear. The pigment is thick and unless you're trying to make white stripes on a solid dark background, one coat will suffice.You *can* blend with the Poscas. Not very well, because they dry so fast. BUT! You CAN put enough paint down by allowing it to puddle/pool a bit with your first color, then come in with the second/lighter shade and swirl/blend to your desired shade. Don't worry if you get color on your pen tip. It'll come right off after a few squigglies on a scrap piece of paper. Do some curly-cues and once the other paint is visually off the tip, press down to get the pen's paint color to come back to the surface. Voila!Read around on other reviews to see how to get dried Posca Paint Pen residue off your clothes. It will come off finished furniture with a little elbow grease and WD-40; unfinished furniture, not so much. This stuff soaks right in and it's impossible to get out - so you might as well just paint the whole tabletop since you've already got your paint out!Hope this was helpful. The Poscas are expensive, but you're getting a high quality product. The writing on the pen's labels is minuscule and in Japanese, and while you're thinking hey, I can keep these in their cute little crayon type upright box, nah forget that noise. Just dump'em in a small plastic container, throw in a few Q-tips and maybe what's left of an old notebook you've had lying around, and then tote the whole thing to your favorite chair, break out the (clean) rocks and start painting!

Sentence: There is a small learning curve as you get finer tips as they will skip.

It’s a hassle to return the bad ones or have them clog/make a mess/ have the colors be way off/ run out after only a few uses.Posca’s are teriffic. These are not the plastic ones. The caps are true to the ink color (hooray!). There are a LOT of sets on Amazon. Go with the ones with recognizable names in art. This set  of 24 has just about every color you’d want (I wish it had apple green but I can get one separately). Only complaint is that the silver flooded on first use. Not shocked. I’ll clean it up and know to be careful with it. Feel free to ask questions! Hope this helps.

Sentence: They could be scraped off, but I didn’t spray with a protectant.All the colors cover well.
Content: I’ve used Posca pens on wood, vinyl, rocks, and paper. On wood, over a good primer coat of Zinnser, they held up extremely well. They were unfaded and didn’t peel or flake after a year of exposure to the elements, including heat, rain, and light sun exposure. (For comparison, bottled acrylic paint applied at the same time did fade.)They were also great and time-saving for adding details on a 3’ x 6’ painting.On medium-weight and up paper, they’re good.They stick great to cleaned rocks, but choose rocks that are as smooth as possible and work gently. I had a tiny bit of texture on my rock, and it made the tip of my pen fuzzy.On a soft leather-textured vinyl iPad cover, they stuck well and didn’t rub off. They could be scraped off, but I didn’t spray with a protectant.All the colors cover well. The white (as typical of almost all white paint) takes multiple passes to cover. The black is silky and opaque on the first pass.There are lower-priced paint pens, but Posca are still the best if you want professional-looking, long-lasting results.

Sentence: Given, they are expensive and I don't think they quite match their price but they work so well.
Content: I purchased these a lil while back and now I am in love with them. Given, they are expensive and I don't think they quite match their price but they work so well. The colors can go on top of each other and layer without seeing the color underneath but keep in mind when layering, the former coat has to be dried so it takes so patience to use these. I recommend the regular/medium size if you work on copy paper sized paper or smaller. Sometimes you have to keep shaking them if you haven't used them in a while because if not, the color will not come out opaque. These can be used on paper but it is not the best surface for it as the nibs are hard and VERY often tear up the paper underneath and leave little paper beads. Overall, you have to have a light hand when using this if you draw on paper. But if you use them correctly, you'll become so happy with your results. These are for thicker paper definitely.

Sentence: It was fun and easy to use since I am more familiar with pens when it comes to drawing.
Content:
I used to experiment with lots of different types of art mediums in the past and one of them were acrylics markers. It was fun and easy to use since I am more familiar with pens when it comes to drawing. However, the old markers I had purchased wouldn't always fill in the area I colored, and sometimes rubbed off the previous layer.

Fast forward to today. I have seen lots of instagramers playing with posca pens and they piqued my interest, but not enough to begin to even invest in them. I kept remembering my past experiences and I remember more cons than pros to them so I strayed far away from them thinking it was not worth the investment. My friend happened to buy some posca pens because of the hype. I saw her drawings in real life and found it so shocking. The pens, even though they were extra fine, did not leave any scratches nor did the nibs rub off. It really made me want to try them so I thought, why the heck not. If I didn't like them then I could give it to my nieces to play with. I am soooooo glad I finally gave these pens a try after sooooo much time eyeing them. Everything I felt peeved about my old acrylic markers have been solved with this brand and I couldn't be any happier. I started using them on grided notebook paper so that it would be more obvious that I was using the posca pens then just some ordinary marker (like copics or something). I especially love them because they have a limited color range. I was a lil skeptical about it at first but definitely appreciate it now. I always use the same colors over and over again with other mediums so my artworks would always look the same, but since posca pens only have a few colors (or at least the ones I bought) it pushed me out of my comfort zone and choose colors that I would normally never put together into a piece, and as a result, actually liking it (rare for me to like my own drawings). So yes, I do really think they are worth the purchase.

P.S I also like to draw Link from Legend of Zelda a LOT.

Sentence: The outer part of the marker is made of a sturdy plastic material, which feels very solid and is comfortable to hold.
Content: I have been looking at Posca Paint Markers for a long time and finally purchased the 21 Extra Fine (1mm) and the 29 Medium (5mm) Tip sets. I use them on Polymer Clay pieces. The variety of colors is a real plus. The paint does adhere to the clay very well. The outer part of the marker is made of a sturdy plastic material, which feels very solid and is comfortable to hold. The one thing I wasn’t expecting was the need to go over the colored areas several times to get a solid, opaque covering. Once I baked the clay with the colors on the surface, the colors remained vivid and bright coming out of the oven. I did use UV resin to seal the colors and protect them. There are so many things I can use these paint markers for to embellish the pieces I make. The Markers are easy to get started and use. I am very pleased with them and will continue to have fun using them on my polymer clay pieces- they’re great!! The one thing that prevented me from buying these markers in the past is the price. I really do think they are too expensive and the price needs to be reduced. Hence the 4 Stars. Yes, I finally did get an opaque finish but it took multiple applications (4-5 coats) to get there. If it took just one or two coats, I wouldn’t be so concerned about the cost.

Sentence: There's a good range of colors and they're all pretty opaque.
Content:
Overall, I'm pretty impressed with these paint pens. There's a good range of colors and they're all pretty opaque. I haven't tried other surfaces but they layer pretty nicely on mixed media paper with little to no warping. As shown in the pictures, I compared the black paint pen to a Sharpie and a Bic marker in terms of ghosting, and then paint pen did the best (while the Bic marker did the worst).

My one gripe would be the excessively wasteful packaging. There were two boxes included (as well as the silver and gold pens, totaling to 21 pens) and in one of the boxes, each pen was individually wrapped. This seems completely unnecessary as the pen caps are hard to accidentally take off and for the color to leak, the pen would have to be pumped sans cap (within the box) multiple times forcefully, which seems unlikely to happen during transit. What's strange is that the pens weren't individually wrapped in the other box... In the future, I hope they'll switch to cardboard boxes and stop with the shrink wrapping.

Sentence:
That wasn't a big deal, there are enough colors that I won't miss the ones missing, and will use the substituted colors.

It took a while to figure out which colors I actually had because the writing on the packaging and on the pens is all in Japanese.
Content:
I have heard so many good things about Posca Pens, I decided to get some. I ordered a combined set that totaled 21 pens.

The first thing I didn't expect was that they were all individually shrink wrapped. Each pen. Whew, that took some time to get them all out of the wrapping.

The second thing I wasn't expecting is that you need to prime them the first time you use each pen. The first one just flooded out onto my paper. Don't shake more than a few times and then press the tip on the paper gently! You'll still have a small amount of paint come out, but not gushing. Don't prime on your work surface, prime on an extra sheet of paper. Otherwise you'll have a small puddle of paint on your work.

The next thing is that, although I did receive all 21 pens, I didn't get two of the colors that were listed, instead got two other colors in their place. Peach and Yellow Green were not included, instead I received Pink and Aqua Blue. That wasn't a big deal, there are enough colors that I won't miss the ones missing, and will use the substituted colors.

It took a while to figure out which colors I actually had because the writing on the packaging and on the pens is all in Japanese. I've seen some that are in English, and if I did this again, I'd definitely make sure I got pens with English. Since the colors aren't readable for me on the pens, I numbered each pen lid and made a chart in my sketchbook of the colors and numbers.

When I created this chart, I found that they pill up on textured watercolor paper. This was noted in other reviews I read, so I wasn't surprised.

All in all, now that I've primed all the pens and made my chart of colors and figured out what paper to use, I'm ready to go and think I will enjoy these pens. :) They really are a good price!

Sentence: They also spit and sputter leaving tiny dots all over your art, which means I have to toss an expensive rock each time!
Content:
Wow, what a let down! I expected true micro fine tips, but these are like a Sharpie medium marker tip! I wanted for outlining and lettering only, but these are more for filling in larger spaces! Their bigger tips must be huge!!! They also spit and sputter leaving tiny dots all over your art, which means I have to toss an expensive rock each time! I use Santorini rocks to paint on, and I don't paint or prime the background because I love the stone itself so much! So when s paint pen spits you can't get it all cleaned up nice. You shouldn't have this issue to begin with.
Also I thought my arm was going to fall off by the time the pens started flowing and I had paint! My arm hurt for days from priming! And lastly, some of them the paint flows out more heavily than others, not even or anything you can depend on. Lastly, a couple of the pens the paint came out around the outside of the tips too, glowing freely and making a royal mess!

Sorry but for any experienced artist that puts out quality work, stick with the Posca pens! I'm done trying these cheaper brands, and will only use Posca from now on!

I wouldn't even recommend for beginners. They will get too discouraged when these pens mess up their work! They try do hard and certainly don't need to use low quality mediums!

Happy painting to all you wonderful artists!!!

The couple of times I tried to use and the tip seemed clogged, I just pull the nib out and submerge it in water, rubbing at it a bit to clean it.  Pop it back in the pen and scribble a bit to get the water out and the ink running through it again, and works perfectly again.  I like these so well, i've purchased 2 more sets.  I wouldn't mind eventually owning them all!

Sentence: I already had a couple of random paint pens from 'the other guys' I'd used to sketch with and lay down outlines, but they weren't amazing and they were hard to use.
Content: Guys these pens are amazing! I'm an artist who hates to paint. I know that's a contradiction, but it's true. I love to draw though! I was struggling to get some paintings finished (I got bored with them) when I thought I'd try paint pens - a combination of painting and drawing, right? With crossed fingers I bought these after doing some research. I already had a couple of random paint pens from 'the other guys' I'd used to sketch with and lay down outlines, but they weren't amazing and they were hard to use. However when I tried the Tooli pens I was really impressed! First of all the tips (I got all Xtra Fine) are very nice, firm, pointy, can get good detail. Very responsive. Love that they send extras! The ink flows smoothly and isn't blotchy or blobby at all (at least not yet, we will see after I use them for a while.) But what really blew me away was the colors. The black is REALLY BLACK! The 'other guys' black is about the same level as the Tooli dark gray! I mean this is super India Ink color black, really beautiful. Other colors are vivid and stay wet just long enough that you can bring in another color and blend quite well. Note that if you puddle two different colors together they will instantly combine, kind of like water colors. Be prepared for that quick bleed. I recommend these to artists who want to doodle on canvas; works great!!

Sentence: But I'm always looking for more colors, so I couldn't resist trying this big, affordable set.First off, EVERY SINGLE pen is individually sealed in plastic, so unboxing is quite a production, lol.
Content: I use Posca paint pens to add highlights on top of drawings done with Copic and Prismacolor markers. For this purpose, I prefer a matte finish (to integrate with the marker sections, and to scan/photograph better) so I've been sticking with Posca, which is a matte poster paint, and avoiding acrylics, which typically dry shinier. But I'm always looking for more colors, so I couldn't resist trying this big, affordable set.First off, EVERY SINGLE pen is individually sealed in plastic, so unboxing is quite a production, lol. I used one of those little box opener blades (one of these guys https://www.amazon.com/dp/B003JBKXRW/) to quickly pierce the plastic at one of the ventilation holes on the cap and managed to open them all at a good rate.Anyway, the paint flows well out of the pens. Blending ability is minimal, as painting on a still-wet section tends to just gunk up the tips—so it's good that there's such a good selection of colors to start from. The paints dry to a satin sheen—not as matte as poster colors, but the sheen is quite subtle. The browns are matte, though.Being acrylic paints, they are also waterproof when they dry. And they are very opaque, so they'd be great for layering.

Sentence: You can see the bleed through on the other side of the paper.
Content:
On the video I uploaded I had only used the markers to draw the snowflakes (I used watercolor markers to write “January”). You can see the bleed through on the other side of the paper. This was 160gsm paper which can withstand watercolor markers and ink with no bleed through.

Viscosity was not consistent. Meaning some markers were watery. Blending was hard, markers would dry to fast and then I would get the clumping. I used these markers on 4 different papers, I had the best results with bee creative marker paper, but still had clumpy blending.

The 1st day I used these markers I had better results than the very next day. On the 1st day I followed all the directions on the back of the box before using markers: shook, aired out, primed, washed nibs after use. The second day I shook again, some markers were still watery. I aired them out and they were still watery. I also now found that the markers were harder to blend, even on the better bee creative paper.

Maybe I will try playing with them some more, I do want them to work, but I don’t want them to frustrate me.

Sentence: I live in a dry climate, at 8200 feet in Vail, CO, and assume that my altitude and dryness impacts the flow and longevity of the markers.
Content: I am struggling with these markers, as they create a pool and bubbles when I initially engage the color, and subsequent attempts create more bubbles, and minimal access to color.  I bought Extra Fine and Medium Point for my pre-stamped ceramic tiles.  I live in a dry climate, at 8200 feet in Vail, CO, and assume that my altitude and dryness impacts the flow and longevity of the markers. I use them as directed, and each initial  flow is a big, bubbly puddle. I don’t want to waste the color, so I use a brush, and hurry to use it before it dries. I wanted the convenience of a marker! There is very little color available after about 3-4 sessions, and  consistency of the colors is variable. The positive is how well the color holds up when it is baked on the tiles.

Sentence: Several of the pens were dried out to start.
Content: Several of the pens were dried out to start.  I was hoping to get a product that would enable me to make fine lines (even along a straight edge) with acrylics.  These work okay in that regard once you get them started.  However, it is quite an effort to get these acrylic pens to deliver any pigment.  They require shaking vigorously for several minutes.  My wrist got sore on just three or four of them.  It feels like a set of 30 is going to cause me to get carpal tunnel.  A paint agitator would be helpful. Perhaps all acrylic pens are like this, but I'm not too impressed with the way they work.  I'm certainly not impressed that some of them were dried out (cakey) from the get-go. They are too expensive to be experimenting with different brands.  I think I'll look for a different solution.

Sentence: I knew that poscas were expensive and I wouldn't be able to afford them anytime soon but I also really wanted them.
Content: I got this product after using a friend of mines posca paint pens and being obsessed with them. I knew that poscas were expensive and I wouldn't be able to afford them anytime soon but I also really wanted them. I took to the internet to find a good quality lower price alternative. That's when I started seeing a lot of the tooli-art pens and reviews and tutorials. I was hesitant but excited to see the quality! And the quality is really nice! I'm not paint pen expert but I think I will really like these. On the paper I used they looked to be one coat which is really exciting and I love that you can't see any streaks! Following the directions was really easy and I think really helped me with figuring out the consistency of the pens. You really have to watch to see when the paint starts to come out of the tip because if you keep pressing down, a lot comes out at once. You can see with my swatches that 12 looks like too much came out and I think that to be user error. I expected the tips to be like the posca ones but with the extra fine tips they seemed to be a plastic tip instead. Overall i really like these and am excited to use them! Also the colors are very vibrant and lively!

Sentence: I love how affordable these are and the range of colors.
Content:
I love how affordable these are and the range of colors. The actual pigment of the paint is wonderful... once you mix them THROUGHLY. That's about where the pros end for me.

**I use these for rock painting so I can't speak to how they behave on canvas/paper. But results are probably similar**

You really do have to shake these up A LOT to get the true color and when you finally get it flowing you have to constantly stop what you are doing and pump the tip get it to flow again... the tip just dries too fast. Speaking of the tip... it's plastic (which is probably why the paint dries on it so quickly). And if you have to layer colors, no matter how careful you are or how dry the paint is, the tip scratches up the first layer. They also spit/splatter while using... even on my smoothest santorini stones...ruining your art in many cases. And some colors take much longer to dry than others and compared to other brands.

If they could improve the pen tip on these I could deal with the rest and they would likely become my favorite paint pen. As is, they really don't get used much. Sucks cuz I've spent a small fortune on all the different paint pen sets TooliArt offers.

I love how affordable these are and the range of colors. The actual pigment of the paint is wonderful... once you mix them THROUGHLY. That's about where the pros end for me.

**I use these for rock painting so I can't speak to how they behave on canvas/paper. But results are probably similar**

You really do have to shake these up A LOT to get the true color and when you finally get it flowing you have to constantly stop what you are doing and pump the tip get it to flow again... the tip just dries too fast. Speaking of the tip... it's plastic (which is probably why the paint dries on it so quickly). And if you have to layer colors, no matter how careful you are or how dry the paint is, the tip scratches up the first layer. They also spit/splatter while using... even on my smoothest santorini stones...ruining your art in many cases. And some colors take much longer to dry than others and compared to other brands.

If they could improve the pen tip on these I could deal with the rest and they would likely become my favorite paint pen. As is, they really don't get used much. Sucks cuz I've spent a small fortune on all the different paint pen sets TooliArt offers.

Sentence: I browsed for a long time before deciding on these, and many other sets seem to either: only contain extremely bright/obnoxious colors you're likely to never use, have too many metallics/neon/glow in the dark, etc.
Content:
I originally ordered these to draw/paint on canvas shoes. They work perfectly for that. What I didn't expect to find was versatility in their use on paper as well. Also, comes with 2 sets of black and white pens instead of just 1, which is really nice.

They are extremely difficult to shake up, and are a pain to get the color down from the tube and into the brush.

I am not sure if I was supposed to store these markers horizontally and not vertically? But storing them horizontally is not always practical for me. I'm thinking maybe by storing them vertically, this allowed for the paint to gather in the bottom of the pen and harden which resulted in them drying out.

When they did work, they had a really nice color and performed well. They allowed for fine detail when I colored. After shaking the pen for what seemed like 5 minutes (and the paint finally got flowing), it didn't write streaky and was well-pigmented. However, I don't think I will be buying these again.

Sentence: Smooth paint, nice, opaque coverage.
Content:
The first time you pull these out of the box they are wonderful. Smooth paint, nice, opaque coverage. Huge selection of colors… then you try to use them a second time and they are a nightmare from that point on.

These clog so, so bad. I’m writing this review because I just spent ten minutes tapping and scribbling one of these pens on a pad of post it notes to even get some paint down to the tip. Which still didn’t flow. I’ve had them for a year and I’m determined to get my moneys worth so I keep doing this every time and it is so frustrating I can’t stand it.

I contacted their support and they told me to soak the nibs(tips) in water, which a) did not work, and b) is not something I’m going to waste time on every time I want to use these pens. They also suggested I replace the nibs - which would work well if I had an endless supply of nibs I could switch out every time, but I don’t and they didn’t answer when I asked if I could purchase additional tips.

Save yourself the frustration and just buy a better brand of paint pen.

Sentence: Others have mentioned splatter.
Content: I really thought I was buying an inferior paint pen to share with the kids but the Tooli-Art pens have replaced my Posca in the studio much to my surprise. Others have mentioned splatter.  I find that is not a problem with the Tooli-Art unless you are painting on a rough rock and then any pen will splatter some. I love the points are not too thick and allow me to paint small areas as well as large.  The Tooli-Art pens mix very well and come out more opaque than the other brand I was using.  I find the Tooli pens to be more dependable when I'm near the end of my work and really don't want to mess up with a blob of paint coming out like what has happened with the other brand I used.  I have an order of a large group of rocks now that need to be done quickly and I'm taking no chances on any other brand.  I will soon be teaching a class with paint pens and I'm seriously thinking about using the Tooli-Art pens. I haven't yet tried them on anything other than rocks but will be testing them on glassware as I have had a request.  I will write another review after I try them on various other surfaces.  Update:  I did try a simple design on a mug and placed it in a cold oven, turned it on to 375 and left it for 45 mins., I then turned off the oven and left the mug in until the oven cooled and it turned out great.  I included a photo of the quickly done cat outline on a mug (this was just a test). Two of us ran our fingernail over the left hip of this line drawing and it did not scratch off!

Sentence:
Nibs are easily replaceable and washable if you hit a clog (proper storage is necessary).

The colors in the E+ pack are perfect for what I need as a sign artist and you really can't beat the price for what you get.
Content:
I've been using these to create signs for beers on tap at my bar for about 8 months or so and they are probably the best quality acrylic pens I've had my hands on.

They seem to last quite a long time and they're extremely versatile. I use them primarily on smooth wood that is coated with black chalkboard paint but I have also used them on cardboard, paper, canvas, and plastic. Have never had any issues with chipping after drying (I do not use sealant). Signs stay pretty dry, so I can't speak to how the acrylic handles an accidental splash of liquid.

The fine detail nibs are incredible and aren't easily ruined or dulled. Distribution of paint is consistent, though when it gets low you may find yourself pressing the tip more often. Nibs are easily replaceable and washable if you hit a clog (proper storage is necessary).

The colors in the E+ pack are perfect for what I need as a sign artist and you really can't beat the price for what you get. 5/5 stars by far.

Sentence: They are a waste of money.
Content: I bought this set of pens and a set of the medium tip pens for rock painting and because of the reviews. After using these for a week I have to say I wish I hadn’t. I’m not a fan at all. They are a waste of money. Over half of them leak, one is dried out with a few more on their way (Takes a lot of priming to get the paint started every time I use them and the caps are on tight ).  The colors aren’t anywhere close to what’s depicted in the pictures.  I know monitors are different. But they are muted colors. The bright (hot) pink is actually just pink, not a pastel like the other one though. I was disappointed as I was wanting a bright/hot pink.  They say these are opaque and dry quickly which I have found out this is not true.  I’ve had to wait minutes for the paint to dry and apply several coats for complete coverage. I’m going to be returning these.  Definitely not worth the time, money and hassle.

Sentence: Tried expensive white, gold, and silver pens from Blick / Hobby Lobby / Michaels and cheaper ones from Dollar Tree / Amazon.
Content: Purchased a couple of black paper sketch pads and journals to try out as travel journals. Since I wanted to (mostly) write on the pages rather than draw, the hardest part was finding writing instruments that look the way I wanted on black paper. Attached is a photo of the results of only some of the pens / colored pencils / gel pens, etc. tried. Shown are the best of all of them and I think you'll agree the examples on the left are superior to the ones on the right. (Depending, of course, what you want to do with the sketch pad.)First the not-so-good ones on the right. Tried expensive white, gold, and silver pens from Blick / Hobby Lobby / Michaels and cheaper ones from Dollar Tree / Amazon. (I now have a fairly impressive collection of pens, pencils, and markers that won't work with black paper but will hopefully be good for other projects.) The colored pencil results are very subtle and almost get lost on the page,. Not that great for writing, but they might be great if that's the look you want. FYI - a couple of different brands of gel pens did not work at all for me on black paper. You could barely see them and once they dried completely they were even harder to see. It could have been the brands I tried, so you might want to see for yourself and your individual need.Now the good - I ordered these Artistro Metallic Paint Pens (Acrylic), and they are the clear winners (shown on the left in the photo) for writing on black paper. You get 12 pens for under $16 (sale price when I purchased them) and all of them look good and pop on the black paper with one possible exception - the black/slate pen. Maybe it would be great for semi-secret messages? There are a couple more colors (rust and turquoise) in the pack that there wasn't room for on the test page, but they're nice too. Also, these pens write very smoothly - no clumps or random gooey places like most of the other paint pens tested.I would definitely recommend these pens, especially if you want to write on a dark or black paper!

I purchased these because I was blatantly ripping off a Van Gogh from memory (relax--it's just for me, I never sell my stuff, I'm happily mediocre), but wanted to outline the blossoms with black (because I'm not Van Gogh, and mine was a little blah). So, I followed the instructions, and it kind of spattered out when I removed the cap after shaking. I blotted on paper, but the first flower I outlined wasn't great (top center flower). It just plopped out even with light contact. The pen quickly evened out, and was really good to work with for the most part, but would occasionally, when encountering a little bump in the paint, spatter a tiny bit. You would have to zoom in on the photo to see the spray, but if I were a professional, I would have cried. Of course, a professional probably would have 100% brought them to room temperature first, and have done more than just give one or two presses on paper, instead of sacrificing a little more of the paint on scrap paper first. That said, I would purchase again, now that I have a learning curve.

And to the reviewer who said he loved them, but needed to use a paper towel to open after shaking...you were correct. I wish I had remembered that.

Sentence: I did some research before hand and thought with all the steps I took that it would last longer but it did not.Regardless, that's not a fault of these pens but of the fact that rubber is too flexible to be painted with acrylic paint.
Content: Bought the 42 piece "extra fine tip" set for a project and they worked beautifully! Very happy with the pen's overall performance.I drew/painted some little rubber rain boots. The boots, unfortunately, did not stay painted for long. After the first wear, the paint ended up cracking off. I did some research before hand and thought with all the steps I took that it would last longer but it did not.Regardless, that's not a fault of these pens but of the fact that rubber is too flexible to be painted with acrylic paint. Rubber bends and moves too much so that's why the paint cracked and chipped. I'm going to try these pens out with canvas slip-on shoes and see how that goes. I'll try and provide an update later on that.In the meantime, I leave a 5 star review on these. Working in layers, the colors build wonderfully, I was most impressed with the white pen as it has a very strong opacity so all I needed was 2-3 layers to get the coverage I was looking for.The paint dries to an almost matte-like finish. The tip on these pens is similar to a fine tip sharpie. It's almost like working with a sharpie but the dry time is not as quick (obviously). Maybe a minute or two for it to fully dry enough to add the next layer.Because I was working with rubber, if I made a mistake I could just use some rubbing alcohol to clean up the mistake easy-peasy without any problems. The paint did not stain the boot or anything like that.While I was drawing/painting, I did have to pump and shake the pen often for more paint to release from the chamber, but that is the case with most paint pens, and was what I expected when I bought these.I'm also happy that they give you 2 black pens and 2 white pens as those 2 colors are what I use the most for my projects.If there is one complaint that I do have, it's that there is only one red pen out of the whole set. No other shade of red is provided which meant I hade to dig out my tubes of red acrylic paints and brushes in order to get the darker shade of red you see on the rocket. It's not that big of a deal, but it's something I noticed that could be improved. There is a surplus of blues, however, so if you have a blue based project then this is the pen set for you lol.

Sentence: When working on a hard, non porous surface the first coat of paint will dry quickly and peel as you’re still applying color.
Content:
I paint rocks...

I‘ve developed a love/hate relationship with these pens. They can be great or awful depending on the surface you’re working on

The colors are fantastic and the pigment density/coverage can be very good. They take a little longer to shake/mix the other pens. If not shaken long enough the pigment doesn’t mix with its base and you’ll get a weird syrupy liquid that’s not true to its color. It usually winds up being much darker than it should be. This can create problems with inconsistencies and color that doesn’t match. So shake, shake shake and have a piece of paper handy to dab, dab dab! You’ll need to “milk” the pen to bleed off any unmixed color that collects at the nib.

The paint is shiny which I didn’t expect & might be helpful for shoppers to know. When working on a hard, non porous surface the first coat of paint will dry quickly and peel as you’re still applying color. This leads to a terrible surface texture as little bits of paint flakes pull up and mix in leaving a lumpy, bumpy, ugly designs. I was ready to toss these in the garbage til I tried them on a new type of rock I purchased...then everything changed!! On the slightly more porous rocks they were incredible!! None of the same issues existed. They created an even, densely colored coat with no flaking issues!

There’s one aspect to these pens that are superior to poscas. The nibs are harder (and maybe even smaller?) and the paint consistency slight different so you can get really thin lines and so some very precise work

It might be wise to get a smaller set of these if available to try them first and see how they do on the surface you’re planning to work with. If it’s a match then you’ll really enjoy these pens and the colors offered

I’ve attached a picture of a few of the rocks I’ve made. I mix media so keep in mind that not all the colors seen here are from the markers

UPDATE: I’ve come back to update my review after working with these pens for a good length of time. I’m loving them! I never even use my expensive Posca pens anymore. The density of color and range of colors is fantastic! The “texture” of the paint is beautiful to work with. The only draw back is the shaking/mixing of the pens. It is difficult to mix them well....it takes a good bit of shaking and “milking” before you start to paint. It’s a small gripe but it’d be easier if they mixed quicker and more thoroughly.

Originally I didn’t like the sheen of these pens since I was used to the Poscas but now I’ve come to hate the Poscas chalky finish which can create an uneven surface and clumps and looks dull in comparison. These pens make a nice even fluid coat

I’ve added a few more pictures of my newer pieces. I love what these pens can do!

Content: I am using this product so far for rock painting.  My designs are rather intricate so I really needed an extra-fine tip.  I have found that the paint doesn't come out consistently. Sentence: The paint is very pigmented and vibrant, and they're very easy to use!
Content: I bought these when they were on sale and I'm very happy with them! The paint is very pigmented and vibrant, and they're very easy to use! I like the translucent barrels that show how much paint I have left. I only have 2 major complaints that bring down the star rating from 5 to 4.1) Some of my pens have a tendency to pour out way too much ink. It's hard to get fine lines when it's pouring out and it leaves small puddles that take forever to dry and end up cracking. It can be really annoying and it feels like a complete waste of paint.2) Some of the colours on the lids and box don't match the actual paints well. 20A and 25A are nearly identical greens, 122A is a very light grey when the box implies it's nearly black, 321A is not nearly as dark of a blue as the box implies, etc.The second problem is a bit more minor, but the leaking paint is pretty annoying to work with. If you're willing to deal with that potential problem, I'd recommend these entirely because of how vibrant these are!

Sentence: Painting with a brush is tedious and time consuming, but these paint pens are efficient and easy to use.
Content: These paint pens opened up a world of possibilities! It is truly amazing how well they paint on different surfaces. The tips are very small and not good for coloring large areas (though using the tip’s side does help), but excellent for small pieces about 4” square when multiple colors are used.  The extra black was much needed for me. I found the 3-4 of shades of each cool color to be perfect, but the 1-2 shades of warm colors were not sufficient. For the cost though, these are excellent! The popular Posca pens I found online are sometimes 2-3 times the price for a similar product!  My only complaint about use is that the paint doesn’t always come out in a continuous flow- but after priming the pens again it begins flowing. Besides this, the ease of painting with these astounds me. Painting with a brush is tedious and time consuming, but these paint pens are efficient and easy to use.  Thank you Artistro for these high quality affordable paint pens!

Sentence: These paint pens are fun to use but there are a couple of things I don't like about them.
Content: I'm not sure yet how I feel about these paint pens. I am a painter and paint with oils, acrylics, watercolors and I draw with all sorts of pencils and pens. These paint pens are fun to use but there are a couple of things I don't like about them. When filling in a drawing say for example a lady's skirt, the paint doesn't fill in the area on the first try. It's because the pen tips are fine which is nice for smaller areas but not so much for larger areas. This is another issue. Filling in smaller areas, the pens flood the paper and the paint goes over the outlines of the sketch.It's similar to painting with watercolor paints. Many times the paint will seep over the sketched lines. This is fine for a watercolor painting but not for the images I am working on right now.I am creating Christmas cards and I want the paint to be nice and neat and filled in with no 'holidays'.I do like the colors and the pen nibs are nice and firm.It will take some practice I suppose to get to where I want to be with these paint pens. Like I said, they ARE fun to use.Update June 20:I need to make a correction on the red color selection. There are two reds. I accidentally mixed the darker red pen with the metallic pens. So the darker red pen is a nice shade of red but the second red pen looks like a dark pink. or lighter red which is simply dark pink.Keep your pens separate! Lol.Update June 25I discovered that if you use a dampened paint brush and brush over your pen painted area quickly, the brush will smooth out the paint and make it go further. I just did it after drawing a holly leaf with the darker green pen.Because the paint in the pens is acrylic you can brush it. Use a good brush though and be careful when painting along the lines. I'm glad I now know I can brush this paint (not being very experienced with these pens) because when using the paint pens on a large area they have a tendency to leave line marks and 'holidays'. A brush takes care of all of that. The metallic paint pens are really bad about this. They leave scratch marks, line marks and holidays and going back over the painted area just creates a mess. The pens tend to flood and this leaves weird looking spots on your picture.Unless you are experienced and skillful with a paint brush I advise you to practice on a scrap piece of paper before applying this to your finished picture.

Sentence: I found this made for uneven application.In my set of 12 colors, there was too little difference between the colors.
Content: To make the color permanent, you have to let the project dry for hours, then bake it at 400 degrees for a half hour and let it cool in the oven for another half hour. So items that melt or that are too big for the oven won’t achieve permanence. It’s nice that the instructions for getting the ink to flow are written on each marker, on the box and on an enclosed card, all with drawings to illustrate. The drawings show that you shake it not from top to bottom but like you’re shaking down an old-fashioned thermometer to remove the last reading. It would be nice if the ink color was also written on each marker. Hard to tell some of them apart. Black and brown are almost the same, and red is nearly indistinguishable from the fuscia, which has a purply pink cap. Interesting that you have to push the tip to one side to kind of burp it, before pumping the point on scrap paper until ink comes down to cover the tip and starts to pool. The instructions say to practice on scrap, then reactivate and apply to your project. When the flow gets thin, repeat the process from the thermometer shake. I found this made for uneven application.In my set of 12  colors, there was too little difference between the colors. Instead of a fuscia and red that almost match, for example, I could have used a second green. They’re ingenious little devices, though, and I plan to personalize mugs and stemware.

Sentence: The images will be dishwasher safe, but will scratch under even the most basic touch of cutlery.
Content: This product is garbage. Although it claims to leave indelible marks on your porcelain once baked, IT DOES NOT. The images will be dishwasher safe, but will scratch under even the most basic touch of cutlery. I was planning a wedding and attempting to make personalized plates for all of my guests. I made about 50 plates before I attempted to use one myself. I discovered that the paint scratches right off, and makes the plates completely unusable. I went to a paint-your-own-pottery store for advice, and was told that all such porcelain pens are garbage and result in “tragedy.” I had to ask these very kind people to use their kiln to burn off all of the work I had done, and start over with paints from their store, which they baked and glazed in the kiln for perfect results. They charged very little money for this, and it is completely effective. If you want to make permanent images on your porcelain and ceramic, do it in this way, with professional pants to be baked in a professional kiln. DO NOT BUY THESE PENS!!!!

Sentence: One of the glasses had paint that ran, the paint is thin, but if you use an appropriate amount (don’t glob it on) then it won’t run.So, it didn’t just do what it said - it helped us with our little problem.

Sentence: When they came in they reminded me of outliners from the 80's with the Metallic ink and then color but they were just metallic ink.
Content: My son got some black post it notes and we needed something to show up on them. So I bought these. When they came in they reminded me of outliners from the 80's with the Metallic ink and then color but they were just metallic ink. You have to shake them a lot and then hold the tip down to get the ink to start. All of that went fine. They are smaller in size than a standard pen and the tips kept drying out as I was writing with them so we had to get a scratch piece to push the tip down (in case of a blob of ink). I did not notice any smells like the old markers of the 80's so that was a plus. But they don't last long. He used 2 markers a few times and they sat in the drawer for 2 months. He pulled them out to use them again and they were dried up and after shaking and pushing it down a lot to get ink started it still was not smooth writing with them. I don't think their value is very good since they are a one time use

Sentence: This was a good deal, but ...
Content: This was a good deal, but ... it took quite awhile to get the paint pen to work.  I think I was pounding on the pen tip for about 10 minutes - not wanting to give up. I am very happy that it wasn't dried out before I even got to use it.  So, if you purchase this and think it won't write, I'd recommend having a little more patience and tell you to continue pressing down on the tip because the ink will (eventually) start flowing out.  Overall, I am very satisfied that I was able to write "nicely" with this paint pen.  And, I'm even happier that it came in a set ... so, I'll have more for 'future' gifts.  After I finished writing our personal message on the underside of the seat, I sprayed a clear coat over it to be sure that it wouldn't scratch off easily.

Sentence: These water-based Flymax Paint Markers are very vibrant on coated black papers and on top of lines made by alcohol-based markers (and other writing utensils)!
Content: These water-based Flymax Paint Markers are very vibrant on coated black papers and on top of lines made by alcohol-based markers (and other writing utensils)! I am extremely grateful for these markers, which are easy to control when illustrating small artwork. They work exactly as described when the directions on the back of the box are followed! I have added extra details to the box directions to help with anyone having trouble, especially when the pen is being used for the first time:1. Leave the pen cap on and shake the pen several times prior to using.2. Uncap, and press down on the pen tip (onto some paper) with enough force to push the tip inside of the pen. Release pressure to let the tip back out. Please do this several times to encourage the white ink to come out until the white ink flows when you write with the tip.3. Recap the pen tightly after using.If you are using a thicker substrate to write with (like ballpoint pen ink, which is actually a paste made by dissolving dye in solvent), the white Paint Marker water-based ink might sink through the thick ink a bit and show some of the color underneath. If you are drawing on top of alcohol-based markers or watercolors, the white Paint Marker may show up better since markers and diluted paints usually sink deeply into textured paper and don't leave a thick substrate on top of the paper. Happy drawing/writing/decorating! :D

Content: These water-based Flymax Paint Markers are very vibrant on coated black papers and on top of lines made by alcohol-based markers (and other writing utensils)! I am extremely grateful for these markers, which are easy to control when illustrating small artwork. They work exactly as described when the directions on the back of the box are followed! I have added extra details to the box directions to help with anyone having trouble, especially when the pen is being used for the first time:1. Leave the pen cap on and shake the pen several times prior to using.2. Uncap, and press down on the pen tip (onto some paper) with enough force to push the tip inside of the pen. Release pressure to let the tip back out. Please do this several times to encourage the white ink to come out until the white ink flows when you write with the tip.3. Recap the pen tightly after using.If you are using a thicker substrate to write with (like ballpoint pen ink, which is actually a paste made by dissolving dye in solvent), the white Paint Marker water-based ink might sink through the thick ink a bit and show some of the color underneath. If you are drawing on top of alcohol-based markers or watercolors, the white Paint Marker may show up better since markers and diluted paints usually sink deeply into textured paper and don't leave a thick substrate on top of the paper. Sentence: Our various white markers had lines too thick - the main problem, were too faint, or did not work consistently - extremely frustrating.
Content: We have a group of stained glass artists who share a facility where we live, and have had difficulty finding a way to mark patterns on dark glass.  Our usual black felt tip markers just become invisible.  Our various white markers had lines too thick - the main problem, were too faint, or did not work consistently - extremely frustrating.  Often it was more than one of these issues.  But these wonderful pens solve that problem.Pros: Very nice thin line, paint flow starts quickly and stays flowing evenly - no blobs, and smears.  If it does stop, just a quick push down on the tip restarts it.  We do recommend it be stored with the tip either down or on it's side.  If used for stained glass, the lubricant from the grinder does not wash away the paint!Con: Almost none with exception that you need to give it time for the paint to dry - usually 10-15 minutes or so.  A heat gun might speed this up.  Also, for stained glass work, the grinder can start to chip off if grinding right next to the paint line.Overall the pros greatly outweigh the minor cons in our view.
