Content:
I have a side business doing mirror calligraphy, mostly for weddings. I used to buy my acrylic paint markers from Miniso which were $1 each, but for whatever reason they discontinued White a couple years ago, so I was then forced to buy either Sharpie brand (not my fave, colour is dull and clogs easily) or Posca (great pens but $7 each and have to buy at an art store).

So needless to say when I came across these I was like WHY DIDN’T I THINK TO LOOK ON AMAZON SOONER. I go through SO many pens during wedding season. The colour on these is great, nice and opaque, and they seem to last as long just as any other pens I bought.

These are really easy to remove with rubbing alcohol and paper towel.

I’m only buying this brand and the finer tipped version from now on!

Sentence: lol) Each marker is VERY FULL of water based, opaque acrylic pigment.
Content: Ok, everybody!  If you look at the customer uploaded pictures, you will see quite a few dissatisfied customers with a serious manufacturing error shown in the pics.  These bad reviewers show a marker with an entire INCH of marker nib sticking out.  When I first opened mine, I had the same thing, so I kept opening them and they were all that way. Sentence: If you're looking for a white paint marker, give these a try.These are easy to use as long as you take a look at the instructions before hand.
Content: If you're looking for a white paint marker, give these a try.These are easy to use as long as you take a look at the instructions before hand. The paint can get quite messy if you're not careful and may run. Simply shake the marker a few times, push down the tip and write.I highly suggest doing a test run to get a feel for how they work before each go as the paint will blob on the first go. Once you start writing the paint comes out easily and is bright. Once it starts to turn sheer or isn't as white, give it a shake or push the tip again--but carefully.The box says "Extra Fine Tip" but I wouldn't call these extra fine by any means. It's also listed as 0.7mm which isn't really extra fine anyway; depending on how hard you push the pen could vary. I would say the tip is closer to 1 or 2mm though. The felt tip resembles a regular marker tip, but with some finesse you can make it "Fine".Using these on cardboard, paper, and opaque washi tape worked just fine.Overall, you get a very nice assortment for a great price and should last you a while depending on it's use.

The writing width is as fine as that from the sharpie, and they don't bleed at all.  I suppose they could smear if you worked at it, but it hasn't happened yet.  You can wipe off a mistake with your finger if you do it quickly, and leave no trace, something you can't do with the sharpie. Sentence: The white acrylic paint flows smoothly from the marker, providing consistent coverage without streaks or smudges.I particularly enjoy using these markers on black paper, as the opaque white pigment stands out vividly against the dark background.
Content: The White Paint Pen Acrylic Marker set is a fantastic addition to any artist or crafter's toolkit, offering versatility and vibrant results on various surfaces, including black paper.What stands out most about these markers is their precision and brightness. Despite the potential messiness, these markers are a must-have for anyone looking to add eye-catching details and accents to their artistic creations.

I'm not sure I'll ever use them all unless I go into business renewing others' iron sight spots, but it's quite a lot cheaper to buy these than to buy new sights or take it to a gunsmith who'd probably just do a slightly fancier job of the same thing.Just follow the directions for use of these pens and have a reasonably steady hand, and you too can renew your iron sight dot markings.  They're bright, white, high visibility sights again for less money than a fast food lunch, with a bunch of pens left over.

Sentence: These water-based acrylic paint markers are a good alternative to oil-based markers.
Content: These water-based acrylic paint markers are a good alternative to oil-based markers. You’ll still have to shake them and press the tip to activate, just as you would with oil-based paint markers. The advantage over oil-based is that the paint goes on smoothly with no clumps, and the coverage is very good. These work on light or dark paper with full coverage. Colors can be layered once dry.I like to use oil-based paint markers to draw or write on plastic surfaces and was hoping these would work just as well. They’re a decent alternative but they do bead up on very slick or glossy surfaces. However, the paint will stay on once dry if it is something that won’t be handled often. But if the plastic has any tooth or texture, these work very well. The paint also beaded up a little on glass, though not as much as on the slick plastic surfaces. I tried them on metal, rocks, wood, craft foam, and fabric, all with success. They also are wonderfully and highly metallic colors, shimmering beautifully with the slightest amount of light. They are easy to manipulate to get a variety of marks and line variation. I’m happy that it’s a more kid-friendly alternative to oil-based markers (although still with supervision).

Sentence: Got these for my wife, who really enjoys art supplies.She found the colors from these markers to be disappointingly dull.
Content: Got these for my wife, who really enjoys art supplies.She found the colors from these markers to be disappointingly dull. Unlike other reviewers who have called them brilliant, she says to her most of them looked like variations of brown, especially when used on white fabric instead of paper. (See our picture, where the strip on the right is fabric.) Also, most of the markers didn’t seem very metallic, although the silver, gold and copper were sufficiently shiny.The colors beaded up a bit when used on glass, though they did dry nicely on the glass and it’s possible to go back over the spotty areas. They wash off of glass easily, so are fun for a temporary project. Because they’re not permanent on glass at all, we don’t know whether or not they’re food safe. They can certainly be good for a decorative project.We didn’t think they were great on paper. Since they contain acrylic paints and not watercolors, they require heavier paper. The tips are blunt and made of fabric with some fibers that came loose while my wife was testing the marker.All is not negative. On the plus side, they worked really well and looked great on rock (also in the picture). If you have a bunch of rocks to decorate, these markers are for you. Otherwise, we’re not recommending them.

Sentence: We've had colored pens before, but not pens that dispense this kind of metallic-shine paint.We were very pleased that the kit came with each marker individually shrink wrapped in plastic.
Content: My wife and I enjoy gift giving for holidays, birthdays and milestones and we especially enjoy making those gifts, when appropriate. We like to make our own cards. And we sometimes assemble baskets or themed gifts, which usually involves making additional cards or labels.These pens are a wonderful addition to our craft supplies. We've had colored pens before, but not pens that dispense this kind of metallic-shine paint.We were very pleased that the kit came with each marker individually shrink wrapped in plastic. We've used craft pens over many years and, even if you don't use them up on crafts and cards, they will dry out over time. So we like the fact that we can pick and choose which pens we'll open at any given time. Of course, once the shrink wrap's off, it's off. And we can't predict how long these pens will last. To do that we'd have to wait a year or so to write this review, which doesn't seem practical.Second tip: These pen tips are fairly broad, meaning they're not ideal for specialized lettering like fancy calligraphy. However, we did do some nice lettering with these pens. They're just not a finely chiseled tip that allows more elaborate effects in writing.Happy to give these 5 stars and to recommend them to others.

Sentence: I bought these for fun to use on both paper and rocks.
Content:
I bought these for fun to use on both paper and rocks. I love them! They release ink smoothly on either smooth or rough surfaces and the metallics are truly shiny without being garish or cheap looking. The colors are vibrant and saturated, but still pair well with the matte colors from other pen sets—it gives a sheen to the same colors instead of popping/taking all of the attention, which I really like!

For anyone just getting started with rock painting and not sure what size to get: I bought the 2-3mm size and it’s great for filling in larger sections while still allowing me to attempt some details, like highlights. It’s not overly wide or particularly fine; it’s a good “medium” size. Since it’s harder to control for fine details though, I would recommend also getting some fine pens (like 0.7mm) for detailed drawings, in addition to this 2-3mm size for filling in sections or backgrounds. You’d likely only need a pen wider than this 2-3mm for larger scale artwork, as this is plenty big enough for rock painting.

My only complaint about this particular set of pens is that I wish it came with a white pen too (maybe pearl or iridescent for the shine). Otherwise I’m very happy with it! Been using it for a couple of months and no clogging or drying out so far. If you’re debating between the smaller or larger set of the 2-3mm pens, get the one with more pens. It’ll be worth it to have more color options!

I recommend this set for quality but inexpensive paint pens, and plan to buy them again when my current set gets used up. They’d make a good gift, too!

Sentence: But they are such a fantastic value I can afford to buy more.
Content: I was very pleasantly surprised by these brush tip paint markers. Sometimes I want to do a little sketch painting but I don’t want to pull out my painting kit, and I had a good time using these as a substitute. There is no priming necessary (so no accidental pooling) and the paint isn’t gloopy like most paint markets. It’s very smooth and the brush works well for details. Blending the wet paint with the marker tips works beautifully too and any color contamination wipes right off. The colors are not totally opaque over black, but no worse than name brands, and I was especially happy with the opacity of white and black. Silver is totally opaque. The only downsides are that there was some unexpected color lift when I tested light colors over what I thought was dry black, and I don’t expect these pens hold a ton of paint. But they are such a fantastic value I can afford to buy more.

Sentence: It comes with a decent selection of colors and the pens are double ended with a nub and a brush head.I tried them on some junk mail when they arrived and was happy with the smooth flow of the brush head.
Content: I bought these specifically for coloring wax seals but with the dual purpose of card making calligraphy if that didn't work out. It comes with a decent selection of colors and the pens are double ended with a nub and a brush head.I tried them on some junk mail when they arrived and was happy with the smooth flow of the brush head. The white in particular stood out quite well, which is usually the most disappointing color in my experience. It takes a few seconds to dry so you have to keep that in mind.As far as using on the wax seals, it kind of worked, but not well. The paint spread and slipped across the wax and neither head was particularly effective. The brush head was a bit too thick and bled. The result is not something I would be happy gifting, so that's out the window.My second test was on card stock. This was better. I prefer the brush head and they glide well but were varying thickness. The nubs seem more consistent and offer a bolder line. My biggest complaint here is that almost every single color is flat matte. Out of the few I tested, only the gold had a metallic hue. This really depends on your needs, but for me, it's not the prettiest effect for card making. Will probably work best on rocks and maybe glass if it doesn't spread too much before drying.The other drawback is the flimsy box. Couldn't get the markers back in and you have to store these flat (horizontally) to prevent leakage. So provided I decide to keep these, I have to figure out how to store them properly. Hope this helps someone make their decision!

Sentence: Because the pens are double tipped, they should be stored horizontally so that one end doesn’t dry out.
Content: These paint pens have a brush end and dotting end.  Because the pens are double tipped, they should be stored horizontally so that one end doesn’t dry out. The paint is water-based, so it will clean up easily while it is still wet, but once it dries it will be hard to remove from surfaces and fabrics.  These are actually good for painting on fabrics because of their permanence once dry.Perfect for craft projects, for paper as well as non-porous surfaces.  These pens allow you to add details and writing that would be hard to do with a traditional paint brush.The colors are nice and opaque and give great coverage with the brush pen end.  I liked that the set comes with a mix of light, dark, and metallic colors – white, off white, and pink for dark surfaces and gold and silver particularly stand out.The dotting end provides less coverage and may need a little finessing to get the desired quantity of paint.  The dotting end has a typical pump action of the nib.  They were already full of paint and did not require priming before use.

Sentence: These pens are easy to use, ergonomic, and have a good ink flow.
Content: These pens are easy to use, ergonomic, and have a good ink flow. Unfortunately, I bought the 24 pack and didn’t look too closely at the color selection. It is severely lacking, at least for my colorful needs, with only one shade of orange and one real shade of green. On this note, some of the pens appear a different shade than their caps suggest. They are not blendable unless you work very fast or use water and an extra brush. The ink is fairly pigmented but again, there seems to be variability. Some colors took several coats where some only took one or two. Overall, great for the cost and some nice, inky pens. Happy with my purchase but I should’ve gone for the bigger pack. If you need a good variety of colors too, don’t go for the 24 pack.

Sentence: These are a great alternative to posca pens, much more affordable but very nice for the price.
Content: These are a great alternative to posca pens, much more affordable but very nice for the price. I think the drawbacks are: 1) the colors are definitely not as bright as advertised in the photos, 2) the pen nibs are very fragile and the cap design makes it fairly easy to accidentally smush/break them when recapping them, and 3) they drip/splatter a teeny bit. HOWEVER. At less than 1$/marker, these are a really nice product and are really fun to use. Lighter colors are a little sheer and these are not easy to blend, but again, for the price, these are great. Just don't expect them to perform like an expensive product. Also, the metallics are very nice and reflective, not dull or flat looking.

Sentence: Once the paint dries, it becomes waterproof, ensuring that your artwork remains vibrant and intact even when exposed to moisture.
Content: I recently had the pleasure of trying out the 24 Colors Acrylic Paint Pens, and I must say, they exceeded my expectations. These dual-tip pens are perfect for a wide range of art projects, including rock painting, ceramic decoration, woodcraft, plastic art, calligraphy, scrapbooking, brush lettering, card making, and DIY crafts.One of the standout features of these paint pens is their water resistance. Once the paint dries, it becomes waterproof, ensuring that your artwork remains vibrant and intact even when exposed to moisture. This is particularly useful for outdoor projects or items that may come into contact with water, such as painted rocks or garden decorations.I was also impressed with the pens' lack of leakage. The caps fit securely, preventing any accidental spills or messes. This is especially important when working on delicate surfaces or when traveling with the pens. I appreciate the peace of mind knowing that I can confidently carry these pens in my bag without worrying about any unwanted leaks.The flow of the paint is smooth and consistent, allowing for precise and controlled application. The medium tip is perfect for filling in larger areas or creating bold lines, while the brush tip offers more flexibility for detailed work or brush lettering. The dual-tip design provides versatility and convenience, eliminating the need for multiple pens or brushes.The size of the pens is just right, fitting comfortably in my hand and allowing for easy maneuverability. The barrels are sturdy and durable, ensuring that the pens will last through multiple projects without any issues. The vibrant and rich colors of the paint are a delight to work with, adding a pop of life to any artwork.Overall, I highly recommend the 24 Colors Acrylic Paint Pens for anyone looking for a reliable and versatile set of paint pens. Their water resistance, lack of leakage, smooth flow, and convenient dual-tip design make them a must-have for artists of all levels. Whether you're a professional artist or a hobbyist, these pens will surely elevate your art projects to the next level.

Sentence: As for the lighter colors, you do have to go through another pass after drying as the dark color of the rocks do appear to show through.
Content: My backyard has a bunch of rocks.  Every time I do my yard, I end up with at least a bucket of rocks varying in different shapes and sizes.I decided to start my own rock garden and had the opportunity to give these a try.  These come with a large variety of colors and what's great is that the tips were not getting worn on the rocks, which was great as well.  I decided to go against putting a base coat on these to save on time and was surprised that even without a base coat the color was able to still pop through.  Depending on how perfect you want your rocks, I do recommend putting a coat of base coat though.  As for the lighter colors, you do have to go through another pass after drying as the dark color of the rocks do appear to show through.  After you are done, I do recommend not skipping the clear coat though.  That will help seal in the color and even add some shine.The use is just like any other paint marker.  You shake it up a few times and then compress the tip on a piece of paper or surface to prime the tip with paint.As mentioned, no issues with the color and could see you using these to even customize stickers; however, it took forever to get here.  I think it was about a month before I got the markers.  Not sure what the hold up was, but when it was out for delivery, it didn't make it until 2 days later.  Also, because of the variety of colors, I would have wished for each color to be marked what the color was as a lot look very similar.

Sentence: It’s runnier than others I’ve used and a lot can come out at once, which means longer drying times (10+ minutes in some cases).Once fully dry, it has a nice semi-gloss finish that feels very durable.
Content: I was lucky enough to be able to test three different Funcils sets at the same time (gold, silver, and black).  Many acrylic pens require constant shaking to maintain paint flow, but these have no such issues.  They take some time to prime but, once that’s done, the paint flows very smoothly.  If anything, it may be a little too fluid for some tasks.  It’s runnier than others I’ve used and a lot can come out at once, which means longer drying times (10+ minutes in some cases).Once fully dry, it has a nice semi-gloss finish that feels very durable.  The drying characteristics often depend on the material you’re drawing on, however.  I found these worked well on watercolour paper and canvas but, when used on smooth surfaces like plastic or glass, they have a tendency to rub off.  I think they’re best suited to porous materials like fabric, canvas, wood, or stone.The different Funcils colours generally mark well on each other (please see photo...and try not to notice that I managed to write one entire section upside down).  The silver and gold stand out nicely on the black (and vice versa), but I found they don’t cover over darker colours quite so well.  They’re often streaky and need at least two coats to achieve a good opaque layer.  The semi-gloss finish might also make it harder for other paints to adhere, so these may not be the best choice for a base layer.I really liked the variety of different nibs.  The fine nibs (1 and 3 mm) are great for detail work, but the markers are so similar in size/shape that I often grab one thinking it's the other.  The 3 and 6 mm nibs are reversible (bullet and chisel tips), and the 15 mm nib has a unique flattened chisel tip with three flat surfaces.The only major concern I have is longevity.  They don’t seem prone to drying out, but I’ve only been using them for three days, so it’s hard to reach a full conclusion in that time frame.  I also worry that, since they tend to put a lot of paint out at once, they’ll run out faster than other pens.  Only time will tell in either regard.At $15.95, I think these are well-priced for the quality and variety they offer.  Most comparable sets only have one or two pen sizes, but these are well-suited to a range of applications.  The paint itself has a couple of minor issues but, from what I’ve seen so far, I’d certainly recommend them.My rating: 4.5 stars

Content: Be cautious when getting the ink to flow in the 1mm tip for the first time use. The ink just spilled out onto the paper in a big blob that ran down the paper. No issues with the 3 or 5 mm tips. But the 2 bigger nibs, the 10 and 15 mm, the ink is slow to flow into the larger tips, really slow. I was shaking the pen, attempting to get the ink to disperse fully into the nib, but instead, the ink just splattered all into the cap of the marker. Making a real big mess when I uncapped the marker. And the nib was still not fully absorbed in ink.After cleaning up the mess, I tested each marker on regular weight copy printer paper. The larger nibs are practical for posters, while the smaller nibs are good for art type projects. Surprisingly, the 3 larger nibs didn't bleed through the standard copy paper. While the 2 smaller nibs did bleed through to the backside of standard copy paper.Although I really wanted to rate 5 stars, the issue of the ink not absorbing fully into the larger nibs was a factor in one less star.

Sentence: We've used Funcil chalk markers so we were interested to try out these black acrylic markers.They have to be activated (easy enough) like most paint markers, and once that's done they can be quite juicy, especially the larger, chisel tip ones.
Content: We've used Funcil chalk markers so we were interested to try out these black acrylic markers.They have to be activated (easy enough) like most paint markers, and once that's done they can be quite juicy, especially the larger, chisel tip ones. If any of the pens start to run a bit dry then you press the nibs down on paper (or whatever surface) a few times and then they run again smoothly.Ink flow in general is good and things can get a bit messy with the larger tips, but the ink washes off your hands pretty easily.The variety of tip types (point and chisel) and sizes (1mm to 15mm) covers all bases, though you would really need to be working on larger or rougher, more porous surfaces to get the best out of (or need) the larger pens.I only tried them out on rocks and they covered the surfaces well with the ink providing a smooth and fairly glossy surface on smoother rocks. They worked well with stones and pebbles and also in covering a stone that already had a layer of acrylic paint on it. I have used the finest tipped pen of this set before (it came with a Funcil watercolour set) and I find it to be fine enough for most detailed line work. The larger pens are of less use to me, but would come into their own on larger images/surfaces and rougher material i.e. wood.Value-wise it is a good price compared with, for example, Uni Posca's etc., but only if you want all of these sizes, whereas I would prefer a set that comprised only the three smallest sizes for less money, or provided a variety of different colours.I haven't used Uni Posca or Molotow markers, but based on this performance these would seem to be decent budget options to consider. The question that remains therefore is do you need a set with all these sizes in one colour or would your needs be better met by a multi-colour set or individual pens?

Sentence: I find that they are excellent for smooth consistent ink flow and quick drying.
Content: These are the Funcils 5 Acrylic Black Paint Pen - Fine Tip, Thin Point & Jumbo Pens (1mm, 3mm, 6mm, 10mm, 15mm) - Black Paint Marker for Plastic, Canvas, Wood, Rock Painting, Fabric, Tire, Metal, Glass. I've been using these markers to do the outlines for my rock painting. I find that they are excellent for smooth consistent ink flow and quick drying. The different sizes is really handy for doing detailed work as well. The ink dries to a flat matte finish and is pretty smudge proof once it is dry. It's completely compatible with my other acrylic paints as well. Seems to be very durable and you don't get any skips or bubbling when using these pans. They stay consistently wet as long as you keep the caps on tightly. I think this is a really good deal for such good quality acrylic paint pens and the versatility is amazing. My next project will be some wine glasses for Halloween. Definitely recommend.

Ich verwende oft Acrylmarker, aktuell am liebsten die von Stabilo. Leider muss man sagen, dass die schwarzen Marker von Funcils den Vergleich total verlieren.Positiv kann ich den Preis hervorheben und die Variation an Stiftdicken und -Formen. Ich werde die Marker auch sicherlich zukünftig verwenden, allerding nur mit höchster Vorsicht oder mit Handschuhen.

Sentence: The instructions say to pump the nib 2-3 times to get the ink flowing.
Content: As with a lot of paint markers, these have strengths and weaknesses.The five pens come in a funky cardboard tube. The two largest ones are wrapped in plastic, which must be removed. All of the pens have a ball bearing mixer inside, so they have to be shaken before use. The instructions say to pump the nib 2-3 times to get the ink flowing. That's true of the smaller pens, but I found the two largest markers needed their nibs pumped quite a few times to get the ink flowing well. Once primed, all of the pens flow really well. Ink laydown is consistent and smooth.I tested the pens on paper first and found them to be really nice to use. They produce a very rich, opaque black with virtually no bleed. With the larger markers, you will notice come cockling of the paper, just as if you were using acrylic paint, so I would advise using at least 300gsm paper or card if you plan to use the chunkier markers for drawing and illustration.Using the pens on other surfaces had mixed results. On anything porous, the ink adheres well. However, on shiny or hard surfaces, I did notice some beading, and the ink adhesion wasn't great on anything glossy. It could be easily scratched off glass, plastic and metal, so if you did use the ink on those surfaces, you'd need to varnish afterwards to protect it.Given their relatively low cost, I think these are decent paint markers. If you're looking to draw on hard surfaces specifically, then you might want to look elsewhere, but if used on paper, card and porous surfaces, they perform really well and are a good buy.

Sentence: And superfast drying times - within minutes on smooth rock.
Content: My wife started rock painting before we were married. And then took off many years to start a family and focus on the home among other things. Over the past year, she has returned to the hobby.In the beginning, when she restarted, she tried acrylic paint pens with less than satisfactory results. We tried the recommended brands, but she had issues with how well the paint covered the surfaces, issues with the tips, specifically with fine detail and also failures of the pens which resulted in leaks and drips. She eventually, settled on using brushes instead of pens. But, in the back of her mind, she hadn't given up on the convenience of using the pens.Recently we came across this offering which was very economically priced and seemed to promise better performance. So, we placed our order.The set contains 24 colors. The pens are double ended which saves money buying two of each. Although we'd have to say neither is particularly sharp. So, detailed work is still an open issue.What these pens supply is really good coverage on the first coat. And superfast drying times - within minutes on smooth rock. Right now, they are new so we can't really judge if the points are going to hold up but, for now we don't have any drips or leaks.So, it seems we may have an alternative to brushes for the broader areas of a surface. But for the details it seems brushes are still her go to tool. We'll have to keep looking for the right pen.So, these are economically price pens that provide very good, first coat coverage that dries relatively quickly. The pens come in a good variety of colors and the tips seem to be holding up well so far. At least as good as anything we've seen including the tips we've seen on the more expensive brands. If you've been looking for an inexpensive brand of capable acrylic pens, you may want to consider giving these one's a try.

Over the past year, she has returned to the hobby.In the beginning, when she restarted, she tried acrylic paint pens with less than satisfactory results. We tried the recommended brands, but she had issues with how well the paint covered the surfaces, issues with the tips, specifically with fine detail and also failures of the pens which resulted in leaks and drips. She eventually, settled on using brushes instead of pens. But, in the back of her mind, she hadn't given up on the convenience of using the pens.Recently we came across this offering which was very economically priced and seemed to promise better performance. So, we placed our order.The set contains 24 colors. The pens are double ended which saves money buying two of each. Although we'd have to say neither is particularly sharp. So, detailed work is still an open issue.What these pens supply is really good coverage on the first coat. And superfast drying times - within minutes on smooth rock. Right now, they are new so we can't really judge if the points are going to hold up but, for now we don't have any drips or leaks.So, it seems we may have an alternative to brushes for the broader areas of a surface. But for the details it seems brushes are still her go to tool. We'll have to keep looking for the right pen.So, these are economically price pens that provide very good, first coat coverage that dries relatively quickly. The pens come in a good variety of colors and the tips seem to be holding up well so far. At least as good as anything we've seen including the tips we've seen on the more expensive brands. If you've been looking for an inexpensive brand of capable acrylic pens, you may want to consider giving these one's a try.

Sentence: For the most part they flowed super smooth.
Content: I wanted to make a wooden sign to go with my Audrey II plant, so I decided to try these paint pens to use to paint it with. They worked amazingly! They were easy to use; and even though the tip is sort of chunky, they were really easy to use to keep straight and even lines.The only flaw (and why I deducted a star) is that the color selection was lacking. It'd be great if this set included at least the primary colors.I think I'll order another, bigger set that has more colors available, because I'm now yearning to use these again and do another craft project. 😀My sign isn't finished yet, but I wanted to include a pic of the paints used on it. I am not one who typically does crafts and/or painting, so these pens were great to use as a beginner.

Sentence: I love the pretty, vibrant colors, though I do agree that a true red, and a true kelly green would be nice.
Content: We love paint markers in this house!  I have a lot of grandkids, and when they come over, they almost always want to do a craft project.  As you might imagine, paint markers can come in very handy for crafting.  This set of 24 markers is very nice.  I tried out the colors using both the ball-tip and paintbrush tip.  The color feeds beautifully, without any kind of priming, which is often a feature of paint markers.  I love the pretty, vibrant colors, though I do agree that a true red, and a true kelly green would be nice.  But for most purposes, the slightly off-colored green and red are just fine.  None of the grandkids have mentioned this at all, so I'm definitely quibbling.  The markers came in a flimsy cardboard box, without any kind of separation.  So if you've pulled a number of the markers out of the box at the same time, chances are excellent that the rest of them will just fall down on their sides, requiring you to shake them out of the box.  To save myself the hassle, I found a conveniently-sized plastic storage container (the disposable ones you can get at the grocery store, or dollar store), and the markers are all now happily living in there.  I like that it has a cover, too.  You do need to be careful to close the caps firmly on the markers (just like all markers), so your paint doesn't dry up.  Time will tell how durable these markers are; but at $14.99 for 24 markers (as of this writing), I won't feel badly about just replacing them when the time comes.

Sentence: I didn't have to continuously shake and press these to get a smooth, steady flow, and it was still easy to use while writing horizontally (my calendar hangs on the wall).
Content:
I've been searching for a good pen to write on my laminated calendar at work. Each of these colors show up well on both light and dark areas of the calendar. I've tried 4 other brands/styles and these have satisfied exactly what I was looking for. They also work well for me writing in my paper planner. Overall, a great office supply purchase with many uses. I wish I had purchased the larger set!

UPDATE: I BOUGHT THE LARGER SET - 136 COLORS! I am absolutely in love with all these colors and the quality of these pens. When I opened my larger set, I noticed the pens were in order: Neon, Glitter, Pastel, etc. I went to separate them, as these pens don't come with numbers to associate with a color (and I wanted to know what I was using), and was surprised to see the description on the pen itself. It's easy to mistake a classic for a neon or pastel, so I am thankful these had the designations on them. The 72-pack does not have the color type designation on the pen, so it's hard to be 100% sure what color you're using.

Probably my most favorite art supply purchase this year!

Content:
This review is for the following item: NICETY 72 Colors Acrylic Paint Pens Paint Markers, Extra Fine Tip Point Acrylic Paint Pens for Rock Painting, Canvas, Wood, Ceramic, Glass, Stone, Fabric, Scrapbooking, DIY Crafts & Art Supplies

I purchased these set of acrylic paint pens for my husbands 3d printing. He goes through a lot of pens doing highlighting to his prints. I can tell you that we will be fighting over this set.

The colors are amazing, and I can get a fine line with these pens which makes it perfect for highlighting lashes and fingernails and eyebrows on his prints.

BUT this set of colors just has me itching to start rock painting again. So hubby will have to play nice and share or another set will need to be ordered.

I do recommend this set of paint pens, they draw nicely, no stuttering, no splattering of paint. If you don't glob the paint on, they dry quickly also. I do like how the metallic colors reflect the light. Great paint pens with so many different uses.

To use the pens, make sure the cap is on tightly, shake the pen and you will hear a metal ball moving around inside. Once it seems to be moving freely, uncap the pen and push the tip down onto a flat surface. The ink will fill the tip. Now you are ready to start your painting. Have fun.

Content:
I absolutely love these colors! This my second set of acrylic paint markers after accidentally ordering a 24 ct and just loving the coverage! Naturally I wanted MORE! The metallic and the glitter are very different as far as the finish and I was happy to discover that! Just get them.

Only tip is DO NOT pump THEN shake the pen bc it might go flying. Also look at the tip while pumping it so you can see the ink fill the tip to avoid having a large spot of ink when first using each color.

The bleed through isn't too bad on just regular printer paper but I will mostly be using these in my sketchbook which has 185 gsm paper so it'll be perfect for what I want to do with it.

Second note is that on the printer paper, the markers do peel the paper a little bit. I'll have to update once it is swatched on thicker paper. I'm hoping it's just bc they were fresh out the box.

Kind of upset they aren't named or numbered but the have a swatch chart on the back of the box to identify the color groupings so I will probably keep them like that....however I do love a good rainbow so maybe not lol

Sentence: The fine tip makes it perfect for details and precise application.
Content: This was such a good find. I was worried it would be just average but they are very nice quality and opaque. The fine tip makes it perfect for details and precise application. The paint flows smoothly and the color selection is beautiful. I am an artist that has tried a few other brands including the popular (and expensive) ones and these are JUST as good quality, they have great usability. I’ve already decorated a number of things around my desk . They mix well while still wet for custom color blends, but with these many colors you’ll have everything you need. I will be trying out other sized markers from this brand when I can, for larger projects. These are skinny and sleek enough to fit into my pencil case. They work well on every surface and they dry with a slightly raised texture off the surface of whatever you’re going to draw on so I recommend grabbing some sort of acrylic finishing seal coat. I use mod podge’s iridescent shimmer acrylic sealer and regular glossy sealer to protect my finished (dried) work.Tips have not frayed whatsoever so far even with moderate use. I do use my art supplies gently with care though, so I am not doing any kind of heavy handed application to deliberately test their strength but from my use of them to customize 8 water bottles so far they are very strong and retain their pointy-ness for continuous fine detailing. Hope this helps I would get these they’re nice and worth the money with the discount especially!I don’t know what the sheerness rating means but I gave it five stars because they are NOT sheer they are OPAQUE and have no issues with sheerness. I only ever needed a single coat for applications and the coverage is beautiful. Have not tried them without a sealer coat on top, except on my stapler and stationary cup and they are still completely fine but It doesn’t get much traffic. I don’t know why anyone would NOT choose to protect their hard work.

Content: I like these acrylic paint pens/markers. I got the set of 36 which has a wide range of colors. The paint starts flowing quicker than any paint pen I've ever used. The nib is 7mm. The opaqueness of the colors is good and what should be expected of acrylic.The downsides - you really have to shake the markers to mix the pigment up otherwise you could get a more sheer effect or different shade. They also do not have color names or numbers on the pens which for someone who likes to sometimes look for a certain color I found this annoying. I had to swatch and then label everyone so if I wanted too come back to a certain color I would know which one it was right away. Like many paint pens this can sometimes cast splatters around the nib, even on smooth paper. It doesn't bother me too much because I use these for art journaling but could see how that could ruin something more detailed and delicate.Overall I think they are well priced with a variety of pretty colors and if you have a project in mine that doesn't require perfect detail then these could be great for you.

Sentence: I did notice sometimes the pens would appear to dry out as others noted in reviews, but with a few shakes or some pressure on the tip, I've been able to get the pens to start working perfectly again in no time.
Content: I used these acrylic pens to paint rocks. It was my first time painting rocks so I was unsure what products to buy. I first used acrylic paint and brushes for the background on my rocks. After they dried, I used these pens for the details and all the writing. Overall they were great. I can have a shaky hand and inconsistent handwriting on paper but I think most of the handwriting came out pretty good on the rocks. Every once in awhile, if the rocks had a little dip or crack or something in it, the marker would catch and mess up my writing. I'd just paint over it and wait for it to dry then try again. Luckily this didn't happen very often. Think that's more of a rock painting issue though, not a problem with the product. When writing, I learned to write very slowly. If you go to fast the tip will sling paint. If you go slow, you'll have a much better result. I did notice sometimes the pens would appear to dry out as others noted in reviews, but with a few shakes or some pressure on the tip, I've been able to get the pens to start working perfectly again in no time. I've painted over 100 rocks (some a few times - when i didn't like something about my first try 😅) and all of the pens are still fully functioning and seem to have plenty of paint left. The white pen, which is one of the ones I've used the most, has started to crack a little on the tip (see picture). I think it may just be because I'm writing on uneven rocks though. If I don't pay attention, the cracked tip makes the handwriting very bad as it causes the paint to come out inconsistently. I just make sure to tilt the white pen a certain angle and it works just as it did when I first bought it. I do wish the pens differentiated between the finer and medium point tips. I threw them all in one box and the pens have no markings to indicate if they're fine point or not. Luckily, both tips seem to work fine for what I'm using them for. There's not a huge difference between the two but it would be nice to know. Overall, great pens. Definitely recommend!

Sentence: They dry quickly, but that's acrylic for you.
Content: For anyone that started out drawing and finds the switch to painting to be outside their comfort zone, these are excellent. Even trying them out for writing, I really liked the way they handled, and let me put a tiny bit of flourish into my handwriting. But for painting, I also found that these are great for applying a bit of color and then mixing on canvas, which is advice I heard in a painting class but didn't click until years later. They dry quickly, but that's acrylic for you. They also do live up to the waterproof claim once they're fully dry. These made me go back to an old painting, in fact I haven't painted at all in a long while, and it felt so quick and easy to get into it, rather than preparing a palette and everything. I'd suggest shaking and prepping a number of pens so you can quickly grab colors and draw them in, then take a damp brush and blend them once they're on the canvas. It was so much closer to the digital painting skills I've been developing, and was a lot of fun.

Sentence: If you're going to buy them search Amazon and buy the least expensive - you'll know they're the same because of the box design and the lettering on the pens.
Content: I call these "generic Chinese pens" because the box and pens don't have a company/brand name on them, and I've seen the same set for sale on Amazon under at least 2 different company names. Sentence: The project was decorating ceramic vases with these markers and then filling them with a small bouquet of flowers.
Content: I took a big gamble and purchased these for a Valentine's day project for a 5th grade class of 28 students.  The project was decorating ceramic vases with these markers and then filling them with a small bouquet of flowers.  For this project to work well with so many students there was a lot of pressure on the markers themselves - they needed to work well with minimal frustration, be vibrant, DRY QUICKLY, not leak all over the place, and not bleed with washing at home.  I have to say, these exceeded all my demands and expectations.  I don't often write reviews but WOW these markers are well worth the money.  Further, we decorated several leftover vases at home and have washed them several times with absolutely no color bleed, cracking, or fading.  Honestly the vases look like they were professionally glazed.  These markers are fantastic and I highly recommend!

Sentence: They are highly pigmented colors and not transparent.
Content: These acrylic paint markers really did impress me with their quality and the amount of colors you receive for the price. The value for your money is very good and these are quite nice. I like the range of colors that it contains and the box that it comes in is pretty good for storage too. It opens from the top and has a flat bottom so it stands up and you can easily swap markers out without having to close it up and open it up each time while you are in the middle of a project. These paint pens also are super quick to get started and flowing in comparison to other brands that I have tried. These take maybe 2-4 seconds to start up and get the color going when you use it for the first time which is so fast and not a hassle at all. As for the flow and saturation of the markers, I am very pleased. They are highly pigmented colors and not transparent. They make nice solid color that dries rather fast so you can easily layer another color over the top without worrying about smudges. It also seems line you don’t have to really do a ton of coats to get a nice solid streak free color, but I haven’t tried it on a ton of different materials yet so this is still up for review. I also really like the size of the nib that these come with. I am not a fan of paint pens with a very fine tip as they tend to get clogged up quickly snd I just don’t think that I usually want a fine tip when I am looking to use a paint pen. I am usually looking to cover a larger area or a material that is not traditional paper so a broader tip is usually the way I achieve what I am wanting with a paint pen and these markers are the perfect size. Overall, I think these are super awesome quality for the price and I may switch to these for my main paint markers from a more expensive brand that are my go to. These are just as good, if not better in some aspects. These are great for any level of artist from beginner to professional, and I think this set would be great for gifting as well.

amaaazing paint markers! 10/10 easily!

i was really, really impressed by these paint markers! everything about them blew me away. the paintflow was great, only took about 4 pumps for the nib to be fully saturated! the coverage wasn't sheer at all, super opaque and easy to work with. the dry time was pretty good as well, didn't take too long! it also didn't tend to puddle up/overflow like some markers i've used in the past.

the markers themselves were super easy to use, easy to clean up, and even easier to re-package. i would 100% buy these again AND recommend to anyone curious about paint markers! you won't be disappointed! :)

Sentence: They seem to pump/fill a bit faster than Poscas, although they are extremely similar at a much more reasonable price point.
Content:
Very much like Poscas. Some of the colors look identical, in fact, including one of the yellows, the light green, the red, and the black and white. The blues and purples are different. They seem to pump/fill a bit faster than Poscas, although they are extremely similar at a much more reasonable price point. The yellows seemed a bit more opaque. Same factory maybe?? Required little shaking to get them started compared to other markers I've used. Love them. Wish they had more colors and other sizes/nibs.

UPDATE: I bought the new 36 set and the paint seemed a bit thinner. There is a nice range of blues and purples, although they could've varied the tones (or even the hues) of the purples. Same for the yellows. When overlapping to fill a larger area, the sheen is a bit different ranging from matte to satin.

I need to compare these to the first set I got. Several colors are like Poscas, but they have unique colors not available in the Posca line, including the yellows and the cool greens. One criticism of this set is that except for the really light green, they are all blue-leaning greens. This set needs one or two warm greens. An emerald or middle-of-the road green.

It seems like the selection of colors was intentional in the way they filled in the missing Posca colors, but also careless as they should have spent more time tweaking the colors. The oranges have a lot of white in them. Similar to Posca, but too much white. This is just one example of where they needed to put forth more time before releasing a product.

Definitely the sheen, film of these markers is different from Posca. Posca's are all matte (you can feel the roughness). It took a lot of chemistry to develop this as every pigment has its own sheen (yes, some pigments are glossy and need added agents to make them more matte).

One of the markers released liquid orange paint that flew through the air when I used it (and landed on my table). These definitely seem more liquid than the other sets I bought. So, nitpicking aside, I like these.

They work well with Poscas and are very similar except not quite as matte or consistently matte. As a standalone set, the greens are lacking in hues. But for the money you pay, they're a nice addition to a marker collection.

The listing now says they are lightfast. I am going to test them, as Posca reds, pinks, browns (and probably purples) fade a lot, and the lightfast ones available from other companies don't perform as well as these or Poscas as Liquitex and Amsterdam have not perfected their paint formulas (they have been selling markers long enough to make them better quality also).

Being lightfast is huge, if, in fact they are, and it would be nice to see this company share how they were tested--or include lightfast ratings. One other marker dealer, Tooli-Art claims to be lightfast, but the proof is in the pudding, and when companies don't rate the lightfastness or the testing standards, it doesn't lend a lot of credibility to the claims, but let's hope this, that SFAIH is telling the truth and their reds, pinks, and purples are really lightfast, which makes them truly artist grade...

After using these, I was able, after letting them dry for a couple weeks, to use a brush-on, Liquitex matte varnish full strength, no fussing. Note, I was able to do this with Poscas too. The key is to let the paint sit for a length of time, not try to do it the same day or even the next day because they will bleed if the paint has not cured. One you use a matte or other varnish, the discrepancies in finish disappear.

One more feature to mention, these have numbers available on the ends for your charts. Will they be sold open stock? Would be lovely to see these in small nib sizes with nib replacements (I am wondering if they will take Posca nibs)... Great Buy.

Sentence: They're not reflective, but they're beautiful and bright.
Content: I've been disappointed by paint pens before, so the first thing I did was shake, pump, and swatch each one. It came with a sheet for swatching, but I wanted to test it on my own paper as well. Sentence: Rock art was my choice, and after a quick shake, depressing the tip upwards to release air, and then a few dabs with the dip on some paper to get the ink flowing, and you could see the bright colors filling the tips.

The pen itself is comfortable to hold and the paint is good quality from what I can see and doesn't crack after application like some cheaper markers do. These are a great buy and I will look for more in the future.

Sentence:
I had never heard of such a thing before ordering this set.

The markers are simple to use.
Content:
These markers are great FUN! And, yes, they actually deliver OPAQUE ACRYLIC PAINT. I had never heard of such a thing before ordering this set.

The markers are simple to use. You press down to start the paint flowing, and the more you press the marker down or the longer you press, the more paint flows down the nib. Hence you can make somewhat wider or thinner lines, even though the range is limited. The lines themselves are uniform, and the flow is consistent.

The paints adhere very well, as you would expect from acrylic paint. They dried quickly and the colors remained beautifully vibrant (see pic).

The paints are quite opaque on white, but might need a second coat on a dark substrate. (see pic)

I've found them perfect for outlining large shapes, and mistakes can be cleaned up with a q-tip and water before they dry.

They are useful for rock painting and can be used for 'dotting', the dots from them are beautifully round. You can also paint on glass, plastic, wood, etc. with them.

One last thing I'd like to mention: I would love to see these markers with a range of different sizes of nibs, if that's possible. I had to use a fine sharpie, not the acrylic markers, for the fine purple lines in the hair on my picture.

CONCLUSION: For the current price of $18.99, I believe these pens are a really great value. I've had a blast using them.

Sentence:

Content:
I purchased these paint pens for my wife. She uses them for her rock painting hobby.

The pens are well-made but a little smaller than other brands we have used. They prime very quickly and paint smoothly with no blobs or leaks.

The paint used by the manufacturer must have a lot of solids as it covers very well. Even the Yellow pen covers the black outlines with no difficulties. We were really surprised by the quality of the marker pens.

In terms of negatives the only thing we can comment on now is the size of the points which are 2-3mm in diameter. This is a medium sized point that is really good for filling and broad coverage. For work on 2-3" diameter rocks, we wish these points were a little finer.

These marker pens are well made and meet the descriptions and images shown on the website. The paint pens work very well and provide very good first coat coverage. Sentence: For instance I used one to write on the lid of a jar of pigment to label it, no smudging once it was dry which was excellent.Mostly I tested these on mixed media paper, some of the fine point sides were a little dried out and required wiping off before they would work.
Content: I have no experience with acrylic markers. Acrylic paint yes and markers of various types yes, but not this style, but I wanted to try them out since I collect various art supplies. I hoped they would behave like overly large gel pens and give me the ability to add some details over black ink or black paint, and they do that, but there is more going on. For instance I used one to write on the lid of a jar of pigment to label it, no smudging once it was dry which was excellent.Mostly I tested these on mixed media paper, some of the fine point sides were a little dried out and required wiping off before they would work. It was a learning experience, my silly illustration turned out a lot more pop art since you layer rather than shade in a gradient to get dimension (in contrast with the alcohol markers which can give you a softer edge, these want a much more harsh distinct lines) these are really not the style I usually work with, but since they are waterproof (I did an ink wash over the whole piece once dried) I could do some really fun mixed media pieces with ink and paint. There is little to no smell and they dry fairly quickly, since they can go on multiple surfaces I find myself wondering if I can add an interesting mural to the side of my boring black computer desk. I am glad I got these markers and look forward to integrating them more in my art and seeing what other weird things I can do with them.

Sentence: They are easy to use on every surface I've tried, whether ceramic, stones, fabric or paper.
Content: These acrylic paint pens come in a strong card storage box. It is recommended to keep the box horizontal to encourage even distribution of the paint within the pens. Also, of course, one keeps the pens capped.The pens are slim and comfortable in the hand. Each pen is double-ended, offering a 'brush' width and a pointed end. The color range is phenomenal and includes fifteen metallics. The choice of blues and greens is excellent, whilst the yellows are not quite so well served. The sixty pens in the range offer both tints and shades with some very subtle tones. It's exciting to open the box and see them all waiting to be used.Opacity varies with the colour. I usually shake pens before use but obviously it's better to store them in the horizontal as recommended. I don't know the life span of the pens because I tend not to use things to destruction. I think the price is good  for such a range, especially with the choice of brush/pen tip. They are easy to use on every surface I've tried, whether ceramic, stones, fabric or paper. Certainly they are far less mess than a traditional brush and water pot and consequently can be used in a smaller work space. I'm really pleased with them.

Sentence: The colors flow smoothly from marker to page.
Content: I'm a multimedia artist for both the eyes and the ears, and I've been looking for my voice while making my own album covers. I figured some good-quality paint markers would be a great way to get started, and gosh am I glad I started with these.The colors received are all unique, and they're various levels of boldness or subtlety – some of them are even shimmery! The colors flow smoothly from marker to page. The fine tip is a bit stiffer than I'm used to, but the brush tip is a borderline-luxurious experience. It was quick and easy to fill out a fun little sketch-page. The paint dries fast – not quite enough time to do a proper smudge after a stroke, if that's the style I wanted – but honestly that works perfectly for the type of art I like to make. Also, the caps nestle nicely into each other, so you can pop it on the opposite end as you draw – but they're not very tight, so do still be careful with that.So would I recommend 'em? Long story short, yeah! These are great! (Especially if you're starting out and don't care about brand-name recognition!)P.S. The markers come completely unorganized – not even inserted in the box in a uniform orientation – and if you're anything like me, that's a big relief. It means I can scatter these markers to my heart's content without fretting about returning them just like I found them.

Sentence: The colors are really pretty and the laydown is smooth and not blotchy or clumpy.
Content: I like these Shuttle Art acrylic paint markers. I love that they are dual tipped with a brush end and a fine line tip. The colors are really pretty and the laydown is smooth and not blotchy or clumpy. The lightest colors are somewhat sheer but as the colors get darker, you get full, opaque coverage. The markers are easy to hold and I think the range of colors is fairly well balanced. I'm happy about the brush nib since I plan to use these to color backgrounds on some of my coloring book pages. My only complaint is that they come in a simple cardboard box with no trays and no real way to keep them organized by color family. Will have to get a case for them, but that certainly doesn't take away from my satisfaction with the markers themselves. This is a really nice set.

Sentence: once you prime the pen (which does take a fair bit of pressing the nib) the paint goes on smoothly and thickly.
Content: I got these paint pens mostly for labelling purposes (for those times a black Sharpie just won't cut it!), so if you are thinking to use these in a more artistic venture, perhaps this isn't the most appropriate review. However, these pens are pretty much exactly what I was hoping for; once you prime the pen (which does take a fair bit of pressing the nib) the paint goes on smoothly and thickly. It's a nice,  bright white with a kind of matte finish.Depending on the surface, it can take a while to dry; on cardboard it dries almost instantly, but on really smooth plastics it can take a few minutes. It also is pretty easy to scratch off plastic (but plastic is a hard material to paint; you need specialized formulas, so I'm not super bothered by that). It is waterproof, at least in my minimal testing.Anyway, these are a pretty economical set of white paint markers, that do their job pretty well. I'm quite happy with them.

Sentence: The ink dries fairly quickly but not instantly.
Content: These permanent white acrylic paint markers work fairly well. They were easy to get the paint initially flowing by pushing down repeatedly with the tip. The tip is rather wide so these will not work well for fine line writing. While the paint flows rather well once started, I have had to re prime the tips on a few occasions and I've also had to go back over the paint again to get it thick enough on some materials, particularly those that absorb paint easily such as cardboard. The ink dries fairly quickly but not instantly. For most surfaces I've tried, it takes a minute or two for a thick coat to be completely dry. I've also rubbed it with a wet finger after a minute and the paint smeared slightly. Overall, these pens work well for my crafting purposes.

Sentence: There is no odor and the ink comes out fairly quickly.
Content: These are a decent set of paint pens with a large, broad nib that would be great for graffiti in a large sketchbook or some type of artistic work requiring a broad nib paint pen. These can be used on a variety of surfaces and depending on the angle, you hold it out, you can do different types of strokes. (See pics).Really awesome pro that they blend! But you do need to work fast in order to blend because they dry fast. There is no odor and the ink comes out fairly quickly. The paint is bold, thick and vibrant. These are very easy to use and they perform well. The only thing that they don’t do and this might be a pro or con for you is that they don’t drip. Most graffiti pens will give the drip effect and I did not have that with these. Although I was using this on paper, so if I was using them on a glass window surface for example, standing at an upright angle, I think with enough pressure applied, perhaps I could pull off some drips. Because remember you have to press down in order to get the ink to the nib, so I think if you were to press down when using these, you might pull off some drips, but you’re also going to be wasting a good amount of paint too.But I like them

Sentence: They are nice and juicy and give off lots of paint.
Content: These markers work really well. They are nice and juicy and give off lots of paint. Making them great for surfaces other than paper, which tends to buckle. Sentence: I found it a bit too 'wet' for paper.
Content: I like these markers and they are generally as expected and described. First time using each marker takes a LONG time to pump before paint comes through. One other thing I am unhappy about is that no actual BLUE is provided. Only a baby blue color, but no true blue.

Sentence: These markers are good for large areas of color that adjoin each other, but if you try to work in layers the solvent in the markers will cause the lower layer to mix and smear unless you work very quickly.
Content: These markers are good for large areas of color that adjoin each other, but if you try to work in layers the solvent in the markers will cause the lower layer to mix and smear unless you work very quickly. Which is fine if that’s what you want, for a sort of painterly effect. But then you have to clean the marker tips off on a scrap piece of paper to get the color back to what it’s supposed to be. None of this is really a surprise though, since pretty much every paint marker I’ve ever used does the same thing.The tips really take some getting used to though. In my experience getting a truly thin line is pretty hard, but wider lines (kinda thick and very thick) are easy. The rectangular tip lends itself well to calligraphy.

Sentence: I've found a bit of a learning curve in getting them primed and making sure they don't drip paint or make a big puddle, but when I manage it well I've been pleased with the results.
Content: This is the first time I've used markers like these, so I can't compare to others like them. I've found a bit of a learning curve in getting them primed and making sure they don't drip paint or make a big puddle, but when I manage it well I've been pleased with the results. I have only used them so far on card stock, glossy and matte, and the colors are bold and appealing. They cover really well so to a certain extent you can layer one on top of another. I'll be continuing to learn and experiment with them, definitely a solid addition to my art supplies.

Sentence: Paint immediately absorbed into the black foam core board and faded away, and became almost invisible.

We used them on black foam core board and these were BOLD, opaque and sat on top of the surface and dried fast, visible from afar, whereas Dr. Paint immediately absorbed into the black foam core board and faded away, and became almost invisible. Dr. Paint was $3.99 per pen at the hobby store! For that price, I couldn’t believe how bad they were. Get these instead.

Sentence: The product is good, dries quickly and will work well for my needs, for the most part.
Content: The product is good, dries quickly and will work well for my needs, for the most part. The description is a bit confusing though. It indicates that you have three width options, from fairly fine to thick (2-3 mm to 15 mm). It also says that the nib is 2-sided. I thought that perhaps the different ends of the nib would have different widths so that it would be fairly easy to get the fine-medium-thick lines but that's not the case. The nib is the same on both ends and you need to play around with the marker to figure out how to get the width you want. The widest is easy, but apparently each side of the nib is cut with slightly different angles so tilting it one way gives you the medium width line and tilting it the other way or rotating the pen will give you the finest line. You can't do real detailed work with this, at least not that I can see. Maybe with a lot of practice. I do think there is a good value to the wider lines but will have to get a fine nibbed pen to do the more detailed work I need this for.

Sentence: I also tested on a smooth plastic bottle, and though it mostly worked you'd want to apply one or more very thin coats to avoid a blotchy, uneven finish.Porous materials like wood, cardboard, fabric, etc.
Content: I ordered these in black to paint the gold metallic frame of a mirror.  The broad, precision felt tips are easier to work with than a brush and the acrylic paint seems to adhere well to the brushed metal finish.  Though the first test coat looked good, I plan on applying a second just for enhanced uniformity and durability.  I also tested on a smooth plastic bottle, and though it mostly worked you'd want to apply one or more very thin coats to avoid a blotchy, uneven finish.Porous materials like wood, cardboard, fabric, etc. should work very well though I can't attest to it being waterproof or UV resistant since I didn't test for that.  During the initial usage you have to firmly depress the felt tip downward for a few seconds for the paint to eventually flow. At first I thought it was defective but was patient and it eventually started working just fine.

Sentence: I was trying to find an alternative to Posca Acrylic Markers.This brand isn't bad, especially for the price.
Content: I like that the ink comes out smooth (save a few misses where there is a bump or warp). It was easy to prime. I was trying to find an alternative to Posca Acrylic Markers.This brand isn't bad, especially for the price. However, the paper I am currently (a rather low gsm) using causes the acrylic ink within the marker to come with a glossy finish rather than a matte finish as would be the case with Poscas.  There is also a smell that comes from them laying the ink out. It also shines on cardboard, so if that is the finish you are looking for, it is perfect! It's just not what I am looking for.If they were loaded in order, the first pic is Big Thumb Graffiti Marker, and the second is a slightly dying Posca Marker.On the page that I used the Graffiti marker on, I did try a couple of overlaying strokes to see if it would do something with the shine. It did not. There was minor bleed through (not pictured), which also happens with Poscas, just not as much as the Graffiti.These markers will also smear with a bit of water, so be weary of that as well.I will continue to use the three that came in the pack, but I will have to continue finding another brand that is similiar with Poscas, unfortunately.  The markers really are great, though it may not sound like it, it's just the finish is not what I was hoping for.

Sentence: The problem with most permanent markers (at least for me) is that the ink simply dries out too fast.
Content: I use wide tipped markers when labeling boxes so that I can easily see what's inside from several feet away.  In fact, I use them for labeling just about everything!  The problem with most permanent markers (at least for me) is that the ink simply dries out too fast.  I can't speak to the longevity of the BIGTHUMB markers because I haven't owned them long or used them a lot but if they end up having an even shorter life than the other markers, I will be back to update this review.  For now, I'm going to assume that they have a reasonably long life and I hope that turns out to be the case because I'm delighted with the way they mark.  Because they are paint markers, once the ink is flowing you get great coverage and have the option of making very wide to thin marks with a single stroke. I suppose the life of the marker will also greatly depend upon the size stroke you make with it; for my purposes, the medium to smaller tip is perfect.  The one caution I would give is that they do take a bit longer to dry than regular permanent markers because the pens are dispensing acrylic paint rather than ink.  Marks are still relatively quick drying but not instant drying so take a bit of extra care, particularly when the markers are first used, so that you don't smudge your work or end up with paint all over yourself!

Sentence: You do have to press down to get the paint to flow but I really prefer that to having my marker tips dry out and become useless.The case is cute and convenient and the color assortment covers all the essentials.
Content: I have a number of different types of acrylic markers and they all do what they say they intended to do. But there’s something about Uniball/Posca products the consistently put them in a class of their own. These paint markers absolutely live up to the brand promise. The colors are vivid, they adhere to whatever surface you want to color and they have really good opacity. They have a little mixer puck built-in so that when you shake the pen you really get the paint mixed. You do have to press down to get the paint to flow but I really prefer that to having my marker tips dry out and become useless.The case is cute and convenient and the color assortment covers all the essentials. The only thing I don’t like about this is that it is not the giant set of every single color and that I don’t have all the different sized pen tips that Posca manufactures. This is a set that makes you want more and makes you want the good stuff instead of other brands’ more basic offerings. It is such an absolute delight to use that you may very well find yourself decorating every single cardboard box, plastic container and rock you can get your hands on. It’s just so fun making every day stuff pretty with these markers.

Content: I've never used Posca markers before, but having recently entered the adult coloring community, I have heard others sing their praises, and now I can say, rightfully so.  This "holiday" set of 22 markers is really 11 makers of the 3 m and 5 M variety.  Same colors - just different sizes.  The colors include:  black (a beautiful opaque black) and white (equally gorgeous for a paint marker), pink, lavender, light pink, blue, orange, sunshine yellow, light green, aqua green, and sky blue.  I'm not sure why this termed a holiday set.  It is coming out near Christmas and yet the set does not contain what you might consider a traditional Christmas red or green.  (Actually, if you get the larger 62 count set, I bet there is one in it. )  It also does not have any "holiday" packaging aside the very nice hard side (?) case that the markers come in which I suppose makes it giftable.  So there's that.  But the markers themselves are kind of impressive for what they are.  The paint/ink is smooth.  It comes easily off the tip with streaking or skipping. These paint markers are great for any projects that will end up using a number of different colors, but just a small amount of each color, where it would get very cumbersome to deal with so many washings of paint brushes, etc.

I have found them particularly useful for coloring in my 3D prints, because the paint dries very quickly so it doesn't require long waiting periods before the next color can be used.

Given the price to number of markers, this is a better value than other sets I've seen, so I definitely would consider reordering this same kit when the markers get used up.

Sentence:

WHAT MAKES THIS A GOOD SET:
First, that you get so many different styles of markers in one big box that's easy to store.
Content:
I use markers for a variety of crafts, and have purchased way too many glitter, metallic and other specialty markers online and from local craft stores.

WHAT MAKES THIS A GOOD SET:
First, that you get so many different styles of markers in one big box that's easy to store. Anyone that has priced buying these in small sets or even individually will appreciate that.
The glitter pens are pretty glittery. I have a few glitter pens that are a different brand that are more glittery, but they were expensive pens that I had to buy individually from a local craft store. For the price of these, the glitter effect is pretty good.
The metallic markers are also pretty good. The effect is comparable to other brands I have that cost slightly more than these.
You get a good variety of colors in the Classic, Pastel, Neon, Morandi (which are "muted" colors btw, vs bright neon colors). The white, and other light-colored markers do a great job - bright and easy to see on dark paper.

THINGS TO KEEP IN MIND:
When you want to use one of these markers, you kinda have to "get them flowing" initially. They printed a little diagram on the side showing you how to pump them to get them flowing. If you're not getting a very strong, bold line, you need to pump the marker some more, to get the ink flowing better.
Due to the nature of how ink flows from these markers, you can get the best result using them if you're very purposeful in your marks. If you want to make quick, very fast marks, these may not be the pens for you.

- My biggest complaint is the box they come in. The way that this box is depicted in the product description pictures makes it seem like it arrives in a tiered, organized box. It's just a box. It's a nice box, but it's just a box, without any tiers or dividers. The markers themselves are numbered, and the back of the box has a chart or "key" that you can use, to identify what type of marker each number is.
Additionally, the names of the actual colors are not on the box, nor are they on the markers themselves. This might not bother you, but for colorblind folks like myself, not having the actual name of the color written on these markers can be a bit of an issue.

Overall, this is a good variety of specialty markers that I'm sure to get a lot of use out of.

Sentence: Every kind of paint pen she could hope for is here: metallics, glitter, pastels, neon, and classic colors.
Content:
My daughter is in heaven. Every kind of paint pen she could hope for is here: metallics, glitter, pastels, neon, and classic colors. All of the various categories worked as advertised. The glitter and metallic both sparkle, and while they're similar at a casual glance, the difference is there when you put them side by side (the metallics are more shine than shimmer). The glitter pens are also all true to color, not just 12 different labels on silver like others we've tried in the past. The neons jump off the page under UV light. They required less shaking than her previous favorite pens, and they go on smoothly. The tips are comparable to all the other fine pens she's had, and the pack includes spare replacement tips in case one breaks or wears out.

As for the packaging, I'm happy with it, but there are a few tiny things I could have wished for to make it perfect. The pens are numbered on the cap ends, but nowhere else on the pen barrels, so I had to warn my daughter not to separate the caps from the pens and only to ever use one pen at a time lest she mix them up. The legend is on the box, which is fine, as the box is very sturdy and designed for easy access, with the numbers clearly visible when the lid is removed, but there are no fixed dividers in the box to keep the pens from getting mixed up, and with 72 pens, them trying to slide around or fall under the weight of their neighbors when one or more pens have been removed is inevitable. They even arrived mixed up: we had to dump them out and sort them ourselves. Just putting in a few fixed dividers would have solved all of these problems. Especially as the product is broken into 12 pen sets, breaking the box into 12 pen compartments would have made so much more sense and taken a 9 star product to a 10. That's nitpicking, though, so I did not let it affect my rating.

Overall, these are a great product, and fully deserving of the premium price. I doubt I'll need to buy them again myself, these should last us a good long while, but I'll definitely be recommending them to our friends, and if she ever manages to use all of these up, I'll be back.

Sentence: They do dry quickly, but there is still enough time to blend a color in to the another to make a very pretty gradient.
