I believe the white could be a little more opaque, but all in all this is a great acrylic marker set and I will definitely be reaching for these to write color and draw with a lot! They also do have a greediness to them if you go over the same color without it being completely dry, so just be aware of that. I will definitely be repurchasing these as I run out of them. They are extremely satisfactory for what I intend to use them for.

Sentence: I wish the packaging and came in was more sturdy and not the flimsy plastic.
Content: The only reason why I’m rating these markers three out of five stars is because of the size. They are extremely small and have thin barrels. Personally, I feel like there is not a lot of paint in them and I can see them running out really fast if you use them consistently. I wish the packaging and came in was more sturdy and not the flimsy plastic. Reminds me a pack of markers you would get at the dollar tree. I love how it comes with the booklet of paper and two different swatch sheets. The pigment from the markers are really nice and they dry matte. I love the metallics they are so pretty. For a beginner artist or a child I feel like these are great to have to learn the basics. However, If you are an intermediate or professional artist, I would suggest the Posca paint pens over these because they have more paint in them and will not run out as fast. I’m not saying you can’t make great artwork with these. You don’t need expensive art supplies to create great work but they have a beginner feel to them. Also another downside is that if you run out of one color, you would possibly have to rebuy a pack to get the color than buying it individually. Overall they’re good but not great. I’m not head over and heels with love with them.

Sentence: No chunky blotches, no drips, and no smearing.
Content: Instead of having a traditional guestbook at my wedding, I decided to have a sign to put up along with wedding pictures, for our guests to write their messages on.I got a wood sign, in gray. I didn’t want people to write all over it in black sharpie, since this sign will be part of my home decor, I don’t want black sharpie writing displayed on my living room wall. I decided that white writing would look nicest against the gray background.I came across these paint pens. I liked the idea of using permanent acrylic paint instead of ink. I also liked that these were extra fine tip, which would make writing easier.I tested them out as soon as I got them, because I wanted to know if they’d be any good, or if I’d need to get different ones. I had a piece of scrap wood that was close to being the same gray as the sign. The directions said that before using them the first time, to press the tip down a couple of times to get the paint to flow down to the tip of the pen. I did that with both pens a couple times on my scrap wood, until each one left a circle of paint. I tested writing with each pen, and they were super easy to write with. The flow of the paint was nice and steady, and consistent.The wedding was a few weeks later. We were outdoors, in 104 degrees. Both pens continued to work perfectly. No chunky blotches, no drips, and no smearing. I posted a photo of how the sign that was written on with these pens, but the pic honestly doesn’t do it justice. In person, the white paint is a little more vibrant and bright. To put it simply, the white POPS!

Sentence: I love the bold colors.
Content:
I love the bold colors. The caps come off easily & back on. The nib is a bullet point, firm but smooth.
I like to do rock painting & these are perfect. I do paint the rocks with acrylic paint first as I don’t want to waste the Sharpie ink!
Then they easily draw on the rock to color an area or do smaller lines.
They dry fairly quick & you don’t need to do a 2nd coat.
Only thing I would like is a different set that is a bit more fine point, to complement this set. I would also love it if they came out with more colors, maybe metallic colors, different shades of the 12 colors provided - a pale green, deep navy blue, dark orange, deep yellow, pale pink & a lavender purple.
How about neon colors too?
I would buy them all!
Rarely do I give a 10/10, but for what I’m using it for, it’s a 10!

Content:

Overall I am super impressed with these markers!!

Sentence: And the ink dries quickly, which is just another huge advantage when using the art pens on different mediums.
Content: I really enjoy making jewelry. In fact I have been to several jewelry/fossil shows where I buy pieces that I love. Many of the stones are just plain, and have no painted edge to make the stones look great after shaping them into the correct size.I have gold acrylic paint in a bottle that I had been using, but it is a huge setup and tear down after completely the job. I also have to use a paintbrush, which I throw out afterwards. It’s too hard to clean. I didn’t enjoy this portion of jewelry making because of all the extra steps in acrylic painting. Finding these Gold acrylic pens was wonderful. Now instead of getting out all the extra materials for what my acrylic pen will do in seconds.Now I just take out my Gold pen and apply the acrylic paint to the exact spot in about 2 seconds. And I can either use the brush side, for more broader strokes, or a fine point, for painting a sharper edge of a stone. I’ve also found that these paints can be used on clothing, canvas, etc. I am so used to doing one thing with the Gold acrylic that I didn’t realize that I could use them on so many other art forms.I tried the inks on both sides, brush, and point. I just did it on a piece of paper, and I very pleased that the ink flowed out into the paper without having to take any measures, like pressing the tip, to make them work. And the ink dries quickly, which is just another huge advantage when using the art pens on different mediums. I appreciate the manufacturers making the acrylic paint flow easily, dry quickly, stay vibrant, and even the price of the pens is excitable. Besides, how much easier could the manufacturers have made these pens? They are incredibly easy to use.

Sentence: They are extremely easy to use.

We will buy more of same in the future.

Sentence: This set of markers comes with a good range of colors as you can see in my swatches photo.
Content: This set of markers comes with a good range of colors as you can see in my swatches photo. The pens are juicy and ready to use when you uncap them. There is no shaking till your arm hurts and pumping and priming to get the paint to flow like you have with most acrylic markers.I found that the brush tip flows better than the round tip which is fine for me because I much prefer the brush tip. The brush tip is flexible and offers anything from a very fine line to a broad swath of color.The paint in these has a medium opacity. They are not as opaque as the most common acrylic marker brand (starts with a P and ends with an a), but they are pretty good and I can always add a layer if I need more opacity.I feel that these markers perform well and have significant advantages over typical acrylic markers with a nib. They are also a great value for the price so they are worth a try for whatever project you have in mind.

Sentence: At about $11.00 or 46 cents per marker these double-ended acrylic markers seem to be a really good value for the money.
Content: At about $11.00 or 46 cents per marker these double-ended acrylic markers seem to be a really good value for the money.  I don't have much experience with acrylic markers so I was happy to see that I could try them out for not a whole lot of money, in case I decided that I don't like working with acrylic paint.  I was interested in using them on canvas and they are advertised as being for painting on "multi-surface" - paper, canvas, glass, cermaci and stone.  I like the way the color/paint flows easily and evenly - one or two coats needed at the most.  The colors don't bleed through canvas or "standard/regular" paper which is really nice and actually surprised me.  As far as the colors themselves, the red is really more of a pink than a red but for the most part the colors match what you see on the box.  Most of the colors are opaque  and there are a few metallic colors.  I couldn't really see much of a difference between the two tips - brush vs dot, except when I wanted to paint dots - then it was clear that there is a difference.  But, if not painting "dots" there is really little difference between the two tips.  I tried painting on glass and stone; the paint glided on very easily but took awhile to completely dry - reminded me of how you have to wait for nail polish to dry completely.  Since this is a water based ink I imagine that if you got water on whatever you are painting with these markers, the paint will run and dissolve.  For someone wondering if they would like to paint with acrylic markers, I think this is a nice little starter set for not a whole lot of money.

Content: At about $11.00 or 46 cents per marker these double-ended acrylic markers seem to be a really good value for the money.  I don't have much experience with acrylic markers so I was happy to see that I could try them out for not a whole lot of money, in case I decided that I don't like working with acrylic paint.  I was interested in using them on canvas and they are advertised as being for painting on "multi-surface" - paper, canvas, glass, cermaci and stone.  I like the way the color/paint flows easily and evenly - one or two coats needed at the most.  The colors don't bleed through canvas or "standard/regular" paper which is really nice and actually surprised me.  As far as the colors themselves, the red is really more of a pink than a red but for the most part the colors match what you see on the box.  Most of the colors are opaque  and there are a few metallic colors.  I couldn't really see much of a difference between the two tips - brush vs dot, except when I wanted to paint dots - then it was clear that there is a difference.  But, if not painting "dots" there is really little difference between the two tips.  I tried painting on glass and stone; the paint glided on very easily but took awhile to completely dry - reminded me of how you have to wait for nail polish to dry completely.  Since this is a water based ink I imagine that if you got water on whatever you are painting with these markers, the paint will run and dissolve.  For someone wondering if they would like to paint with acrylic markers, I think this is a nice little starter set for not a whole lot of money.

Good staying power-Note that these are matte colors once they dry. So not shiny.Overall I am pretty happy with the way these are working and the color selection is pretty good.

Sentence: The one thing I haven't done is test how the ink holds up to water/washing.All this to say, I'm really surprised and pleased with what these markers can do and how easy they are to use.
Content: I'm no artist. I'm reviewing these just as a regular non-artist who occasionally needs/wants to do some arty stuff.First I tried these pens on paper. Regular paper. They work great. The colors are good and, surprisingly, nothing bled through, even repeated layers of ink.Next I tried them on fabric. I have some plain canvas bags I use recycling and for my fruit/vegetables at the grocery store. I used the pens to decorate the sides of the bags to make it easy to identify & sort, etc. Again, even with repeated layers of ink and very low thread count/loose weave fabric, there was no color bleeding at all. The one thing I haven't done is test how the ink holds up to water/washing.All this to say, I'm really surprised and pleased with what these markers can do and how easy they are to use. The markers are fun & easy to use and the price is great.

Sentence: 3_ The pens I received all seem to be 'full' with no dried out tips - I tested both ends of each pen.
Content:
Purchased the set of 24 (came in a blue box) - wanted more than just basic colors but didn't want to spend a lot - a good compromise. Haven't used these yet except to test them out, but so far, so good. Pros: 1) they write nice - nice flow, movement, etc. 2) as 'paint' pens, there's no shaking or pressing to get the paint to flow. 3_ The pens I received all seem to be 'full' with no dried out tips - I tested both ends of each pen. 4) The lids all have a nice 'snap' and stay on securely. Cons: 1) The box comes with a swatch on the back, giving each color a name and number - but the pens themselves have neither names or numbers, so you can ONLY go by the lid color. And that's pretty tricky. While testing, I made a mark on the swatch with the best, to me, corresponding colored pen. Some colors are amazingly close, others - not at all. First photo shows how I -mistakenly- marked the 'brown' pen on 'Gingerbread' before realizing it left no swatch for the lighter (tan) color. Yeah - the 'brown' is supposed to be 'Stone Grey' apparently. Go figure. In a case like this, I like to mark the pen on a white label, cut a strip, and stick it around the lid of the pen so I can see the true color. Unfortunately, 2) the lids are all very textured with ridges, so this time I'll have to stick it on the pen itself. But where? not on either end close to the caps (it'd cover the symbol showing which tip is which, & don't want it under my fingers when using the pens) so it'll have to go in the center of pen, annoyingly over the text. Not really any other option.
Overall, I do like the pens and would buy them again - the annoyances are small compared to their quality.
Edit: Added my 'actual color' strip to each pen (except black, white, gold, & silver) and added the color # in case I decide to order a larger variety later. Amazingly, the actual colors are VERY close to the cap colors! Amazing because this isn't usually the case! The photo shows how just 2 of the colors are a bit off - the bright pink & the yellow next to it in the top row. Realized I missed the 'tan' and 'grey' pens after the photo was taken. The tan is spot on, but the grey ... it's the same color as the cap, but lighter. You'd need 2-3 coats to make it the same as the cap.
As for how they work - great! Coverage, even over a dark color, is impressive. On the head shown I used black (for the outlines and the eye area), red, light & dark blue, and white (ONLY for the dots on the black part of the eye). The light blue was over the black of the eye and 2-3 coats gave the color shown.

Sentence: These markers were expensive, and the buyer should be cautious about the intended purpose of these markers.
Content: I had high hopes for these jumbo acrylic paint markers. I followed the instructions on the box and shook each marker. When I took the cap off, the nib fell out, and the nibs were reluctant to stay in place on the marker when replaced.  I applied the required pressure to get the paint to flow from the marker through the nib.  Once it started to flow, there was no stopping it.  I had to put the cap back on and store the marker vertically in its box.  This was incredibly frustrating.  I placed the packaging in a plastic bag to ensure I didn’t get paint all over my house.  Usually, I have a problem with getting a consistent flow from acrylic paint markers.  In this case, there was too much paint coming from the marker.  I could not control it at all when drawing any design.  Perhaps I should have taken these markers at their word and acknowledged that they were only for large street murals.  The manufacturer claims these markers work for smaller items like rocks and wood.  I don’t see how this is possible.  These markers were expensive, and the buyer should be cautious about the intended purpose of these markers.  I can’t use them at all.

Sentence: They are made in China, are acid free, &
Content: I want to start this review off with saying that I appreciate the fact that the instructions are on the back of the box for those who aren't sure how to prep this type of marker. They are made in China, are acid free, & water based. There are 12 different colors with silver & gold included. I had no issues with prep or coloring. These markers perform just as good as popular brands especially with the coverage of the versatile rectangle nib. It can create lines ranging 3mm-15mm...fine, med, & jumbo. It's for covering larger areas mostly but the way the nib was designed it comes to a flat point so that you can use it at a tilt to get a slightly smaller line. I've provided such examples in my swatch photo. They dry pretty quickly, quick enough that my hand didn't smear any of the colors/swatch. I also tested the waterproof statement on the blue color on white paper & the color didn't move at all! So that's a true statement. I swatched these on a popular cheaper kids marker/watercolor paper & there was very little bleeding. I think black was the only color that bled through but it was only where there was more than 1 swipe of the marker. I've used these on white boards, rocks, fabric, shells, glass, plastic, & metal. I can't complain about these at all. I'm pleased with them & the fact that my kiddos can use them. I recommend the SRUOLOC markers for students, crafters, hobbies, or in place of your more expensive markers that you want to save for serious works...but these aren't far from the more expensive brands other than the fact that it's only 1 nib which is why I suggest such. I really like them and they're great for learning if nothing else.

Sentence: The markers are advertised as having vibrant colors, but most of them are dull and streaky.
Content: I was really excited to try the SRUOLOC 12 Colors Jumbo Markers for my rock painting and other crafts, but I was let down. The markers are advertised as having vibrant colors, but most of them are dull and streaky. The felt tips are too soft and tend to fray quickly, making it hard to get a clean, smooth line. The paint inside is also inconsistent—it’s either too thick or too watery, and it doesn’t cover well on surfaces like stone or wood. I ended up with smudges and uneven coverage, which ruined my projects. These markers are not worth the price. If you want reliable, high-quality paint markers, look elsewhere.

Sentence: Fortunately none of the paint had leaked out but I had to find and replace every tip and cap for every marker before I could even think about using them.
Content: I'm giving these markers five stars because the markers have nice wide tips and a really nice selection of beautiful opaque colors.  However, they need to be housed within a box instead of a plastic bag.  When I opened the outer packaging, the inner plastic bag that housed the markers had come open in transit and all of the markers tumbled out onto my granite countertops and not a single one of them still contained either its cap or the felt tip that controls the flow of paint from the marker!  Fortunately none of the paint had leaked out but I had to find and replace every tip and cap for every marker before I could even think about using them.  Once assembled, they work beautifully and the colors and paint flow couldn't be better.  I've given them five stars despite the debacle of their arrival but I do encourage the seller to do a better job of providing some kind of case for transport and storage of such a nice product.

Sentence: They function about how you'd expect - they're lightweight so easy to hold, they have quite vibrant colors, and they will work on many surface types.
Content:
For the price, these are excellent paint pens. They function about how you'd expect - they're lightweight so easy to hold, they have quite vibrant colors, and they will work on many surface types. I'm using them on a light, unstained wood, and I have to use at least two coats of whatever color I'm using. That being said, the end product is going to look really nice.

The case they come in is not the best, so I would recommend planning for an alternate storage solution. I purchased a separate pen/pencil case for them that will hold them horizontally as is recommended from the product for how to store them.

The fine side writes really fine and nice. The thicker side is all good. If you go in swirls, you can't really see the strokes. That said, I go side to side because I like the look of strokes because it really screams hand painted. You will need to leave whatever project it is to sit and dry. It's still paint, and as such needs to dry. If you grab it right after, you will get paint on yourself. Thus, if you're getting these for children, I would recommend close supervision. Otherwise, I can see people of most ages really enjoying these for art projects, and especially those who may find it difficult to hold certain brushes or those who don't have storage space for lots of brush types, palettes, etc. Paint pens are a nice alternative.

You can paint over your mistakes after they've dried. I have tested that because I don't have the steadiest hand, so I make mistakes often. However, I have not tried to correct a lighter color over a darker color. Only dark over light, so be mindful that it's paint. It will bleed or blend together. Would not recommend for single-use/one-day projects. Most projects with these will need multiple days. I could see this being fun for really unique beading designs if you're making household decor, crafts, jewelry, etc.

WHAT: 30 Colors Dual Tip Acrylic Paint Markers,Fine Tip and Brush Tip

Sentence: This is important because on some markers the colors are very different than their caps and when you're making art you want to know what the paint actually looks like.Paint quality: Thin, dries quickly and is very translucent.
Content: I use paint markers to paint rocks.Here's what these are like:Colors: The colors are extremely close, if not exact matches to the marker caps. This is important because on some markers the colors are very different than their caps and when you're making art you want to know what the paint actually looks like.Paint quality: Thin, dries quickly and is very translucent. It takes 5+ coats to cover a surface. One of the biggest problems with these markers is that the colors mix when you layer them. For example, if you paint down green, and then let it dry completely, and then paint white over it it, your white marker will be ruined and pick up the green paint. My other acrylic markers don't do that.Tips: The brush tip is great as a brush. It' makes it easy to do thin lines and also fill in large areas quickly. I do like that you don't have to press the tips to release paint, although sometimes this is frustrating when you want the paint to go on thickly or in more quantity.Overall - Good for kids and teens. Probably best for paper. Not at all appropriate for serious artists.

Content:
First time using paint pens of any kind, so take this review with a grain of salt ofc!!

Was apprehensive about buying something like Posca pens because of the price and not knowing whether or not I’d actually enjoy them, so I decided to try these as like a…trial run I guess.

PROS:

Firstly, they are super easy to use. I particularly like the brush nib because it allows for that line variation and filling in larger areas.
Something to note is that I’m using suuuuuper thin (A5) paper, and so far, after layer upon layer—the paper hasn’t buckled hardly at all!! Was a really nice surprise tbh!! In fact, the only thing that made it buckle and bleed through was the pen I was using for my lines after laying down the paint. I have been having so much fun experimenting with the colors (which there are a lot!!)

CONS:

Be prepared to layer these. They aren’t suuuuper duper pigmented like others I’ve seen especially if you’re laying a light color over a dark one, even after shaking them for a bit as it says to do on the back of the box. (Though in all honesty, I enjoy it more as a feature than a con, but I know some people might not find that appealing—but it could be that I’m impatient and don’t shake them long enough before use)
Something I also noticed is that there are NO lighter/pastel type colors. It’s not a huge deal, but I’d really love a few of those just to lighten things up if I need to. Generally good flow, but some of the markers have little fibers on the nib that need to be picked off. ALSO. Before you start layering, give the first layer a little bit of time to dry. I noticed it takes about 10 seconds but then you’re good to go!!

I will say though, for the price and what you get, they work wonderfully and other than what I listed above I can’t think of any complaints!! Great for anyone like me who hasn’t tried them before and doesn’t wanna break the bank on other brands. :)

PROS:

Firstly, they are super easy to use. I particularly like the brush nib because it allows for that line variation and filling in larger areas.
Something to note is that I’m using suuuuuper thin (A5) paper, and so far, after layer upon layer—the paper hasn’t buckled hardly at all!! Was a really nice surprise tbh!! In fact, the only thing that made it buckle and bleed through was the pen I was using for my lines after laying down the paint. I have been having so much fun experimenting with the colors (which there are a lot!!)

CONS:

Be prepared to layer these. They aren’t suuuuper duper pigmented like others I’ve seen especially if you’re laying a light color over a dark one, even after shaking them for a bit as it says to do on the back of the box. (Though in all honesty, I enjoy it more as a feature than a con, but I know some people might not find that appealing—but it could be that I’m impatient and don’t shake them long enough before use)
Something I also noticed is that there are NO lighter/pastel type colors. It’s not a huge deal, but I’d really love a few of those just to lighten things up if I need to. Generally good flow, but some of the markers have little fibers on the nib that need to be picked off. ALSO. Before you start layering, give the first layer a little bit of time to dry. I noticed it takes about 10 seconds but then you’re good to go!!

I will say though, for the price and what you get, they work wonderfully and other than what I listed above I can’t think of any complaints!! Great for anyone like me who hasn’t tried them before and doesn’t wanna break the bank on other brands. :)

Sentence: The pens are neatly packaged in a sturdy and organized zipper case.
Content: This set of 80 acrylic paint pens earns a mixed review.  The pens are neatly packaged in a sturdy and organized zipper case.  This makes storing the pens horizontally easy and ensures your art area is not messy.  I laid out the case and took a piece of pre-cut 4X6-inch white cardstock.  I attempted to start drawing with the black pen.  I couldn’t get the cap off the paint pen.  I eventually had to get a rubber gripper that is used to remove jar lids.  I got into a rhythm and was soon able to remove the tops off the sample pens I tried as I drew my drawing.  I needed to twist and pull using the rubber gripping pad.  If you have arthritis, you may have to work around the fact that the tops are incredibly difficult to get off the paint pens.I started with the black pen, creating a basic drawing to fill in with different colors.  First, I used traditional paint markers to fill in the petals of the flowers.  Then, I used several metallic markers to fill in the flower center and leaves.  Finally, I touched up the black ink and attempted to do some detail work.  I colored the four blue corners last.  The three white dots in those corners took three coats with the white acrylic paint marker.  In contrast, the whitish/grey coloring on the stems is one coat with the white marker (see photograph).The paint pens dry fairly quickly.  I got several paint spots on my hands, which I cleaned with a scrub brush, warm water, and hand soap.  The black pen easily covered minimal mistakes made while coloring the petals and center.  I had to use a light touch, or the nib would wear away my paper. I used a metallic pen to color the center of the flowers. The paint flow was too heavy and made a mess when I opened it.  Eventually, that particular marker’s paint flow slowed, and I could continue to use it.I decided to test whether these paint pens are waterproof and quick-drying.  I waited fifteen minutes after I was done with the drawing.  I wetted down a paper towel with three squirts of water and dragged it two times across the right-hand side of the drawing.  The ink did not smear on the paper but lifted off and covered my paper towel (see photograph).  I have concerns about using these paint pens on anything exposed to water.  Paint from both the regular and metallic pens was present on the paper towel.On another 4X6-inch piece of cardstock, I used two colors to write letters, numbers, and common words  (see photograph).  As you can see, the medium-sized nibs make detailed drawing and writing difficult.  The manufacturer does not hide this; few examples of tiny writing or detailing are on the product description page.  Additional acrylic pens to finish your artwork may be necessary, depending on what you are creating.This paint pen set is much better than others I have tried, but it misses the mark with caps that can’t be easily removed and paint that is not waterproof.  Even with that in mind, I believe this is still a good value for 80-paint pens.  This set may work for you if you are a doodler and want to have fun.  However, if you are serious about your art, you may need to look elsewhere to be completely satisfied.

Sentence: Instead of making colorful see through colors, these pens laid down opaque colors.
Content: This set of paint pens I sort of dithered about getting it as I have many markers and wasn't sure if I needed more things in this type of category of art supplies. I am so glad that I got this set of 80 pens which included 24 metallic pens and the rest in regular colors. When I first started swatching the different pens, something I do with any set of colors, I was stunned at what I saw. Instead of making colorful see through colors, these pens laid down opaque colors. They only come with one bullet tip that is fairly narrow.I finished my swatch page and was happy with them and then over this weekend I have had other reasons to use them. I had gotten a package with preprinted canvas boards and little pots of paint like those in a paint by number set, as well as brushes. Even with using the narrowest of brushes, I made a hot mess of the picture and couldn't begin to stay within the lines with the gloppy paint. I tried these paint pens on the board that I had made a mess of and was able to make the leaves and stems much better and then tried coloring in two of the 5 flowers. They did an excellent job! Amazing to see what a better job the pens from this set made. Now I will be able to use them with the rest of the canvases that I got and send the paint pots to the thrift store. I wonder how many times I got discouraged in my art work because the products that I was using weren't up to par, and not knowing that I blamed myself as causing the trouble. I love these paint pens!I apreciate the opportunity to use these pens. Thank you.

Sentence: The paint dries immediately and I had no problems with smudging on paper.
Content: This is an interesting set of pens. Usually dual tipped means the pen has a fine tip and a broad tip, but these actually have a different color on each end as well. So 50 colors have a brush tip and 50 colors have a fine tip. The paint comes out very smoothly and the coverage is mostly opaque, with a few lighter colors a bit more sheer. There is a wide selection of colors including 20 that are metallic. The paint dries immediately and I had no problems with smudging on paper. I tried them on metal and plastic, and had to let the paint dry a little longer (about 1-1 1/2 minutes) before they stopped smudging. Decent paint pens for the price.

Sentence: They have great flow and none of them were dried out.
Content: These markers do not require priming. They have great flow and none of them were dried out. The cap was fairly true to the color of the paint. I prefer a brush tip. I liked the different color choices and that the colors on each side were harmonious. For those that are 'color' challenged and don't know what goes with what color, these are a good way to keep in that color family, hue, tone etc. They need to be stored horizontally for the best flow. They are a good price for what you get. Coverage is good and they dry fairly quick.

Sentence: The manufacturer claims these markers are fast-drying and waterproof.
Content: I drew a small drawing of flowers, testing several paint markers from this kit.  The acrylic paint markers work well on paper.  There is good paint flow without excess paint on the paper.  I had excellent control of paint placement.  Also, the markers did not require any shaking.  The large selection of colors is pleasing.  I let the drawing set for fifteen minutes.  The manufacturer claims these markers are fast-drying and waterproof.  I ran my fingers across the paper’s surface without ink on my fingers.  Next, I wet down a paper towel with a spray bottle. Sentence: They are hard to get started, in that you have to wait a bit to get the pigment to go into the market tip, which is fine, but once it does, it comes out in a glob, and if you are not careful, you get a big paint smear on your painting surface.

And the smear does not dry quickly!  I wound up with a lot of messes.  There's a lot of colors included, but most of them are not that vibrant.  They do blend fairly well, and I managed to paint some rocks which, in the cases where I didn't get any big splotches of paint, dried well and look pretty nice, but I've tried other paint markers I liked a lot better.

Sentence: The individual marker caps click to indicate they are closed in a very satisfying way, feeling secure but not overly difficult to open.
Content: Unfortunately, my particular box of markers contained two of T329 and missing T333, which I didn't notice until I was in the process of testing them and transferring to a new holder. I was only given the option to request a return and replacement and ultimately decided against it since I had already started using them. I have my concerns about the delicacy and endurance of the marker nibs. I probably will not use them on anything rougher than cardstock and I'm not sure they would hold up against use on wood or stone unless they are extremely smooth or polished surfaces, but I will admit that I did not attempt this.With that being said, these have to be the best quality acrylic markers I have yet to use. They went on my cardstock paper consistently, smoothly and the colors are still vibrant after drying with no clumping, bumps or bubbles. The paint seems to take other mediums layered over the top well, such as outlining markers. The individual marker caps click to indicate they are closed in a very satisfying way, feeling secure but not overly difficult to open. While not a functional part of the markers, I also really enjoy the clear section where you can see the paint inside.While I am a little disappointed by the missing color from my order, I still would consider purchasing these markers again.

Sentence: All the colors have good to excellent coverage.
Content: I have tried about half a dozen brands of acrylic brush markers and these are among the very best.  I like the selection of colors (I got the set of 36) and have tried them all.  All the colors have good to excellent coverage.  I painted small squares of each color with only one coast of paint on both white and black papers and have attached a picture to this review.  As you can see, the colors with only once rapid coat covers completely (the white spots in some of the colors are only because I missed; I did not want to go back and fill in those spots because then I would create a second coat in some areas).  The coverage for black is very good considering how thin the acrylic ink is for one coat.  If you go over the paint a second time the colors are as vibrant as the ones painted on white paper.  I do wish there were names on the colors, but I guess names are just names and the best way to determine which color you want is to base your selection on the paint brush itself.  The covers on the pens are very close to the actual color but not quite exact; I recommend looking at the nib.  I will be using these pens often.

Sentence: They have good pigment, a little light, but you may need to layer to get rid of some streaking which is not uncommon for brush tip acrylic markers.
Content: I got the 72 pack which is a good selectiom of colors for blending. They have good pigment, a little light, but you may need to layer to get rid of some streaking which is not uncommon for brush tip acrylic markers. They don't peel or rip the paper because it is extra soft. I am obsessed with acrylic markers and have 5 different brands and this is probably my second favorite one. For those complaining that the ink runs out, these are acrylic markers so instead of the ink running out, it may have just dried out. They give you extra tips to help with this. Just add a new tip or flip over the old tip and soak and swish around in water for a minute or so, shake them, and at least 10 minutes after, they should be good to go again. Also make sure to have them rest laying flat down all the time. In the 72 pack, there are 2 metallic colors, gold and silver. In the 120 pack it looks like they have a whole row of metallic colors.

Sentence: I heard about these on TikTok, they were cheaper than the other paint markers I had seen.

I kept these depict the problems listed- because of the variety of colors and the fine tip nib. It’s come in handy.

Sentence: The markers are not flimsy in my hands, they're pretty solid.
Content: First these markers are AMAZING!! They are super smooth and dry super fast. I bough the 120 count as I love having a variety of colors and boy I wasn't disappointed! The markers are not flimsy in my hands, they're pretty solid. The overall look of the case and markers look like they could be high end. Overall really happy and in love with my new markers. Now onto the less 1 star review. They supply numbered stickers so you can chart them on their board, they supply as well and so you can reference them as you want. But (and. I know it's a small thing) but the stickers don't stick very well and kept coming off. Not only did I spend time putting the stickers on but than I put clear tape over the stickers to wrap the individual markers just so they will stay on. Over time of taking the markers out there is no way that I wouldn't lose the stickers off the markers and than try to double check on a separate sheet of paper just to match my chart. So if you get these markers my suggestion is to do what I did and put some clear tape on the sticker wherever you decide to place them.

Sentence: All in all, with how many colors you get and the price of them, its a decent value.
Content: Eh its ok. There are some really light colors that dont show up too well. The thin side of the markers are a different color than the brush side. They are not fully opaque and although you can layer them, that doesnt really help. Some thin markers bleed when you color something while others don't. They dry matte which I like and dont come through the other side of any paper. They do have a "medium" drying time compared to other markers i have. I hate that they are not numbered or named because i do a lot of color by numbers and its frustrating to figure that out. Yes, you gwt tiny stickers to put on with numbers but i cant even get the sticker off the sheet! They all rip instead of coming off! All in all, with how many colors you get and the price of them, its a decent value. I've only had them for maybe 2 weeks so I can't speak to durability yet. Guess we will see. (In my picture, the black is the markers, the colors are a gel pen).

Sentence: The colors are vibrant, the metallics are excellent, both nibs are just flexible enough, and I can’t get over the cute “After-Sales Service” piece of paper that came with the set.
Content:
So much thought and care was put into this set, and it shows! The colors are vibrant, the metallics are excellent, both nibs are just flexible enough, and I can’t get over the cute “After-Sales Service” piece of paper that came with the set. The only complaint I have is that the numbers for the markers come on a separate sheet and you’re supposed to stick them on the markers in your preferred order (great idea!), but the stickers won’t stick to the caps or the marker barrel without coming up at the sides.

Otherwise, I’m SO excited to use these markers for my projects!

Sentence: The case they come in is outstanding, so well packaged whether it be for doodling , travel, or using in any way.
Content: Welllll, my dearest little doggy chewed up one of my favorite colors and according to the instruction card, they say they will replace damaged or defective markers. So I emailed them for a replacement pen, just the one pen and they sent a whole new box of 120 markers ( which is what I had originally ordered only about 7 days before he had such fun ) !!! Their response time was practically immediately plus they offered a whole new container of 120 pens!!! This is an unsolicited review that just felt I needed to share. Their customer support was fabulous!! So I haven’t had enough time to really make anything yet but I can expand on what I know so far. The case they come in is outstanding, so well packaged whether it be for doodling , travel, or using in any way. Coverage is very good. I am used to another, lacquer medium and was pleased with the ease and coverage. There is a color chart to fill out with the pens. I was surprised at no primary colors, which was no big deal, and except for the metallic pens, all the other colors are a matte, creamy , smooth finish. The pens and packaging, and enclosed literature are very convenient. A note on their note!! It is hilarious to read, they obviously have approached instructions with a touch of humor and it’s entertaining!!! They encourage you to contact them with ANY problems! I’ve enjoyed them immensely!!! Thank you Pagather for a quality product and great customer service!!! I’ll be back for more!! And will include a photo of what I’ve made!!

Sentence:
Amazing markers — but major consistency issues

Content:
Amazing markers — but major consistency issues

These are hands down the BEST acrylic paint markers I’ve used (and I’ve tried at least 5 other brands). The colors are vibrant, smooth, and cover beautifully on all kinds of surfaces. When they’re working, they’re honestly unbeatable.

The problem is quality consistency. My first set was fantastic until I started using some of the less-used colors — many of them were dried out on both tips. I received a replacement, but I’m running into the same issue again. For such an otherwise amazing product, it’s really disappointing.

If Pagather can fix the drying-out problem, this would easily be a 5-star set. For now, I’m stuck between loving how they perform when they work and being frustrated when I open a marker only to find it’s completely dry.

Sentence: Some of them feel dried out and do not flow well at all.
Content:
I wanted to love these markers, but there are a few things about them that disappointed me.

First, I received 3 markers that had duplicates of the exact same color. I can see how this happened: the markers have no color names or numbers printed on them. So it was probably easy for the person who initially packed them to make that mistake. With such a wide color range, some colors look very similar to others.
Second, the quality of the markers is not consistent from color to color. Some of them flow nicely with rich, vibrant color. Some of them feel dried out and do not flow well at all. The metallic colors seemed to be the best as far as the paint flow.
I found it surprising that with 120 different colors, some pretty basic colors were not included. For example, there is no navy blue or maroon. Maybe they were supposed to be included but they got switched for the ones I received duplicates of?
Finally, they come with stickers so you can label them by number. But the stickers are garbage and they fall off instantly. It’s odd that the manufacturer doesn’t just assign each color a number and have it printed on the marker.

The carrying case is very nice quality and like I said, some of the markers work beautifully. I am going to keep them because I’m too lazy to return them. I think I will get use out of some of them.

Pros:

Content:
Absolutely love these. I originally bought the 72ct. After a couple months I decided I liked them well enough to buy the 130ct. For a larger variety.
(First pic is of the 2 sets side by side without the opposite sides of the fold out sections.)

There’s a couple differences between the 2 sets outside of the obvious color range. The 72ct came with just the markers in the case. I expected the same from the 130ct however I was pleasantly surprised to find a baggy of replacement nibs and instructions on how to replace said nibs as well as instructions on how to fix them if they become dried out.

Pros:
- Easy control
- Smooth consistency and flow.
- Juicy
- Bright, bold, vibrant, gorgeous colors.
- If your main qualifier is brush tips these are perfect! Capable of creating thick lines but also capable of creating those fine details as well as get into the smaller nooks and crannies.
- layer well with like colors.
- No smudging or smearing.
- Dry quickly
- Fine tip is great for dotting. I’ve used them primarily for adding dots and other embellishments over top blocks of color.
- Case is well made and makes for easy storage as well as taking them on the go.
- good color variety in both sets making smooth and subtle color transitions a breeze.
- NO BLEEDING

Cons:
- 3 of the markers in the 72ct arrived dry, however not entirely. (Upon receiving instructions in the larger set in how to fix this I feel this has been made up, tho these instructions should be included in the smaller sets.)
- The fine point is not very fine, it is indeed a small bullet tip that doesn’t do well at all for fine details. The brush tip works better.
- There is some color consistency issues between the brush and bullet tip on some colors however slight.
- Some of the fine tips leave behind fibers.
- These do NOT work well on fabrics, colors will not show.
- Majority of the colors do not appear well on black surfaces. (This does not seem to be the case coloring over lines in coloring books).
- Not all colors layer nicely as these are water based, if you attempt to layer colors on opposite sides of the spectrum they just mix.
- There is only one Red in the 72ct.
- Some colors are more transparent than opaque in the fine tip.

Overall, very worth it. I have sets Ive paid more for that were far less quality.

** The ONLY metallics from this set used in the posted pictures were the SILVER and GOLD. The rest of the metallics used in said pictures are from Karin.**

**All NON metallic colors used in my posted photos are from these 2 sets.**

Sentence: It's a really good palette.The brush tips are a joy to use and the paint feels consistent.
Content: Now THIS is a set of acrylic pens! Every set has strengths and weaknesses, so I'm always on the lookout for certain things in particular:- Caps that can be retained on the end of the markers- A set of colors which all have good contrast against one another- Brush tips, so I can do both very fine and very broad strokes with one tip- A good array of DARK colors, not just a good array of midtones and light colors- A good box or case that shows every marker at once and doesn't require lots of searching for an empty spot to put a marker back intoThis set has four of the five things. There aren't many dark colors in here. But I can say that this set has enough color & saturation values for you to be able to make an amazing range of stuff. You can paint things that require lots of fine variations - fancy birds, iridescent bugs, opal, space pictures, and more! There are also a LOT of skin tone options so you can make an accurate likeness of just about anyone. Lots of tan-/dun- like colors for realistic animal fur too. Finally, there are a lot of distinct hues in the red, purple, and pink parts of the spectrum - something I don't see in other marker sets. It's a really good palette.The brush tips are a joy to use and the paint feels consistent. Even the reds and yellows go on very strong, and I don't have to go back over them a lot like I do with other paint pens. In the picture, you can see some doodles I made on a dark rock, and I only had to draw each thing one time to get colors that solid. It's definitely good paint with a lot of pigment in it. I really like the range of color and saturation values on offer because I can use a ton of colors without making something that clashes or hurts my eyes.If you're gonna use or move the box often, I recommend cutting some small holes in the top of the lid. This breaks the vacuum so the lid comes off much more easily.I recommend the pens!

Sentence: Well, the Dual tip is not worth it, imo.
Content:
Tried 3 different sets, these 30 single brush tips and 2 sets of 48 of the dual tipped markers, one from this brand and the other from Pagather that were all in similar price rance during sales. The main question was to see how the brands differed, but also to understand why the dual tip set from THIS brand was so much cheaper despite the additional tip and carry case that these lack. Well, the Dual tip is not worth it, imo. I felt the difference in the weight of the pens, which clearly is due to the amount of LIQUID in them, and these win by a mile. I can see the duals running dry in much less time.

Given the value of how much more coverage you will get from these, this is worth the money where the other is not so much. I easily would choose this set of brush tips only over the dual marker, if only because fine lines are just as achievable with this tip anyway. The fine point of the other is more like a marker than a brush, which maybe is preferable for those without as much motor control in the hands, like kids. But for the price to usage ratio, I think there is much more to found in these.

I am currently considering how much color variety I really need, and whether I am willing to return all three sets to get the 48 single tip markers and case to go with it, or maybe just go with 36 since neither of those is discounted and I don't really NEED this, just thought it might be nice go have as a crafty sort of person who loves art supplies. If I were wanting them for creating paintings myself, I would definitely get the 48 set of these over any of the dual tipped varieties.

If I had these in a zippered case, I wouldn't even think twice about the extra colors and be very satisfied. These seem to be vibrant, more like opaque paint than watercolor, and supposedly waterproof, and seem to have the most favorable reviews with fewer complaints than other brands.

So the only question is how much more is that case worth to me if I decide to return these or not.

Sentence: They dry so so fast and they don't bleed through your paper, at all!
Content: These acrylic markers are absolutely perfect! They work so well coving the black lines of my coloring books. They dry so so fast and they don't bleed through your paper, at all! For 72 colors, they have a huge variety of colors, making it so easy to add those details to each coloring page. I have tried other brands but these are my absolute favorite! They are extremely affordable for the quality of the markers! If you're debating on these and not sure, let me tell you that you're going to want to order them! They are absolutely worth all the hype! Now that I have them, I can't see my pages without them! The brush tip is perfect, it's great for any size, you can use the tip for smaller areas or lean it to its side and cover larger areas or whatever it may be. All you do is shake the pen & it's already activated, that's basically to make sure your ink is flowing. No pressing and waiting for the ink to come out, it's already ready to use! They are so juicy, too. The ink flow isn't too much or too less, it's perfect! I really believe they are good for all ages, also! I mean clean up is pretty easy, maybe with adults present for younger kids but I believe probably 6plus would fine to use them. I'm in my 30s and I absolutely love them and use them every single time I color. The only thing I wish I would have done differently is get a bigger pack! I hope this helps!

Content:
I’m impressed with the quality and variety of these acrylic markers! They’re the kind you have to prime by shaking and pressing down the nib a few times but they prime much more easily than some so I didn’t find that to be a hindrance.

You get a great selection in this set and most of the colors are very different from each other. I love that there are glitter, metallic and neon markers included as I don’t often see that with acrylic marker sets — I do wish the glitter shades were a bit more glittery than they are but they’re still nice.

The markers have .7mm tips and are described as ‘extra fine’ tips in the listing. While I would normally associate ‘extra fine’ with a .5mm tip, I’ve never seen acrylic markers with a tip that fine. The tips are definitely fine enough to use for line work, lettering or small details and the ink flows very smoothly.

The only thing I haven’t had a chance to test so far is how long the markers will last. But with that in mind, they are easy to use and the color goes on super sheer. Between that and the fact that this is the best color selection I’ve found in an acrylic marker set so far, they are definitely worth purchasing.

The price of $52.99 is a bit higher than I’d usually pay (although it’s not a bad deal considering that it’s still less than 50 cents per marker) but the seller is currently offering a 50% off coupon. At that price, this marker set is an absolute steal.

Sentence:
I got these to use on wooden Christmas ornaments with my grandkids so we will all be wearing painting aprons to protect our clothes.

I found this set to be so much fun to use.
Content:
These paint pens are simply fabulous! Not a marker or a pen, but actually paint in a pen. So much fun to play around with! I had just sketched out a little scene from Pinterest, trying to decide if I wanted to purchase the stamp set. Since it was just sitting there I decided to use these paint pens … FYI, I had a blast and was pleasantly surprised.

First you have to prime each pen to get the paint flowing. Originally I had used a permanent ink sketching pen to do this and I was pretty amazed that these paint pens are opaque and could completely cover my black sketching ink. I purposely left some of the black in showing, but I could have covered it if I had wanted too.

I discovered a fun little hack. On the paper towels I was using to prime these pens, I also had a piece of clear scotch tape. I primed some ink on the tape and it stayed wet long enough to dip a wet paintbrush in the ink and smear it onto the watercolor paper that my sketch was on. An improvised paint pallet! I had to move quickly, but it was doable.

When you prime these paint pens, use multiple layers of paper towel as the ink is permanent and you dont want to mark up your work surface. I got these to use on wooden Christmas ornaments with my grandkids so we will all be wearing painting aprons to protect our clothes.

I found this set to be so much fun to use. Just remember that this really is paint flowing out of a pen. It dries quickly. The metallics are especially sparkly. Any artsy kid or adult would love this set!

Sentence: The whole set is in a very sturdy box which shuts well with a tuck in lid on top.
Content: I got this set of paint pens because I am going to be doing some acrylic paintings soon and I want to have a variety of techniques available to me.HOW THESE COMEThese come in a clear case with an envelope of paper and swatch sheets.  There are also a few drawing papers to practice coloring on.  The whole set is in a very sturdy box which shuts well with a tuck in lid on top.  This also allows you to store these flat.CASEThe case is clear. Each level comes apart pretty easily.  It has to be laid out side by side for easy access to all of the colors which requires a table top.  To use these on the lap, it is not convenient.  The pens might have to be moved to a holder and then stored flat in the case when you are done.  Alternatively, you can move it to a book style case with pages but remember to store the pens laying flat not end up.PAPERSThe papers inside are excellent quality paper to play around with and do swatches on black and natural light color.  The coloring pages are also really fun to play with.PENSThe paint pens are fantastic.  The brush tips allow for a great flow of paint and it is very close to painting with a brush dipped perfectly.  The colors are painterly vs bright and loud.  The window in the side lets you see how much paint is left.  Since each pen has to be used and covered immediately, I hold the lid while using the pen.  The colors on the end and labeling are well done.QUALITY PAINT AND PERFORMANCEThis is one fantastic set of paint pens.  They paint perfectly and are smooth and have excellent coverage.  There is no skipping and it can go from thin to thick lines pretty easily too.CANVASI used this to test on canvas board and the results were great.  They really look nice on the canvas and dry to nice intense colors.THE BOTTOM LINEThis is a beautiful set of paint markers.  The colors are beautiful and performance is excellent.MY RATINGFIVE STARS.  I like this alot.  The case is a bit tough for me to use in my recliner, but if I move the pens to a book case, it works well.  I just have to remember to lay them flat.  These will also be excellent to do detail work on acrylic paintings and make greeting cards.

Sentence: UPDATE::: Y'all I love these markers so muchI've been using them consistently since I got them in october- no issues with drying AT ALL, though I would recommend taking them out and giving them a good shake periodically as a precaution.I find that they work smoother/more painterly on canvas or primed surfaces- they dry a bit too quickly on paper and soak up a bit more, but they still didn't even bleed through my mixed media sketchbook, so that's a major win!The case does take up a lot of space when you have all the sections out and accessible, which isn't my favorite, but is only a minor hindrance.
Content: UPDATE::: Y'all I love these markers so muchI've been using them consistently since I got them in october- no issues with drying AT ALL, though I would recommend taking them out and giving them a good shake periodically as a precaution.I find that they work smoother/more painterly on canvas or primed surfaces- they dry a bit too quickly on paper and soak up a bit more, but they still didn't even bleed through my mixed media sketchbook, so that's a major win!The case does take up a lot of space when you have all the sections out and accessible, which isn't my favorite, but is only a minor hindrance. No issues with snapping or breaking at all.I still have nitpicks about the color range (lack of oranges and yellows, mostly) but have found that, while they're still wet, they do mix quite nicely. You can achieve a lot of good in-between colors by mixing on the surface you're creating on before the marks dry.Though I am still so sure I will run out of white and yellow before anything else, which has me wishing I could buy individuals.Despite that, these are one of my favorite sets of art supplies in recent years. I'm obsessed.Updated pros/consPROS:-Surprisingly opaque-very saturated colors-dries fast and layers well (colors do dry a bit darker, as it goes with acrylic)-The brush tip is actually the best, no more pumping a paint markerCONS:-color range is lacking a bit in oranges, yellows, and dark colors-case takes up a lot of space when opened--------------------------------original review--------------------------------(I got these today, so this is a 'first impressions' review)I'm a artist and art instructor by trade, and I like to use a wide variety of materials to make recommendations to students as well as find new supplies for myself.These markers are pretty solid- I like acrylic paint for its opaque layering properties, as well as the quick dry, and these markers are pretty effective at both. As with acrylic paint, you do have some transparency and a need to layer, especially on lighter colors like white and yellow, or on top of darker colors. But overall, the coverage is pretty solid and the saturation is impressive.The case is a bit weird, you have to be careful separating the layers (they tuck into these little ridges at the back to hold together, and I can see there being a risk of snapping) but otherwise it seems convenient.The color range is odd. Acrylic dries darker than it applies, so after you let them sit for a moment you do have deeper hues, but the black included is SO much darker than the deepest of any other color.I'd really love to see a deep jewel tone range for each hue so I can achieve solid depth without just resorting to black. A deep alizarin crimson, phthalo blue or Paynes grey, deep viridian- the problem, I assume, is that these markers all have an almost chalky binder to keep the opacity up, and it sacrifices the deeper values as a result (many of the above listed colors are traditionally transparent.) So I'm not sure this would even be possible with the current pigment/binders used.Still, it would be wonderful to have a really deep set of colors, and if I'm just missing them in this 60 pack, I'd love to be directed to where I can grab them.Also, there's not a lot of orange options, and there are a whole lot of certain other colors, like green and pink.Anyway tldr;PROS:-nice opacity-very Saturated-dries fast and layers well-smooth flow with convenient brush tipCONS:-color range is lacking in oranges, yellows, and dark colors-case is a bit confusingI'll come back after a couple months of use to update on whether the markers have any trouble or not, but as of today I'm liking them.

Sentence: The pens are ok, but one application didn't cover the black line around the swatch box on the white card, and on the black they were fairly streaky.
Content: The box that these come in is really nice. It's hard plastic, with each tray coming out separately. You can take out one tray, then put the top on that so you have a handle to carry it, so you don't have to take the entire box with you if you don't want to. It's also compact, so it won't take up much room, and the markers can lay horizontally, which is the way acrylic markers should be stored.  I found this box to be the very best feature of the set. I swatched the colors on the swatch sheets that came with it (one white and one black) and I wasn't terribly impressed. The pens are ok, but one application didn't cover the black line around the swatch box on the white card, and on the black they were fairly streaky. I realize that paper isn't the best medium for using acrylic markers (canvas paper, glass and metal would be much better) but I expected the paint to have a little better coverage. I do like that they hold a lot of paint, and that each marker has a number that corresponds with the swatch sheet. I also like the window in the marker that shows how much paint is left, and I really like the brush nib as opposed to hard nibs some other markers have.Do I think this set is worth $69.99?  No. I have other acrylic markers that perform as well, although they might not hold as much paint, and don't have the awesome box. But I'm cheap, so you be the judge.

Sentence: The things that kept me from giving it five stars were as follows: the case is kind of a pain to deal with.
Content: These were really nice paint pens. The things that kept me from giving it five stars were as follows: the case is kind of a pain to deal with. You have to unsnap each layer and lay them all out to have easy access to any color. And then when putting the cases back together you have to make sure that the clip on the case above doesn’t get snapped in when you clip the one below. It just seems very unnecessary when a zipper case that you can unfold and lay out works much better. I have another set of 60 of these almost identical pens and they came in a zipper case that was much easier to deal with. I will say that the case looks very nice tho. My second problem that I took a star off for is that some caps fit nicely in the back of the pen when using it while others were too loose and wouldn’t stay on. I don’t like having loose lids to keep track of and it just seems strange that some would do that while others didn’t.As far as the actual marker goes tho, I would say that they perform at a five star quality. On the swatch sheets I only did one layer for each shade except for the white on the black sheet. I did two layers on that trying to see how many I would need to get a good solid coverage on black. I would say three layers would do it. I don’t ever color on black paper so it’s not an issue to me but that might be a problem covering black lines in coloring books. Rarely would I want to cover a line with white so again that’s fine with me. I also absolutely love the color selection! There are a great range of colors and many neutrals which I appreciate. On white paper it only took one layer for opacity. In fact if you look at the sample flower I painted the darker blue/green outline around the flower had red below it. I changed my mind after coloring it red And then went over with the darker shade of blue/green and it only took one coat to cover the red. I was impressed by that.The presentation of the set was really sharp too! It came with a thick black envelope containing all the swatch sheets, instructions, and sample coloring sheets. Shuttle Art if you’re reading this please make a coloring book specifically using that same white paper and gray outlines for acrylic markers! I would buy that in a heartbeat! I love that paper! Also the case looks really nice setting on your shelf. While I’m not crazy about its functionality it does look sharp and is nice quality. For these reasons I think this set would be a perfect gift for the color lover in your life. It feels a step above the others. Just fantastic presentation.Update: after playing with these for awhile and getting the new pastel set I decided to change the rating to a 5*. The case has NOT been the pain that I thought it would be and for the value of the pens it’s worth it. I would highly recommend these to anyone! Btw if you have the set of 60 and get the pastel set too, the trays DO fit together into one stack. They are a pleasure to color/paint with. 🥰

Sentence: If you can't reach into some areas 'cause the tips are too wide, you can then just use a qtip or traditional brush to push the paint into those areas and spread it around.The black pens come in real handy for weathering and fake shadows.
Content: I use pens like these all the time in painting my 3D resin prints. They're great for experimenting 'cause you can try out different colors and color combinations on your prints without having to clean your brushes out each time. You can blend colors together easily on your prints and you can get rid of mistakes just by wiping the paint off. Then, once you get the color scheme you like laid out, you can continue using these pens to apply your final paint job or you can transition to brushes and just use what you just did as a guide.These also work well when it comes to actual painting. You can paint straight areas like pipes and panels and walls with no problem. If you use metallic colors, you can make these things look nice and real. If you can't reach into some areas 'cause the tips are too wide,  you can then just use a qtip or traditional brush to push the paint into those areas and spread it around.The black pens come in real handy for weathering and fake shadows. You can selectively paint over some areas to apply that paint and then just wipe those areas off to leave paint only in the recesses to simulate weathering or shadows. These work great for that.Just be aware that there are limitations with using paint pens like this. You can't easily paint large areas 'cause you'll end up leaving visible pen strokes. You can get around this issue to a certain extent just by gently wiping your painted areas down and applying perhaps more coats. But still large areas could prove difficult.

Sentence: The paint markers come in a sturdy case that snaps shut.
Content:
This is a great set and I started playing with it the day it arrived. The paint markers come in a sturdy case that snaps shut. It's nice that you can see all the markers at the same time. It's a bit tough popping them out, but they stay in place. The lids also securely snap shut but you really have to be sure they are shut -- look at the cap to be sure it's all the way down because it takes some pressure to close them. Because of this, the lids won't fall off.

It comes with a color card so you can test each color and know what they look like, but the layout is confusing and doesn't follow the order of the pens in the case. Why not make them go in the same order? It's very weird but I got most of the colors on it. Still can't find one but eventually I will. The problem is that the paint color is on the top of the cap, so it's hard to see them when the markers are in the case. Also, some are printed in white on light colors so they are really hard to read because they are also very small.  It would be much easier if they were printed on the sides of the pens so you could see them all at once. There is a system to naming them, such as BV1 for blue violet 1. Some of them don't make sense, but most are easy to figure out. Again, all the colors in white on the sides would be a great improvement in the future.

The paint is very nice -- it's really opaque, goes on smooth, and is a bit wetter than typical paint markers like this so you have a bit of time to blend it. Not much, but enough for small areas. You don't have to pump these to prime them as they are ready to go. The tip has a nice flexible point that makes both thin and thick marks really well.

The color selection is what really makes me happy -- this set has not one but two actual REDS! Holy cow, I have been waiting to find a set with red and not some coral/vermillion color pretending to be red. There is a bright red and dark red and they look beautiful. The paint dries darker so don't be fooled by the color you initially see. I was worried the darkest purple wasn't really dark, but it dried to a beautiful dark violet color. The dark brown also dried to a nice deep brown -- another color that is hard to find. I do wish the darkest blue and green were darker, but they're still nice. The green include a light lime green as well as regular grass green, cool greens, olives, and some blue-greens. There is a nice array of purples with warm and cool tones. The pinks are okay -- the dark one is darker than most others I've tried, but still not a true magenta. There is a nice selection of light pinks. The yellows and oranges are wonderful, with shades all the way from light yellow to dark orange and even includes mustard. There are a lot of colors that I would classify as pale skin tones, as well as an array of light to darker browns. There are far more light colors than dark, so this is great if you need pastels. The black is nice and dark with no noticeable cool or warm tones. Overall, I am really happy with the color selection; the cap colors come close to what you actually get.

This set is a bit more expensive than others, but you get so many colors that the cheaper sets just don't have. And the paint is better quality. If you like painting with paint markers, you will love this set.

Sentence:
There is no window on the side to see the paint level and you do not have to shake them to get them to work.

COLORS
This set has a LOT of colors.
Content:
I have been collecting a few sets of acrylic marker/paint pents so that I could do some detail work on paintings, models, or artwork and not have to use a brush for some things.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a great case. It has a lot of room in it and is very well laid out. They are easy to see and use from a chair or table.

MARKERS
The markers themselves are brush on one end and fine point on the other. There is no window on the side to see the paint level and you do not have to shake them to get them to work.

COLORS
This set has a LOT of colors. If you do anything like rock painting or other bright colored projects, you will have plenty to choose from. Some of the colors are similar, but I don't mind because if one runs out or dries up, I can just change to another.

PERFORMANCE
On paper, these are pretty good intensity. They are not as opaque or thick as some others I have but they still work great for projects that don't need a heavy opaque laydown of paint. On canvas, they are hit and miss. Some of the colors are more transparent than others and will need more coats. The best ones on canvas are the metallics as they cover well and the texture is excellent. I have included a quick photo I took of some tests I ran showing the metallics up close. I hope you can see it.

DRY TIME
These dry very quickly. On paper it is really fast. On canvas, it takes a little bit of time, but not much before you can put on another layer.

USE
You will need to use these. Once you get them, use them. They will most likely dry out pretty quickly and you won't get to have fun with them if you wait too long. This is the type of art tool you want to enjoy when you get it and not put it away for that project you will probably not get to anyway.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For models, artwork, and even rock paintings, these are decent acrylic marker pens. The paints are somewhat transparent in some colors, so plan accordingly

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. For what these are, they are really nice. I love the case and apprecaite how easy it is to see them, store them, and take them with me when I want to do a project. I can do it in a chair or at a table. I just have to remember to push to use them before they dry up at some point so I can enjoy them while they are still working.

The markers themselves are brush on one end and fine point on the other. There is no window on the side to see the paint level and you do not have to shake them to get them to work.

COLORS
This set has a LOT of colors. If you do anything like rock painting or other bright colored projects, you will have plenty to choose from. Some of the colors are similar, but I don't mind because if one runs out or dries up, I can just change to another.

PERFORMANCE
On paper, these are pretty good intensity. They are not as opaque or thick as some others I have but they still work great for projects that don't need a heavy opaque laydown of paint. On canvas, they are hit and miss. Some of the colors are more transparent than others and will need more coats. The best ones on canvas are the metallics as they cover well and the texture is excellent. I have included a quick photo I took of some tests I ran showing the metallics up close. I hope you can see it.

DRY TIME
These dry very quickly. On paper it is really fast. On canvas, it takes a little bit of time, but not much before you can put on another layer.

USE
You will need to use these. Once you get them, use them. They will most likely dry out pretty quickly and you won't get to have fun with them if you wait too long. This is the type of art tool you want to enjoy when you get it and not put it away for that project you will probably not get to anyway.

THE BOTTOM LINE
For models, artwork, and even rock paintings, these are decent acrylic marker pens. The paints are somewhat transparent in some colors, so plan accordingly

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. For what these are, they are really nice. I love the case and apprecaite how easy it is to see them, store them, and take them with me when I want to do a project. I can do it in a chair or at a table. I just have to remember to push to use them before they dry up at some point so I can enjoy them while they are still working.

Sentence: This just makes it look cheap.
Content:
This set of 72 colors includes a wonderful selection of colors! I really love that I have so many choices which are not always offered or they’re a color I wouldn’t typically use so it doesn’t get used. I can see ALL of these being used. They are in a nice zippered black case, but there are two things I don’t like (hence the 3 stars vs 5). I don't like the large white print on the front that just states what it is: “DUAL TIPS ACRYLIC MARKER 72 PCS”… it isn’t attractive in any way… understatement. Keeping it free of print would be best, or at minimum a better font, imo. This just makes it look cheap. Otherwise this could appear to be a nice gift, which at $50 is a very nice gift. And here’s the second thing I don’t like. I feel that price is WAY too high since I easily found a comparable set (72 dual tipped acrylic markers in a case) for just under $30!! You could buy two sets of 72 markers (that don’t come in a case) CHEAPER than this one!! Why so expensive? It’s a mystery to me. And from what it showed in pictures, the other one didn’t have tacky writing on the front of the case. So I’d say yes this is a nice set of markers and colors, but definitely shop around before making a selection because there are many other options on Amazon for about $20 less! That’s why I gave it 3 stars vs 5. I feel a little over priced is one thing, but $20 over what most others sell for is another, and gets you a reduction in stars.💁🏼♀️ I can’t speak on durability since they’re new, but I’ll update my review should anything come up.
Happy shopping!

Sentence: This set has 72 fabulous vibrant colors!
Content: This set has 72 fabulous vibrant colors! With 72 unique, bright, and vibrant colors to choose from, this complete set of double-ended acrylic markers is colorful enough to meet all of your creative needs. The ink provides excellent coverage and durability, allowing your creations to stand the test of time. Its super important to ensure the cap is closed after each use so as not to compromise the integrity of each marker.The dual tip design, including a 1-5mm brush tip and a 0.5-1mm fine tip, is brilliant! The brush tip is perfect for drawing and coloring large areas. The fine nib is perfect for outlining fine line work, and you can create different strokes by changing the pressure of the brush, bringing more convenience to your creation.They dry quickly although do not dry out as long as the cap is on firmly. They are super functional. The thickness is perfection. I could write a review that's 3 times as long although for the sake of brevity, I'll say if you're interested in these, buy them! You won't be disappointed.
