Sentence: Each marker’s ink is opaque, metallic, and glittery enough to blind any dullness in your life.With a 0.7mm fine tip, these markers deliver lines so crisp, you’ll wonder if you’ve secretly become an art prodigy.
Content: Who knew your next masterpiece (or attempt at one) was just a pen shake away? These 16 shimmering colors are here to take your arts and crafts game from “meh” to “wowza!” Whether you’re jazzing up rocks, paper, or random objects around the house, these glitter paint pens will have you channeling your inner glitter god or goddess.From bold blues to radiant reds, these markers scream, “Look at me!” Perfect for crafting, drawing, or doodling on your coffee cup while pretending to take notes in meetings. Each marker’s ink is opaque, metallic, and glittery enough to blind any dullness in your life.With a 0.7mm fine tip, these markers deliver lines so crisp, you’ll wonder if you’ve secretly become an art prodigy. Whether you’re sketching elegant greeting cards or just aggressively doodling glitter mustaches on magazine photos, the ink flows as smoothly as your best pick-up line (or at least smoother).These markers are non-toxic and odorless, so go ahead and let the kids join in—though we can’t promise they won’t cover the walls in glittery doodles (hey, it’s called modern art). The ink is designed to sparkle forever—or at least until your cat decides to knock your project off the table.Don’t panic when nothing happens at first—these markers aren’t broken, just shy. Give them a good shake, press the tip, and voila! Glittery magic. (Pro tip: read the instructions on the box—yes, that box you already threw away.) Once the mystery is solved, you’ll love how easy these are to use.These bad boys write on glass, wood, stone, fabric, paper, and probably that one surface you swore couldn’t be decorated. Turn anything into your personal glittery canvas! Tired of boring notebooks? Done. Want to bedazzle your favorite mug? Go for it. Need to leave passive-aggressive notes on your roommate’s leftovers? Glitter makes it classy.Love the colors, love the glitter, and I’ve left sparkly reminders of my genius on every surface I own.

Sentence: What you get a thicker line that is very satisfying, and consistent.
Content: I purchased this item because I am an artist and I've become very comfortable with the Ohuhu brand name. I saw that they had this new acrylic marker out and I wanted to try it out.My opinion is that this is sort of a niche acrylic marker, because the tips are a little different than what I'm used to. Compared to other brands on the acrylic marker market these brush tips seem to be sort of hairy, and seem to shred at the tip ever so slightly.The results are different. It isn't like an alcohol felt tip that produces the same fine lines and bold edges until the tip starts to degrade. It is sort of like a brush tip of an actual paint brush tip. What I've achieved with this tip is either very fine sketchy lines or blocked in areas of color.What I mean about sketchy lines is that the brush seems to be designed to feel like a paint brush. If you lightly drag the brush across the page you're going to get thin lines, but they aren't going to be consistent. What you get is a thin sketchy line that is fine, but sort of annoying at the same time. I did play with them for a while and after a while I figured out how to use that sketching motion to get some fine points and light lines, but still the ability to paint a long consistent thin line just doesn't really happen or apply here.What happens is if you put the slightest amount of pressure on the tip, you're not really going to get a fine line anymore. The flow of this pen is really good and the paint sort of pools. What you get a thicker line that is very satisfying, and consistent. What I'm used to is a pen that can produce thick and thin lines in the same stroke. With this pen I find myself laying down thick lines, then going back over them and refining the lines to look like it was a thick and thin stroke.My opinion is that it is a good marker. I love the thin body style, and the paint flow is remarkably premium. I love that the set comes in such a nice organizational travel/ storage case and as always Ohuhu's Colors just seem to be so dramatic and satisfying. Actually, I think that is what I like best about this pen. The colors are vivid and beautiful. Compared to other acrylic markers, Ohuhu's colors just seem to pop more, are more precise and opaque on the first coat.On the note of how I feel about the tips?I think I've settled with this marker, I can say that I suggest them but I will also say just be ready for a little bit of a curve ball if you're used to another brand. The brush tips are just slightly different than competitors and maybe you will like them. My conclusion on the tips is that they are niche and have function, I consider it to be a tool whereas because it is different it is valuable. This marker can and does become usable for certain detail situations.Overall, I will say this is a good pen. I think that most people are going to be satisfied with them. I've been a little nit picky about the tips, but I am an artist and things like this that appear to me will probably appear to other artists, so as a reviewer I want to make note of them.Great marker and highly suggested.

Sentence: This would make a perfect Plein Air sketch set, so light and easy to use.Inside, there is a multilingual instruction booklet and 3 swatch cards.
Content: This 24-piece acrylic paint pen kit is a blast--and at a little over $1 a pen, it gives you a lot of entertainment hours for your buck!The set comes in a beautifully decorated hardcover case, with the name "Ohuhu" (leaf in the 'O'), and drawings of leaves, flowers, stars, cactus, a cute gecko, peaceful dove, and other geometrics, designed to inspire, printed on the front in white. The back has Ohuhu's motto, "Draw. Feel. Empower." and a bunch of legal data printed on it. The zipper on the case moves very smoothly, and each pen has its own velcro loop to hold it secure in travel. This would make a perfect Plein Air sketch set, so light and easy to use.Inside, there is a multilingual instruction booklet and 3 swatch cards. 1 swatch card is filled out and has a white background, and there are also two blanks: one white and one black. I encourage you to fill both of these out, first, to prime your pens and get them ready to do an art, and second, so you can notice how the different background colors affect the perceived color of the pens. Even though you are using the exact same color on both cards, the final outcome looks VERY different. After that, you're ready to go!The colors of the paint are opaque, provided you let the bottom colors dry before adding more on top. This takes maybe a minute. You can also blend the colors just a bit by working two colors together quickly, but be careful that you don't foul and muddy your pen tips.Protip: if you've treated your item with gesso (highly recommended), you can blend, work, and even dilute the colors with a damp brush and a little water, allowing you to create watercolor-like effects or blend and smooth sharp lines. The gesso protects your item from the water and smooths the surface in order to accept the paint more readily. It's fairly cheap and available here on Amazon. Think of it as primer, except for art!These pens may not be as versatile as a full acrylic paint set, but neither are they as expensive or as messy. For a more advanced artist, these pens make a great color sketch set so you can get ideas down in the books quickly and conveniently, then you can use your full acrylic or oil paint set to make a full final copy. These paints are great for casual artists or smaller multimedia art projects such as rock painting or just adding a few quick touches to a knitting or sewing project. Not everybody wants or needs to bother with a full paint kit. These pens are also great for card-making and stencils. I'm sure there's a ton of other uses I've forgotten, or don't have the wit to imagine. 10/10, versatile, affordable, and FUN.

The price is good and the actual ink seems to be good quality even if the pens themselves have some design flaws.

Unfortunately about half of the pens came partially exploded in the cap. Not a huge deal because they are perfectly functional and the ink spillar was contained inside the cap, but you will want to be careful uncapping them unless you are ok with getting permanent ink splatters on your clothing. The ink does separate when not in use, so you will want to shake them well before using them again. The price is good and the actual ink seems to be good quality even if the pens themselves have some design flaws.

Sentence: The packaging is very nice, definitely giftable for someone starting out.
Content: On sale for $24, I think they're worth it. The packaging is very nice, definitely giftable for someone starting out. They are very pigmented and need zero time priming. Sentence: Good flow, enough colors accent anything, but no true red, IMHO.___I debated how to rate these.
Content: Good flow, enough colors accent anything, but no true red, IMHO.___I debated how to rate these. The paint itself, the case and the markers are all fine and worthy of a 4-5 rating. The issue I found were the colors themselves.___Now judging color on monitors is tough, no doubt about it--what you see and what I see may differ in our homes, and what the item actually is can be different than the image taken by the vendor. I am deducting 1 star because I believe that in a set of 24, there should be at least one of each primary color hue that is free of other hues. Here, in particular, the red that is of an orange leaning, and the blues were just okay.___So how can I show you? I took every color marker (except for black/white) and put a streak on the MAKER'S color chart and took a photo to show you the variance. My streak is going OVER the side of the color printed, and upwards. When wet, there was a huge variance, but when dry, the variance was less. This photo was taken a week after I made the marks. This way, while you can't know how close my image and your monitor are to reality, you CAN see how the actual colors vary from the maker's color chart.___I really hope this review helped you in some way.

Sentence: Overall, these seem to be quality markers and when these are eventually used up or dry out, we will likely replace them and keep a set around.
Content: I’m not an artist, but we keep some art supplies around for my daughter’s school projects. We tried these out on a coloring page and were pleased with the results. Colors are vibrant and they require no pressure to the paper so it almost feels like painting. These will definitely get use in our house. I also tried these out on an aluminum plant tag. We ordered these tags by mistake as we usually get ones that you can easily etch writing into. I let it dry and then left it out in a torrential downpour for three days and even when I rubbed it with a dry paper towel, it was mostly intact. Sharpies do not hold up at all on these metal tags, so now we have a way to use these tags up. Overall, these seem to be quality markers and when these are eventually used up or dry out, we will likely replace them and keep a set around.

Sentence: They do take a bit to dry, but I don't expect paint pens to dry quickly.
Content: This review is for the set of 24 Ohuhu Acrylic Paint Markers with the brush tip. I absolutely love these paint pens! They come organized in a case that fits them snugly, and has a carry strap you can tuck in or pull out as needed. Each color is labeled on the paint cap. The paint cap tip and end of the marker are color-coded so they don't get mixed up. The caps also have a small ridge ro keep them from rolling away, and snap so you know they're closed tightly. The side has a window so you know how much paint is left. You need to shake them well and the bonus is you can also tell how well the paint is mixed by looking at the window. There is a mixing bead inside but some colors take more shaking than others to fully blend (like purples and grays). They come with swatch sheets in black & white as well as a printed swatch sheet. I'm glad they included the swatch sheets for you to make yourself because some of the colors came out lighter than the printed sheet. They write really smoothly and you can write slower to make sure the color is fully opaque if you don't want to wait for it to dry and do two coats. They do take a bit to dry, but I don't expect paint pens to dry quickly. Overall, I highly recommend these markers. They work so well and on top of that, this is a great price for 24 markers.

Sentence: This is a review for "SHARPIE Creative Markers, Earth Tones, Water-Based Acrylic Markers, Bullet Tip, Assorted Colors, 12 Count, Everything The Light Touches Is Your Canvas, In celebration of Disney’s Mufasa: The Lion King"This set is a compliment to the vibrant set of pens Sharpie released in this new series of paint pens.
Content: This is a review for "SHARPIE Creative Markers, Earth Tones, Water-Based Acrylic Markers, Bullet Tip, Assorted Colors, 12 Count, Everything The Light Touches Is Your Canvas, In celebration of Disney’s Mufasa: The Lion King"This set is a compliment to the vibrant set of pens Sharpie released in this new series of paint pens.  I don't know how this magic works, but these pens do not bleed through paper, yet they very much behave like acrylic paint once they are dry.The pens do not blend very well with each other, so these would be good for projects where you were not trying to create a gradient effect.All of the pen bodies are very well made, the caps are easy to get on/off and the caps to stack or post on the end of the pen.In my opinion, if you could only afford one set of these pens, I would go for the "vibrant" set as this set of earth tones does not give you a rainbow of colors (unless you want an earth-toned rainbow.) There is also no black or white in this set.  This set is a terrific compliment to the vibrant set and the two sets combined, give you a ton of flexibility in creating and coloring.I would describe the tip as a large bullet. These will not be your best option for super small detailed drawing or coloring. They will work wonderfully for larger areas.Three blues, two greens, two purples, one brown, three oranges and a yellow is your pallet.

Sentence: The colors are vibrant and there is a great variety!
Content: These markers are the best! They have two sides on each end, one with a broad stroke that covers a large surface area and one with a fine point tip for precision coloring. The broad tip is able to cover so much surface area so quickly, with a great feel that is much different from traditional non-acrylic markers. The colors are vibrant and there is a great variety! There is a color chart on the back of the box that helps you find the colors you want easily by the cap numbers which are present on both sides. My kids use them all the time, these are their favorite markers. They don’t dry out easily, in fact we lost one of the caps and the color still works, after about 2 weeks without it! The lost color of the cap that was lost is not as prominent as the other colors that have a cap but it is definitely still useful. They wash away with soap and water and they hold their colors extremely well on multiple types of paper. Love them.

Sentence: Secondly, not ALL the colors are metallic.
Content: I specifically chose this 72-count set because I am looking for a colors that span the spectrum. This set has numerous colors that are so close they are practically the same, while also completely omitting basic colors. There is not a "true green" in this set. Several teals, two limey greens and a very light mint green, but no basic green. There is an excessive amount of browns- yellow browns, red browns, bronzes, etc.Also, almost all colors have a pearlized, metallic sheen. First, this set was not advertised as metallic. I already have several and was specifically looking for a matte set. Secondly, not ALL the colors are metallic. In general, wouldn't use metallic and not metallic markers together on the same project, so after separating them by finish, I now have two smaller sets of markers with huge gaps in colors. I am not at all pleased. This set was a complete waste of money.As far as the quality of the markers go, they're fine. They all write well. This set should be aimed at small children or people who do not care about color selection.Lastly, the packaging is super flimsy. The marker caps get caught on the paperboard sheets separating the rows, so you have to wrestle the markers out. Also, the carton bows, so the markers bunch together and fall to the bottom of the carton. It's not fun to try to dig them out. I will need to provide my own reusable storage. Would not recommend!!

Sentence: It's not a big issue, but for some reason I like names with the colors.The colors lay down cleanly and I have not experienced any bleed/bleed through from these pens which is really nice.
Content: A nice collection of 48 dual tip acrylic markers that are perfect for your everyday arts and crafts or even the professional. The tips are either a brush style tip or a fine point and with the collection you will receive a small pack of spare tips for both styles. I am not sure how you might replace them as I have not had to do so, but it seems you would simply pull out the old one and place in the new one small end first.One issue I have with these markers is they are not "named" by color. While the caps will indicate the expected color they will lay down, none have a name other than the number on the caps. There is a color card that comes with the pack and you can color in the box for each corresponding pen to know what to expect. It's not a big issue, but for some reason I like names with the colors.The colors lay down cleanly and I have not experienced any bleed/bleed through from these pens which is really nice. The color selection is decent with about an equal mix of darker shades/tones vs lighter ones. I typically prefer to have it skew to the lighter side of the spectrum but these are fine.The brush tip allows you to really vary your lines from as fine as you can make one to a good solid line while the fine tip is just that. I enjoy coloring and creating mandalas, and these work quite well for that purpose. Especially when coloring some of the more intricate designs. Having the fine point allows me to get in the super fine details while not ruining the piece with bleeding/bleed through.The pricing on these is perfect at $15.98 for 48 markers. That really is a good price with what you are getting. These are perfect for the budding artist in your home or for everyday use in projects.

Sentence: As is, 48 dual-tipped markers that work well for around $15 is a good price.
Content: This is a great set of acrylic markers for amateur artists (maybe even professional, which I am not.) There are 48 different colors, with a brush tip on one end and a fine tip on the other. The paint goes down smoothly on many types of surfaces; they worked well for me on paper, glass, and rocks. Each marker is numbered, and they come with a card marked with numbered squares for testing the colors. I colored half of each square with the brush, and the second half with the fine tip, and now I have a great reference card for what each color will actually look like once dry. The set also includes two extra replacement fine tips and two extra brush tips. I have never tried replacing marker tips and I am hesitant to try, for fear of ruining a good marker; but I will try one out if any of the tips become damaged.The markers were not in the box in numbered order when they arrived. I took a few minutes to put them in numerical order, and soon realized that they seemed to be numbered randomly. For instance, one shade of red will not be consecutively numbered next to other shades of red, but instead is randomly placed amongst other colors. So I abandoned the numbering system altogether and arranged them by color.The markers come in a box of thin cardstock that won’t stand the test of time. I would have preferred a sturdier case, but then the price would have had to be higher. As is, 48 dual-tipped markers that work well for around $15 is a good price.

Sentence: Secondly, not ALL the colors are metallic.
Content: I specifically chose this 72-count set because I am looking for a colors that span the spectrum. This set has numerous colors that are so close they are practically the same, while also completely omitting basic colors. There is not a "true green" in this set. Several teals, two limey greens and a very light mint green, but no basic green. There is an excessive amount of browns- yellow browns, red browns, bronzes, etc.Also, almost all colors have a pearlized, metallic sheen. First, this set was not advertised as metallic. I already have several and was specifically looking for a matte set. Secondly, not ALL the colors are metallic. In general, wouldn't use metallic and not metallic markers together on the same project, so after separating them by finish, I now have two smaller sets of markers with huge gaps in colors. I am not at all pleased. This set was a complete waste of money.As far as the quality of the markers go, they're fine. They all write well. This set should be aimed at small children or people who do not care about color selection.Lastly, the packaging is super flimsy. The marker caps get caught on the paperboard sheets separating the rows, so you have to wrestle the markers out. Also, the carton bows, so the markers bunch together and fall to the bottom of the carton. It's not fun to try to dig them out. I will need to provide my own reusable storage. Would not recommend!!

Sentence: These pens are similar to other markers, but the acrylic goes on smoothly and dries fairly quickly (not quite as fast as other markers).
Content:
These pens are similar to other markers, but the acrylic goes on smoothly and dries fairly quickly (not quite as fast as other markers).  The coverage is much better than regular markers and you can fill a lot of space without having to go over areas repeatedly.  It also does not bleed through paper, even lightweight paper.
It may be just a bit messier than some markers because it takes a bit longer to dry, but it cleans up easily with soap and water.
It also goes on pretty much any surface.
I liked that they have both broad and fine tip markers in the set.
The selection of colors is good, but could have used a few more colors like a brighter green and blue.
One other difference with standard markers is the ability to color over things that you have already colored.
I used these with the kids and they loved it.  The exceptional  coverage really makes a difference. Definitely a winner!

Sentence: These water-based acrylic markers are well-designed, both in function and appearance.
Content:
These water-based acrylic markers are well-designed, both in function and appearance. The sleek bodies and caps have a clean, aesthetic look, with a handy color indicator line on each cap to match the ink inside. They write smoothly with excellent paint coverage, and I was impressed that they required no shaking or priming before use. The included video was recorded immediately upon receiving with zero shaking or priming done.

Per the product’s recommendation, they should be stored horizontally to maintain their ability to write immediately without priming. They claim to work on a variety of surfaces, from canvas to wood and rock.

At the time of review, they are priced at $40 for a 24-pack, which isn’t cheap, but the quality and user experience reflect that higher-end pricing. If you’re looking for a smooth-writing acrylic marker set, these seem to deliver.

Sentence: These Sharpie water-based acrylic markers are everything I expected from the Sharpie brand!
Content:
These Sharpie water-based acrylic markers are everything I expected from the Sharpie brand!  They are just as described---no shaking the pen and pushing down for a long time to get the acrylic flowing...just color.
I did two coats on house paint and it turned out pretty good. I was careful to not rest my hand on the wet paint, so didn't experience any smearing.  It did dry fairly fast, as acrylic is known for.  Long lasting, so far.
I like that there's a set of fine and a set of brush nib.

Sentence: These are pricey for acrylic markers, but I guess you’re paying for the Sharpie brand name.
Content: These are pricey for acrylic markers, but I guess you’re paying for the Sharpie brand name. The ink flows well and has good coverage; it looks great on black paper. I think the tips are pretty good quality. Just be aware that you’re buying 12 brush tip markers and 12 bullet tip markers, not 24 markers with dual tips — which I think was sort of an odd choice. The brush tips and bullet tips come in different colors, which is kinda weird to me but I’m glad to have 24 colors as opposed to just 12 repeated twice. Some of the colors are fairly similar to each other, which isn’t ideal to me with a set of 24. Overall, while these are perfectly serviceable markers I don’t feel the brand name makes them worth the price when you can easily find much larger sets of other brands for cheaper.

Sentence: Plenty of colors to choose from and a nice box to hold them in.
Content:
I'm probably using these in a way that most people will not, but they work perfect for my application.  I'm a model railroader and like to customize rolling stock and buildings.  Sometimes I just need a quick bit of color here or there, and to get my paint bottles out, see if I even have the color and go through the process of a quick touchup and then clean brushes, well, admittedly most of the time I simply pass with the idea "I'll get it next time when I need to paint more touchups at once."  Yeah, that never seems to happen.

These have worked perfect for quick touchups or for painting tiny little details.  The kit came with what I consider a broad brush tip and a finer brush tip marker choice.  They work just like a marker, but it's more like paint than ink.  Plenty of colors to choose from and a nice box to hold them in.  The finer tip markers even include white and gray — a very nice touch!

If I had to be picky, the only gripe I might mention is while the caps show the particular color the marker is, it would be nice if the color were larger and even wrapped around the cap.  Trying to find the color I need isn't hard, but not a quick visual reference if you know what I mean.  But that's just me being picky.  One could simply "paint" the color around the cap if it were necessary.

The photo is of a recent project I finished.  The yellow fine-tip paint marker was used to "paint" the steps and ladder on the crane and also the hooks on the boom (boom hooks were then weathered with chalks).  Simple, fast and easy.  No brushes to clean.

Sentence: The water-based acrylic ink flows smoothly, and the colors are vibrant and opaque, even on dark paper.
Content:
I love that this set comes with different tip sizes, so I can experiment with fine details and bold strokes. The water-based acrylic ink flows smoothly, and the colors are vibrant and opaque, even on dark paper. I’ve tried them on paper, canvas, and even wood, and they worked great on all surfaces.

One thing to note is that some colors take a couple of layers to be fully opaque, but that’s expected with water-based markers. Also, shaking and priming the pens before use is necessary, but once you get the hang of it, it’s easy.

Overall, this is a fantastic set for beginners like me who want to explore acrylic markers without spending too much. I highly recommend them for anyone getting into painting or mixed media!

Sentence: PRO's: -good coverage and flow -a nice variety of colors -includes two different tip ends for your needs CON's: -they don't have to be primed, that seems strange to me and I question longevity as well as settling of paint.
Content:
Sharpie is a trustable brand, so I didn't hesitate to order these acrylic markers.  For me, acrylic markers are the perfect supply for rock painting and with a young granddaughter, we do a lot of that around here.

PRO's:
-good coverage and flow
-a nice variety of colors
-includes two different tip ends for your needs

CON's:
-they don't have to be primed, that seems strange to me and I question longevity as well as settling of paint.
-there is only ONE white (bullet tip) my favorite and most used color.  There should be a white in both size tips
-my red had already leaked prior to opening the box
-cost is much higher than comparable sets.

All in all, a 4 star product for me but I will look elsewhere in the future due to high price and non-priming nature.

Sentence: They go on smoothly and they layer nicely.
Content:
I was expecting a lot from these SHARPIE acrylic markers, mostly due to the name brand and the steep asking price. They are good quality acrylic markers. They go on smoothly and they layer nicely. You can layer lighter colors on top of darker ones, provided that you allow drying time in between.
There are 12 of each kind of tip, different colors in each, for a pretty decent variety of color/tip options.
These are fun to use and the colors are great.
Price wise, you are paying for the name here. There are other brands of acrylic markers that work just as well for less than half the cost. These are nice and do everything you would expect, and the box is sturdy enough you can easily store them inside. But I do have to knock off a star in my rating because of the high cost.

-------------
Pros:

* The dot tip is surprisingly handy if you have trouble making perfect circles by hand, like most people do. XD

* The paint flows easily, so the markers move smoothly. That specifically makes them good for painting, writing, and detail work.

* The acrylic "ink" is easily layered, doesn't bleed (even on paper), and works well on multiple surfaces, which makes it a fantastic tool for craft projects.

* The paint dries quickly.

* The pens -don't- dry out quickly.

* There's no strong smell.

-------------
Meh:
* The markers come in a range of pastel and medium colors with only a few dark and metallic colors. If that's what you're looking for, you're golden. If not, you won't buy these anyway, so it doesn't matter. :)

* The marker colors are named AND numbered, making finding replacements quick and easy. However, this is only true on the back of the box, NOT on the pens themselves, so you'll need to keep the list on the box / take a picture of it / whatever if you want that information.

* They suffer the same issues as using acrylic paints... because they ARE acrylic paints.

For example, the markers work on smooth surfaces like glass and plastic, but when you try to paint over a part that you've already painted, there's a chance that it will remove the paint on these surfaces instead of adding more (Sharpies and dry erase markers do this, too). And sometimes the lighter colors will be a little see-through, and might take multiple coats to fully cover a surface.

These are very common paint issues, but people sometimes seem to forget that acrylic markers are paint, not traditional markers, and as such, they act like paint. XD

-------------
Cons:
* None! At least, not yet. :)

-------------
With the quality, versatility, and variety of these paint markers, $30 for 80 markers ($0.38 each) is an absolute STEAL, even considering that you're getting less paint with each marker than is standard.

And even with taking the lack of replacement options into account, if given the choice, I would choose to order these again. The color variety is just too good to pass up. :)

I hope that this helps! :D

Sentence:
Pros:
-GREAT, vivid colors, without being blinding!
Content:
Pros:
-GREAT, vivid colors, without being blinding! lovely.
-bought the 30 pc set, so big variety

Conclusion: absolutely lovely colors, not the full spectrum, and waterproof quality yet to be determined

Sentence: These are decent acrylic markers, but definitely not professional level artist's paint pens.
Content:
These are decent acrylic markers, but definitely not professional level artist's paint pens. They go on smoothly and dry quickly. No issues with bleeding or smearing, but make sure you give a couple seconds to dry on metal or glass before touching. Each pen has a fine tip and a ball tip (great for doing dots for mandalas). Colors aren't as vibrant as oil markers, on some surfaces colors will be muted. For the purpose of this review, did some dot patterns on wood and many of the purples and pinks looked the same. Layering works great, darker over lighter, but not the other way around. Lighter colors are lost on the darker backgrounds.

Still, these would be great for a variety of crafts and projects. Very cost-effective for kids as well.

Content: I like the size of this kit. The sixty markers give you so many colors to work with. Notably, there are a few colors so similar they would be hard to tell apart. There is a color chart on the box but I couldn’t find any matching numbers on the markers. I guess it doesn’t matter as you can only use one marker at a time and you have to replace the cap immediately before going on to another color or it could dry out. Sentence:
simply uncap and go to town
- The caps click when closing so you know it’s firmly capped (some other markers have dried on me when I inadvertently did not put on the caps tight enough)
- While it’s waterproof on surfaces, it washes off clean from your hands.
- Good price point.

So why not 5 stars?
Content:
I am NOT an artist - I am a crafter and, therefore, my review is based on how I would use these paint markers. There’s a lot to like:
- There’s a nice variety of colors though some of are subtle variations
- The bullet (or dot) end is a nice bullet point, which will be good for mandala painting (for me, on river rocks)
- You can get a pretty fine line with the fine tip
- You don’t have to do a lot prep just to get started (e.g., pressing down nibs, waiting for paint to appear, etc.); simply uncap and go to town
- The caps click when closing so you know it’s firmly capped (some other markers have dried on me when I inadvertently did not put on the caps tight enough)
- While it’s waterproof on surfaces, it washes off clean from your hands.
- Good price point.

So why not 5 stars? Well…these might be minor to some, but for me, I was kind of “meh”:
- The colors are in no way labeled. Yes, you can see the color from the cap BUT, as I mentioned, a couple colors are very similar. I swatched all but one pen, but because there’s no number or name, I can’t figure out which one I missed.
- I do like a solid, clicking cap. However, there was an inconsistency - some caps were fine and easy to open; a few were on so tightly, it was a struggle to open. By the time I got one or two uncapped, I was grumpy.
- The coverage is okay, not super-duper. To get a good opaque coverage, you have to wait for one layer of color to dry then go over it. Not a big deal, but the white could be whiter. The silver and gold are nice but my other acrylic metallic markers are more shimmery/shiny. Again, not a bit deal.

Overall, for the number of pens, the quality of the color, and the price point, this is a good purchase - at least from a crafter’s perspective.

Sentence: My last set of acrylic markers would bleed through the pages of my sketchbooks, so I had to keep a page between designs to ensure the markers didn't ruin other pictures.

Sentence: The twelve glitter inks are quite vibrant colors and the glitter effect works well.
Content:
These are very good pens for crafting, creating artistic effect or just fancy writing.  The twelve glitter inks are quite vibrant colors and the glitter effect works well.  Although described as Extra-Fine Tip, remember that for this type of pen the line will still be quite wide, about .7mm so more like a fine point.  You need to 'charge' the ink by shaking the pen well and pressing the nib on a piece of scrap paper multiple times before the ink covers the nib.
Personally, I recommend gently cleaning the ink off the nib after each use and ensuring the cap is on tightly to help prolong the life of the pen.  Otherwise, it will 'gunk' up and dry out rendering the pen unusable.
Good product, great for crafters, artists , schools etc and worth the cost.

Sentence: I love that these are water based and don’t have any strong smell either while using or when dried.
Content:
All 12 glitter markers work well and are so vibrant.  I love that these are water based and don’t have any strong smell either while using or when dried.  When priming each marker, I noticed some seemed a tad bit more watery than others, so be cautious when allowing younger children to prime the markers upon first use.  I ended up with a small puddle with a few of the colors.  Also, I would use a thicker paper or adult coloring book with a paper separating any other drawings, as they do bleed through a bit.
Overall, they dried nicely and fairly quickly on paper.  When you are first coloring with them, it’s hard to see the glitter, but after it dries, you clearly see a glittery sheen.  I used this to label some clear cups and they worked nicely for that, but did take a while to dry and the glitter was less noticeable on the plastic.
The pens themselves seem like a very nice quality, with a sturdy plastic and a cap that snaps on very well.  I used the markers after a few days of opening them and they were working as new.
The price seems fair for the nice quality and for the 12 vibrant colors.

Sentence: The paint is too thin (to help the flow?), flat and chalky.
Content:
I chose this set because I wanted to paint some rocks. I followed the directions and shook each color before use.  The paint is too thin (to help the flow?), flat and chalky. I buy and use a lot of art supplies. I painted the first rock partially white (base for a rocky mountain goat) and after 3 layers the paint is still thin. I painted the second rock black. After letting it dry layer by layer; I started painting flowers on the surface. Again adding 3 or 4 layers to deepen the colors of the petals, letting the paint dry in between. The added colors soaked up the black base paint making the flowers muddy. The end result was a "faded" look.
I painted on paper where it did better.
I would not recommend this paint set if you wanted to use it for anything other than paper - and do not mind the lack of vibrancy, and thinness.

Sentence: I have not used them a lot, so I don't know how long they last.
Content:
I spent many years as a professional graphic, commercial and fine artist, mostly graphic. So my opinion may not really fit with the average person who would use these paints. I think the average person who will buy acrylic paints will like them, because they are used to using acrylics, and are not as picky as I am about precise colors. the paint is acrylic, so it does what acrylic paint does. The best thing about them is The tips. They are amazing. They are not a felt tip, they are a brush tip, so you can make a tiny line by touching very lightly, or wider depending on the pressure you put on the tips, all the way to a really wide line by laying it a little sideways. no need to have double tip, and as far as I can tell, they do not moosh down and loose their sharp point. I have not used them a lot, so I don't know how long they last. The paint dries very quickly, so it will be important to click the lids fully on, each time you quit using one, even for a few minutes.

The reasons I gave this a 3 star rating is that  a) at least one of the most standard colors I would use a lot, and is critical for painting plants or flowers is not included. There is a good light green, but no dark green, and the middle green, is not a good standard green. In my opinion it is a little too blue to look right on green leaves. Unfortunately, you cannot blend acrylics, so you cannot create your own colors, which is why acrylics are not my favorite type of paint. b) these are more expensive than most of the other acrylic paint sets I saw on Amazon, so I don't think it is a good value (one set has 72 colors for about the same price.)

Sentence: These, however, work on every surface, they have plenty of paint/ink, and the COLORS ACTUALLY MATCH the caps that go on the markers.
Content:
I have tried so many different paint markers and either the colors are wrong, the tips of them are easily destroyed, they don’t have enough paint/ink in them, or they only work on some surfaces and not others.  These, however, work on every surface, they have plenty of paint/ink, and the COLORS ACTUALLY MATCH the caps that go on the markers.  They also come packaged very nice.

One thing that I really liked about these markers is that they come ready to use.  You don’t have to press down and wait a minute or so for the paint/ink to come to the tip of the marker.  That also means that you don’t have to occasionally press down on the marker to get the paint/ink flowing.  For those of you who use paint markers on a regular basis, you know what a pain that can be.

The only reason I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 is because it’s very difficult to draw thin lines with these.  If you move very slow, you might be able to make a thin line.  I’m not sure if that’s worth losing a whole star considering all of the other pros, but it won’t allow me to take away 1/4 or 1/2.

I highly recommend this product!!!!

Sentence: I got them to play with in my art journal, and they have been perfect for that use.
Content: I’m very happy with these acrylic paint markers. I got them to play with in my art journal, and they have been perfect for that use. The paint flows out steadily and evenly. There were no blobs of paint and no waiting for the paint to flow, either. Just nice, even strokes of paint. The paint can’t be too thick in pens, or it wouldn’t work, but the paint isn’t so thin that it’s transparent. Some of the colors are a little more opaque than others depending on how quickly your hand is during the application of the paint. Layering a second coat would be easy enough for that, though, should it be a problem. For me, it wasn’t. I’m not using these for my canvases. It’s just for my journal. I feel like this set of acrylic markers is a fabulous bargain at the current price of $15.99. I very highly recommend them.

Sentence: These markers are vibrant, smooth, and packed with ink—no weak streaky lines here.
Content: I received this set of paint markers for free through the Amazon Vine program, and I’ve been happily doodling on everything that’ll sit still long enough. These markers are vibrant, smooth, and packed with ink—no weak streaky lines here. Whether I’m decorating a notebook or turning a boring stone into a tiny masterpiece, they handle it like champs.They work well on a surprising number of surfaces—paper, glass, pottery, even the random seashell I found in a drawer. The ink dries quickly and doesn’t smear, which is ideal for impatient artists (like me) who inevitably poke at their work too soon. I also appreciate that there’s no awful chemical smell, so I can craft indoors without worrying about fumigating the place.If you’re looking to add a pop of color to your next creative project—or just want an excuse to draw on things like a grown-up child—this set is a fun and easy way to do it. Bonus: now my rock collection has more personality than some people I know.

Sentence: You just shake it up a bit, pop off the cap and you're good to go!So far the brush tips have held up to repeated use and have kept their shape.
Content: This 18 pack of acrylic pens by The Best Crafts is perfect for painting rocks, crafts, or whatever you'd like to easily paint with acrylics! While these are like the "shake up" pens, they have a soft nylon tip so you don't have to keep it pressed down to get the paint to saturate the nib (aka priming) which I personally hate. You just shake it up a bit, pop off the cap and you're good to go!So far the brush tips have held up to repeated use and have kept their shape. The paint itself is very pigmented and opaque, they blend decently, and they can be easily layered after they dry (see my photo). These are definitely one of my favorite sets I've ever had and I highly recommend them!

Sentence: The colors are vivid, and they go on smoothly.
Content: Overall, these are nice acrylic markers. The colors are vivid, and they go on smoothly. The color variation is decent, but some colors like red and yellow have few options on shades. Conversely, there are a ton of greens and blues. There are also 3 metallic shades... silver, gold, and black. Some colors are more opaque than others, while some seem to have thinner paint and streak a bit. I've only tried them on paper, so I can't speak to how they work on other materials. I was specifically looking for a brand that had brush tip and fine tip, and these fit the bill. They are great for large areas, as well as finer details. I'm sure I will get a lot of use out of these!

Sentence: It doesn't eem to smudge once it is dry, but you will need to be careful until it is dry because it will definitely streak when it is still wet.
Content: I have tried these markers on paper, cardboard, and faux leather so far and they have written very smoothly on each. I tried them on both black and white paper and the writing showed up well on both. The cardboard was more like a paperboard, but the markers showed up well and wrote smoothly on that too. It doesn't eem to smudge once it is dry, but you will need to be careful until it is dry because it will definitely streak when it is still wet. Fortunately, it does dry quickly, so you won't have to wait long for whatever you use it on to be safe to handle. The markers seem like they should work on almost any surface and I really like the assortment of colors. I haven't tried them on any fabrics that I might wash yet, and I don't see any mention of care for fabrics that you use them on, so I don't know if they can be washed.

Sentence: Overall these are priced well, have dual tips and vibrant colors.
Content:

These can be used on fabric, paper, wood and rocks as well as other materials like glass and plant pots but I definitely recommend that most of these get sprayed or coated with some kind of sealant especially if used outside or around water. The tips are smooth and the paint goes on easily. They never drip, splat or clog. Colors are vibrant and have a great opaqueness to them so you don't have to layer to cover. However, depending on the material you use , you may have to apply a second coat.

Overall these are priced well, have dual tips and vibrant colors. definitely quality markers.

Sentence: She is a huge fan of a youtuber that I won't name, but this youtuber introduced my daughter to an expensive product that she loves to use frequently: the Posca paint marker.
Content:
My daughter the aspiring artist is constantly working on some sort of artwork or craft project. She is a huge fan of a youtuber that I won't name, but this youtuber introduced my daughter to an expensive product that she loves to use frequently: the Posca paint marker.

Posca makes (as far as I know) the premiere go-to paint marker and they are not cheap. When I saw these being offered, I figured they were worth giving a try and worst case scenario I figured I could at least convince her to use these less expensive markers on her less important projects or for "practice" before using the pricey markers. Either way, when I gave these to her she was much more excited than I expected and was very happy to have this new big set of markers.

She used them for the first time not too long after she got them and loves them. She says they are almost exactly like her Poscas and likes that these have different tips on each side. She said she still prefers using the Posca but that these are really close. Myself, looking at things she has used the markers on, I really can't tell any difference in quality of the paint itself. It looks vibrant and bold.

Honestly I can't think of any negatives to mention. These are high quality paint markers that work well and look great. The price point is excellent compared to premium brands with the product itself performing just as well. Highly recommend to
artists and other parents of artists.

Sentence: Overall, the pens are a joy to use.
Content:
As long as you shake these paint markers before using, they work great. I love that you can layer light colors over dark ones. I am extremely sensitive to chemicals, and these have nothing in them that triggers my allergies.

They have two tips, a blunt one for wide strokes and a pointy one for variable line width. I personally could not control the line width of the pointy tip, but I imagine that someone with good fine motor control could. So it's not really great for super detail work, because if you accidentally press a little too hard, the pen will create a wide stroke instead of thin.

There are just a couple of minor things I think could have been designed better. To tell which tip is which without removing the caps, you need to read the fine print on the middle section of the pen. It would have been nice if they made the caps different to make it more obvious. Also, the box doesn't work great for storage. You have to dig around to get the pens out, and they don't always go back in easily.

These detractions are minor. Overall, the pens are a joy to use.

Sentence: Only one of the colors required a little touch up in my swatch book to get full coverage.
Content:
I'm normally a brand snob, enjoying only the finest of my curated art tools and wanting nothing but the best for what I create in my sketchbook. However, even though I hadn't heard of this brand before, I was really surprised by the quality of their markers. Compared to POSCA and Arrtx, these are closer to POSCA in terms of vibrancy. They pop off the page, plus they went on very smooth and opaque. Only one of the colors required a little touch up in my swatch book to get full coverage.

One huge selling point (and a gripe I have about most brands of markers/pens) is that these markers are labeled/numbered on both ends. Again, this is huge. I never understood why Arrtx made you put stickers on their paint markers and try to eyeball which sticker went with which color. I very much appreciated Betem's simple design here and the ease of use to quickly identify what each color is, whether the marker is up or down.

Sentence: The pens are comfortable to hold and use.
Content: I ordered this paint pen set for the wide assortment of colors. I have other sets, but their colors are limited, especially with the pinks and greens. This set has an excellent selection and even some metallic colors, too. The pens are comfortable to hold and use. I prefer the round barrel than the square shape with rounded edges (like my other sets). I have more control with this set. Even though they don't have to be prepped before use, when you first use them, the paint is a bit lighter and gets a richer hue as you make more strokes. The coverage is pretty good, but you may need to go over your area more than once to get full coverage. I tried them on an unpainted vinyl doll head and a foam clay flower, and both pieces received the paint very well, but I did have to keep applying paint here and there to get a good coating. Overall, they're nice for hobbyists and crafters, but may not be up to professional standards. They come in a securely sewn storage pack that has a smoothly functioning zipper. The set doesn't have names or numbers for the individual pens, so it could get confusing trying to remember which shade you are supposed to be using. It would be much better if they were numbered, but it's a nice set and I recommend it for amateur artists, crafters, and as a much cleaner alternative to traditional paint and brush setups.

Content: I have used this brand before and I prefer these acrylic paint pens, so I opted for the 240 count to expand my color selection. Thankfully they all worked, and gave me all the variety packs except for #718 'Tumeric' from the 'Light skin' pack.These paint markers are fantastic and work on just about any surface I've tried them on. They last a decent amount and have replaceable nibs in case they get clogged or dried, which can happen on certain surfaces or excessively blending.My biggest gripe is that the included swatch page is not in any discernible order, and the only color chart with color names (also not in color or number order) is on the bottom of the box! Where are you supposed to put 240 markers to look at the bottom of the box? It took me HOURS to try to sort these by color.Now I want to add something for others that was driving me crazy: some of the color names were not translated properly. I had to do a fair amount of research to try to figure them out. They are as follows:755 xianchi red - maple red815 canghuang - dull yellow-brown817 juyi yellow - yellow gold746 fotou blue - "blue hour" or sunset blue710 changchun - long spring or eternal spring713 nelumbo red - lotus red699 felongrass purple - aka Masterwort or "star of beauty" plant purple657 bishan green - pavilion green or jade hills pavilion green636 bicheng blue - dust blue750 kongqing blue - Azurite blue739 ormosia - Red Bean Tree747 quetou blue - I couldn't figure this one out749 qingming blue - clear and bright748 tianqing blue - Sky blueI hope this helps if you care about color names.Tl;dr: These are great markers that work on a wide variety of materials that are opaque and vivid. Highly recommended if you are new to these types of markers or are looking to complete the color selection offered by Guangna.

Sentence: However, there are some issues that really brought the rating down.For one thing, I had one marker completed dried out.
Content: I wanted to give these four stars. After all, it’s 240 colors at a very fair price and the paint and color range is great. However, there are some issues that really brought the rating down.For one thing, I had one marker completed dried out. It was a fairly important one for the type of work I do but at least there are a few similar colors and 1/240 isn’t horrible.For another thing, some of the caps have dark writing on a dark cap so I have to really strain my eyes to see the numbers. Sometimes it’s so bad I have to use my phone’s flashlight to see what the numbers are. I wish they’d used white on those like they did most of the dark lids. I don’t know why they failed to do so in so many colors.The thing that bothers me most about the set is that the color numbers are totally out of order on the swatch card. So even if you manage to put them in order you’d never be able match them up quickly to the card. It took me about FOUR HOURS to swatch them all because I had to search and search for the appropriate number on the swatch card for every single marker. Why on earth couldn’t they have put them in numerical order on the swatch card or just given us an un-numbered card so we could write them in ourselves? This is the issue that lost them the star for me. It’s really, really frustrating.Overall it’s a beautiful set, but because of the swatch card issue I’ll have to totally redo the ordering of my entire set to try to put them into an order where I can halfway match them to the swatch sheet. What a hassle.

Content: I have had a need for acrylic markers.  Everyone in the family has different things they are doing, but I prefer we all have our own sets to use.  I got this one for our son who wanted a complete set for his 3D gaming projects which are extensive and intricate.BOXThe box with this set is GREAT.  It is a not hard to get the markers out, but they are not in order which makes doing the swatch sheet annoying and frustrating.  If you want to make the sheet easier to access markers from, you will need to put them in order yourself.SWATCH SHEETThankfully this comes with a really nice heavy duty paper swatch sheet.  It allows for really good swatches to be made for reference.MARKERSThe markers do not have color names, but each cap is marked with the color number.  There is a window in the side which allows you to see if the paint needs mixing, or if the levels are getting too low.  You can shake each one easily side to side, just don't go nuts with it.LEAKAGE?There was no leakage with these markers.  Flow was even and nice for almost all colors.COLORSThis is the most complete set of colors I have ever seen.  It is really nice and covers any type of project you can imagine.TIPSThere is a bag of replacement tips if you need one.PERFORMANCEThe performmance of these markers is really nice.  The colors are pretty decent, the application is smooth, and it allows for fine details or broader coverage.  I like these on paper and canvas a lot.  I am not as fond of them on glass or smooth plastic.  They tend to chip or scratch off if hit just right.ONE ISSUEI had no colors missing, but one of the colors has the tip put in backwards.  I haven't had the opportunity to change it around yet.THE BOTTOM LINEThis box is great, the swatch sheet is great, and the markers/pens are good performers.MY RATINGFIVE STARS.  This set of markers is a great collection.  None of th pens were dry, all of them worked well, and with the exception of the upside down tip they performed very well.  I highly suggest these, ,but use testing before doing a project to see how well it lasts on the surface you intend to use.DOES HE LIKE ITOur son really loves this set.  He is already opening up his 3D gaming manufacturing for his projects and enjyoing the flexibility that it allows for his textured plastic pieces and landscaping set ups.

Sentence: Set of 240 acrylic brush markers with bright fresh colors, smooth flow, and a window to show how much pigment is left.
Content: Set of 240 acrylic brush markers with bright fresh colors, smooth flow, and a window to show how much pigment is left. Includes a swatch card on Cold Press card stock, which is great except the numbers are chaotic. You have to do a 'Where's Waldo?' search for each number to match them up. It's probably easier and faster to use a blank sheet to swatch them, although you may not need swatches since you can see the color on the bristles when you open the cap.Great range of colors, which is helpful because acrylic brushes dry fast and aren't as easy to blend as watercolors or tube acrylics.The price is about $0.50 per pen and sometimes less when they have discounts.Very versatile and fun to use. You can paint on almost anything... stones, glass, plastic, rocks cardboard, metal, paper... just remember to shake them well first. My only complaint is the order of the numbers on the swatch card, but it's not concerning enough to take off a star. The paints themselves are good.

Sentence: All in all, I think this is a great set and a good value for the money.
Content: This is an amazing selection of colors - more than I have ever seen in a collection before.  I personally just grab a color in the general range of blue and test it to see if it is what I want to use.  I have read that others are totally frustrated by the fact that these paint brush-pens are not labeled and there is no semblance of order in the numbering.  But if you look at the colors on the outside top of the pen you have a pretty good idea of the hue and can experiment with the color.  I have rearranged mine in the box to generally group together the general color on a basic color wheel ( red, purple, blue, green, yellow, orange) and then the metallics and other odd ones out at the end.  This works perfectly well for me and happy with these.  I like the fact that the paint  dries appropriately fast allowing for layering without having to wait any length of time.  The only thing I don't love about(but don't hate) is the container these pens are in.  They are made of paper rather than held inside of a canvas holder like some other brands.  But perhaps this is the tradeoff for having the largest set I have ever owned.  All in all, I think this is a great set and a good value for the money.

Sentence: The quality is what I'm concerned about and I have yet to test to see if they are really waterproof.
Content: I love the variety of colors this set of brush acrylic markers offers. I've been using paint pens or acrylic markers for about 7 or 8 years. I used to buy them individually and pay through the nose. Then I started looking on Amazon because my granddaughter requested acrylic markers for Christmas. She loved mine and is my up-and-coming little artist. When I found the markers she requested and bought them I got to play with them too. They were great I wanted more. And I bought a few different brands that I say the quality is probably just as good as these are however I paid a lot more to get a lot less. And with these markers the variety is outstanding I'm always looking for more earthstone colors and different shades of red yellow green and brown.These markers are great. A rival to any high dollar marker set out there like Posca. You will have to have an outline marker because these are all brush tips. And I haven't found that they have any hard tip markers from 1 mm through 3 mm. Only the brush tip. But you can do so much with these and they are wonderful. They also supply you with extra tips which is phenomenal. So far I have enjoyed these markers. They do not come in order with the swatch card that they provide. Which was kind of a pain in the butt. However that's just a tiny little complaint. The quality is what I'm concerned about and I have yet to test to see if they are really waterproof. But I have another statue to paint and several signs to repaint that have been sun bleached over the years. So I will update if I need to on how they last outdoors. I have submitted a small cartoon that I sketched & painted just for this review, with the number markers provided. Just to show you how true the colors are. I am very pleased and excited to continue on my paint marker journey. And can I just say for the record paint markers are the best thing since sliced bread. They have changed the game. Well done thank you!

Sentence: The colors are vivid and there is pretty much every color you can think of.
Content: This is a beautiful set of paint markers. My daughter's and I have been using them every day since they arrived. All 3 of us took turns doing the swatches. Which was actually really fun - and a bit stressful at times.The numbering system of these paint markers is an absolute atrocity lol. I didn't remove any stars for the numbering because the markers themselves are great.The colors are numbered - from 600's - 900's. 6 and 9 are the two worst possible numbers you can use for a numbering tangible items. It's so easy to conflate one for the other. Some of these pens caps had little dots on them (either above or below the 6 or 9?!) since no one knows if the dot indicates up or down/top or bottom, it's essentially just a useless decorative mark above or below a 6 or a 9 lol.About halfway into the color chart, I started to see a pattern and deduced that the colors seem to be more organized by their secondary tones/color temperatures as opposed to primary. I also realized that most are grouped into similar colors, so you can look in the same color family as the previous one for the next number. However, when a new undertone section starts, you won't know - and good luck finding the numbered pen you're looking for at that point haha.Aside from the numbering nightmare lol, these are perfect. Every single one worked flawlessly and had a great flow. The colors are vivid and there is pretty much every color you can think of. I did notice that a few tips were more flexible than others. I definitely prefer the firmer ones are they are easier to control for smaller designs - which is mostly what I do.  This set also includes extra tips - which is appreciated.If your planning to buy this set of 240 paint pens, keep an eye on the price. When I acquired this, it was selling for close to $150. At the time of this review, it's selling for $118. If you break it down, it's like 50¢ per marker. Which is pretty reasonable compared to Posca. I think this set would make an awesome gift for anyone who loves art. My teenage daughter's and I have been painting rocks with these and they work beautifully for it. But there are so many applications for these besides just rocks. We are very happy with them and although the color swatching was a bit maddening, I really did enjoy the challenge of it.

Sentence: I would definitely see this as an investment at this price, I feel it's a really good price for what you're getting.
Content: I would definitely see this as an investment at this price, I feel it's a really good price for what you're getting. There are 240 acrylic markers in the set, so be prepared to spend some time getting them in order, because they do NOT come that way. Also, the numbers do not make any sense at all! There are some hundreds apart and then you'll come across the rare gem with a few in order (very few!)... But a treat when you're sorting this many. But it would be nice if these numbers meant anything at all versus the randomness that exists. I got over that annoyance, at least a little, by the fact that the lids are a very close match, if not exact, to the color you'll get on the swatch card. That's refreshing! There were only a few things I found during my long swatching and reorganizing session and those were as follows: 1) I found a weird black substance on one of the pens and later on the paper when one of the pieces fell off. No idea what it is, but it's pictured, 2) there was a visible "division" or splitting of the paint in the window of one of my markers. I don't know if it matters or if it's all mixed up in the end when you shake the pen each time?, 3) I had the felt from the end come off a few times while marking in the little swatch box. I can only imagine what this would do on a rough or large surface!! On one it came off in little pieces and ended up in/under the paint causing it to be all bumpy (see arrows in pic). The other few times it happened it was all one piece and while it did dull the tip slightly, it wasn't a huge enough chunk to make a big difference., and 4) the annoyance that this large set of 240 markers didn't come with a better divided box. It has thin dividers that are barely held in place by a notch and mine is broken. I don't know if it was already like that, but I don't know of it happening that I was aware of. It just makes it even harder to keep the pens in place while trying to sort them. And because they don't have they're own individual spot (or at min. their own rows) they move around every time you take one out, therefore causing a bit of an ordeal **everytime** you remove a marker and go to put it back in. This would've been eliminated had these been in a case where each marker has it's own spot. I don't need a headache each time I use these and I can see this making me not want to deal with them and choosing one of my other sets instead. Overall I think it's a good buy, but with 240 chances for something to go wrong, I only had a handful, so that's good. I felt it was worth about 3.5 stars sure to the issues (the biggest deduction because of the box not being properly divided bc it is a huge hassle) but since I can't do that, I gave 4.I tried to be as thorough as possible and include pictures so you could see for yourself what you'll receive (or potentially in the case of issues... Hopefully those are left out of your order!;)) But I hope you found it helpful. Take care and happy creating & painting!

Sentence: They're really juicy, but don't leak all over your work.
Content: I love these paint pens!  They're really juicy, but don't leak all over your work. There are so many colors! Of course when you get as large a selection as this, there's bound to be a few that are too close to tell them apart, but you'll find that in most large quantity paint pens. I really like the brush tip, and the free ink system. You do have to shake them before using, but that's a small thing. Most are quite opaque, with only a few of the lighters colors needing 2 coats. They go on smoothly, and I can use colored pencils easily on top.  Here's the con.... they come with a swatch sheet, which I always fill out whether it's markers, pencils, paint, etc., but this one was a real trial of my patience. The numbers were not in order. For instance on row one, the numbers are730.700,648,727,647, and they aren't on the swatch sheet by color either. So  you pull out a pen then hunt through 240 tiny boxes to try to find where it goes. It took me a few mind numbing hours to get them all swatched, then I organized them the way I wanted. Besides that, I enjoy using them. The box is sturdy, but the separating 'cubes' even though quite thick, can break easily from the weight of the pens when you store them on their side like you're supposed to. The colors are rich and well, colorful. lol  At about $.45 per pen, they're a really good buy. I'm not a professional artist, so they might find them lacking for one reason or another, but for my needs, they're great.

Sentence: Streaking or bleeding can be caused by the ink or paint settling on one side or the other.
Content:
Definitely get these if you want an high-quality beginner’s set of acrylic markers…you just can’t beat this price for the quality and variety of markers you receive!!

**IT IS VERY IMPORTANT that you STORE THESE MARKERS ON THEIR SIDES AND FLIP THE CASE OVER EVERY WEEK OR SO** this tip is for ANY art markers. Streaking or bleeding can be caused by the ink or paint settling on one side or the other. Particularly if these have been stored vertically in the warehouse. For dual end markers, always store the case so that the markers lay on their side, and the flip the case on its other side anytime you think about it.

Do some test swatches and practice drawings before starting on your final project. This way you understand how these particular markers perform. If you’d re having a problem with streaking, lay the case on its side overnight, and also flip the case to the other side for the next morning, then try again. Usually solves the problem with new markers!

Yes, the individual markers *don’t* come labeled with numbers or color names, BUT they come with a chart to assist and have colored caps at both ends. When you think of how many countries (with different languages) they have to ship these to, I think this plan makes sense.

Don’t mix up the caps! But it’s also a good reminder to instantly replace the caps after you use a specific marker….you DON’T want to leave the caps off of acrylic markers longer than you have to in order to color with them.

Also consider the cost savings of not labeling each individual marker….savings that got passed on to us!

I’m impressed with the case quality. I received a different case of markers from another brand, and that case was very flimsy—not this case!!

This is a great deal for good quality markers. 5/5

Sentence: There isn't a bad smell to the markers that you sometimes get with these types of paint pens so you can go extended sessions of coloring.
Content: These markers are great. With the adult coloring books we have using them to highlight the edges and borders it works great. my only complaint with them is that there is no number or indication on them that tell you what color they are. You get a color sheet that tells you the color and the look of the marker color but if you don't put them back in the same spot you might end up grabbing a different color than you want so you'll have to label them yourself which is a pain. There isn't a bad smell to the markers that you sometimes get with these types of paint pens so you can go extended sessions of coloring. The size of them is what you would expect about the size of the smaller sharpie pen. I haven't colored long enough with them to see if they last longer with out them drying out like you do get from time to time. The marker tips are small and allow color to fill the tip adequately for your coloring. I love the little case that you get with them to keep them all in order and it zips up, with a carrying handle. It feels like a cd case back in the 90s but feels great and it would be easy if your like me hosting or going to color parties

Sentence: First of all, just the NUMBER of markers you are getting with this are worth the price, but the quality makes it even more reasonable.
Content: First of all, just the NUMBER of markers you are getting with this are worth the price, but the quality makes it even more reasonable. Each one is dual tipped, one with a more flared "painting" style tip, and the other with a finer tipped style. The shades are plentiful and vibrant, and it is very easy to color with them. Each one has a very smooth flow and operate very easily. The paint dries quite quickly (faster than I expected), and does not bleed through which was a nice surprise. I DID use a cardboard separator to be safe, though. No complaints at all, and the case is fantastic. I also love the addition of the color/shade chart and the flow assisters.  Remember, these are acrylics and not alcohol markers, but if you're looking for acrylic, I think you will love these. (Also great for rock painting!)

Sentence: They are easy to use and the paint flows pretty well although the consistency seems to vary a little bit between different pens.
Content:
These are average quality markers - perfectly ok and usable for personal use. There are lots of colors and a nice range of them. Although it comes with a completed swatch sheet, it doesn't coordinate well with the actual pens because some of the colors don't really match the paint colors and there are no numbers or names on the pens that match the swatch. They are easy to use and the paint flows pretty well although the consistency seems to vary a little bit between different pens. You need to work carefully to avoid streaks.

Given the number of pens and the fact that they come in a case
and are perfectly usable for non-professional work, i think the price is fair.

Sentence: Seriously easy to use, and the colors are super vibrant.
Content:
Wow, these acrylic paint pens are fantastic! Seriously easy to use, and the colors are super vibrant. The paint goes on so smoothly with great coverage, no annoying flooding, just smooth sailing.

The dual tips are brilliant! Need fine details? The fine tip is perfect. Need broader coverage? Flip to the brush tip. It makes working on projects so much easier. There's a great selection of colors, including 8 metallics which look awesome (honestly, I wouldn't mind even more metallics, hint hint!).

Big shoutout for including replacement tips for both ends, that's a really thoughtful touch and a major bonus. They say these work on all sorts of surfaces, and they seem pretty versatile, but definitely do a little test spot on your project first to be safe.

I definitely recommend these pens. They're high quality, fun to use, and a great value. Go get 'em!

Sentence: When swatching them, I noticed that some are nice and “juicy” where the paint flows nicely, but others are dryer, and you’ll need to go slower to get better coverage.
Content:
For what I like, I would have probably given 3 stars, but I want to review these paint markers for what they are. Personally the paint inside isn’t up to my standards, but considering the price and the amount of markers, in addition to a case, they’re what I expected.

First, they come in a zippered case which I prefer over a cardboard box, which I wish more companies would do. Each marker has its own slot and the inserts are removable. It also comes with a printed swatch chart and extra nibs. Some of the swatches are pretty close, some are not, so you’ll want to make your own. The chart has names and numbers, but there’s no markings on the paint pens themselves - kinda pointless and you have to just go by the cap color. As long as you have a chart and keep them in order I guess it’s not that bad, but what if you take multiple out or use different storage? When swatching them, I noticed that some are nice and “juicy” where the paint flows nicely, but others are dryer, and you’ll need to go slower to get better coverage. The paint is on the thinner side, so they can get a little streaky, and the opacity just isn’t there. The dark colors are obviously better, but mid tones (like red) didn’t cover black ink, even with three coats, and some of the dark colors (like dark green) failed here, too. Personally, I prefer opaque paint, but this might not be a negative for some. Of the colors, I do think there’s a nice selection of warm, cool, a couple of skin tone, and neutral colors, and even a handful of metallic. For a beginner set, I think there’s colors are good to get started for sure.

I plan to play around with them a little more, but I think this set will get passed along to the kids for their projects and play. For the current price, they’re worth checking out, and would make a good gift for kids. If you are familiar with some of the more expensive brands of paint markers though, I would probably skip these. It just depends on what you want them for.

Sentence: But they did hold in place until putting them out, so not too difficult to keep organized either.They are not "cheap" in terms of total cost.
Content: I do a lot of painting - across lots of media.  I paint wood, canvas, fabric, stone, shoes, clothing, hats, metal plates. . .To be fair, I have not tried these on all of those yet - and I would probably wait for a few until I get a really good fixative. . . But I have tried quite a few of the colours and. . .they are surprisingly bright and vibrant - even on the wood.  They bonded well so far with: wood, the plastic, canvas, and fabric.  The tips are small enough to get a decent amount of detail - assuming you have a decent to better than average steadiness in your hands.  There are an insane amount of colours - some more subtle and some incredibly different - I'm still playing around to figure out which to use for what, but I did appreciate the fact they included a few little boards that you can effectively use as test swatches for the colours (though. . .you could just use scrap cardboard or whatever you have on hand. . .but still nice).The case holding it is nice.  Simple unzip, and the markers essentially just cascade and unfold - and as I noted. . .there are a lot.  But they did hold in place until putting them out, so not too difficult to keep organized either.They are not "cheap" in terms of total cost. . .but when you consider you are getting over 200. . .the price actually seems pretty fair, too.  Once I get a protective fixative to test on it, I could say more, but right now. . .these are pretty great.

Sentence: There is a LOT of colors to choose from for whatever you'll be using them on.

Our daughters and myself have had a lot of fun with them already and we've only had them a day so far.
